title: Reject noncanonical piles and malformed generic atoms at the codec door
description: Two exact ingress-door gaps violate the canonical wire contract and failure taxonomy. First, _atoms_ok checks ref/offer arity but not field types: a canonical ref value [] passes decode, then ctx.has_fact raises TypeError and leaves poison retrying forever; unhashable/non-string offer fields similarly escape later. Second, ordinary decode_pile accepts semantically equivalent whitespace/key-order JSON and duplicate-key/non-finite aliases because it never compares the exact bytes to canonical re-encoding. These are immutable input defects, not program failures.
design: Make core.fact own one strict generic atom grammar before family dispatch: bounded nonempty string role/name fields, valid-fid ref targets, string offer address/value fields under central byte limits, plus the existing strict suppression/action marker validators. Make the bounded JSON decoder reject duplicate object keys and non-finite constants, then require ordinary pile bytes to equal the exact canonical encoding of the decoded workspace+facts envelope. Classify every grammar/canonicality failure as InvalidPile/PermanentIngressRejection. Keep unexpected family RuntimeError/AssertionError outside that class so it remains retryable.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Canonical piles still round-trip byte-for-byte. Whitespace, key-order, duplicate-key, NaN/Infinity, mixed/foreign workspace, malformed ref/offer field type, empty/over-limit role/name/value, invalid ref fid, malformed suppression/action, and one-over bytes reject at decode before kernel/archive reads. 2. Real RepositoryApplier tests show each malformed canonical pile writes typed permanent evidence, retires only its exact source under F10, leaves root unchanged, and a later healthy generation applies. 3. Internal family RuntimeError/AssertionError still preserves source and writes no rejection evidence. 4. Generic grammar limits are central, documented beside codec code, and exercised at exact max/one-over boundaries. 5. Codec, kernel, RepositoryApplier, staged/direct upload, provider wrapper, and F10 tests pass.

title: Allow exact AWS staged-state missing-key probes
description: Reproducer: a fresh RepositoryApplier.apply_staged checks absent canonical staged/rejected, staged/done, staged/admitted, staged/object-* receipts, page receipts, and object cursors before conditionally creating them. Production canonical S3Store enables 403 missing-key probes, but the SAM ListBucket probe omits CanonicalPrefix/staged/*. GetObject therefore returns 403 and the exact probe is itself denied, wedging every first direct-upload application before publication.
design: Add CanonicalPrefix/staged/* only to the existing canonical missing-key ListBucket statement, retaining expected-owner and s3:max-keys <= 1. This is exact absence disambiguation, not whole staged discovery. Derive a fake IAM matcher from the checked-in probe prefixes and run a cold apply_staged through real S3Store/RepositoryApplier so a missing template prefix fails the behavioral test.
acceptance_criteria: A cold valid direct upload against deny-missing-GET fake S3 traverses all fresh staged receipt/cursor checks, commits through RepositoryApplier, and observes only exact MaxKeys=1 probes allowed by prefixes parsed from the SAM role. Structural tests require staged/* in the constrained canonical probe and continue to forbid pile/*, failed/*, arbitrary canonical listing, ingress, or mutation widening. Focused AWS Applier/S3 tests pass.
close_reason: AWS staged operational state exact-probe scope is present and a policy-derived cold apply_staged succeeds without broad LIST.

title: Never retire ingress after a swallowed family program failure
description: Reproducer: build a real valid message pile, monkeypatch facts.content.message.message (called by validate) to raise RuntimeError, stage it through RepositoryApplier.apply, and observe the broad except Exception in the family validator turn the program failure into False. KernelRejected is then persisted as permanent evidence and F10 deletes the exact source. Settlement reconstruction also calls resolve_edges/accepts with strict=False, so the same internal failure can silently relabel an admitted candidate dormant.
design: Make every registered durable and ephemeral family validator total for malformed untrusted values by catching only the expected input/shape exceptions it can actually raise (such as KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, and named codec errors). RuntimeError, AssertionError, and other unexpected program failures must escape into kernel Judgment.failure. RepositoryApplier treats those as retryable: preserve the exact staged source, write no permanent rejection evidence, grant no F10 receipt, and leave root unchanged. Admitted-candidate settlement/reconstruction must invoke resolve_edges and accepts with strict=True so program failures cannot silently become dormancy. Add an exhaustive registry/static ratchet to prevent broad family validator catches from returning.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A real internal helper RuntimeError during RepositoryApplier.apply propagates/reports retryable failure, preserves the exact source bytes, writes no failed/pile or failed/meta evidence, leaves root unchanged, and grants no retirement receipt. 2. The same failure during compile_snapshot/settlement propagates instead of relabeling an admitted candidate dormant or advancing root. 3. RuntimeError and AssertionError escape every registered family validate path; malformed bodies/atoms/refs still return False without escaping for every durable and ephemeral family. 4. Kernel drain records unexpected family errors in Judgment.failure while ordinary semantic invalidity remains failure=None. 5. Static/registry coverage rejects broad except Exception/BaseException in family validators. 6. Focused family, kernel, RepositoryApplier, candidate archive, settlement, ingress/F10, and full nearby tests pass.

title: Require an exact member provider for every removal target
description: Reproducer: construct and admin-sign an evict fact whose removed offer names a public key that has never had a member provider, then stage it through RepositoryApplier. The family currently needs only author+admin, so the action is admitted and preemptively activates member:<never_key>. The CLI roster lookup is not an admission rule and crafted/direct uploads bypass it.
design: Make the removal family derive Need('target_member','member',target_pk) from the exact canonical removed offer and validate that offer/body binding in the simple handler. The selected edge is historical admission evidence: later target removal does not invalidate the action. Current commands still resolve the target's live member provider through the pinned Reader. Do not add a Node, CLI, Applier, or tag-specific core check.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A real RepositoryApplier pile carrying an otherwise valid admin-signed removal of a never-member is rejected without root mutation; F10/rejection behavior follows the ordinary invalid-fact contract. 2. removal.needs exposes author, admin, and target_member with target_member derived from the sole exact removed offer. 3. The command supplies all three named dependencies and rejects absent/already-removed targets through pinned current authority. 4. Removing an existing member remains terminal across a later provider/rejoin for the same key. 5. Historical admitted removal survives later grantor/target liveness changes. 6. Focused removal, suppression, candidate archive, RepositoryApplier, and fact-policy tests pass.

title: Reject directly deletable families without a SELF suppression selector
description: Reproducer: register a synthetic FamilyPolicy with direct_targets=DELETE_SELF and owner_edge='member' but suppression=NEVER (or only a parent selector). The registry accepts it. A validated delete can therefore offer the target's fact:<fid> suppression ID while the victim FactRecord never declares or consults that ID, so the action is admitted but has no effect. This contradicts both explicit selector semantics and the rule that a fact with no offered suppression selector is unsuppressible.
design: Make the family-policy registry enforce the bidirectional contract at load time: every direct SELF target requires exactly one canonical Self() selector in that family's suppression declaration. Additional declared parent/ancestor selectors remain legal. Keep the check generic over DirectTarget.selector and SelectorRule; do not add a content-family or Node branch.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Synthetic families with DELETE_SELF plus NEVER, parent-only, malformed SELF, or duplicate SELF selectors are rejected during compile_families. 2. A directly deletable family with exactly one Self() plus optional parent/ancestor selectors remains valid. 3. Existing registered deletion families pass the registry ratchet. 4. A valid delete action can never target an undeclared suppression slot, and a family with no suppression selector remains unsuppressible. 5. Focused family-policy and deletion tests pass.

title: Reject non-stream Cloudflare request and canonical response bodies
description: Reproducer: both Worker _bounded_body helpers fall back to await request.bytes() when request.body is absent or lacks getReader, and R2CanonicalReader._bounded_response falls back to await response.arrayBuffer(). Those whole-materializing FFI calls allocate the provider body before enforcing the advertised byte ceiling.
design: At the Cloudflare runtime boundary, accept a missing request body only when Content-Length proves zero; for a nonempty or non-stream body surface, fail closed instead of invoking whole-body bytes(). Require a ReadableStream for canonical Fetch bodies and reject missing/non-stream surfaces rather than arrayBuffer(). Preserve incremental chunk and total limits, cancellation, length equality, and normal empty-body routes.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime and reader tests use request/response fakes whose bytes()/arrayBuffer() raise if called. Empty requests remain accepted without whole-body allocation; nonempty missing streams and malformed stream surfaces are rejected. Oversized streamed bodies cancel at the existing bound and valid streamed bodies still pass. A structural ratchet forbids bytes()/arrayBuffer() fallbacks in these three bounded helpers. Focused Cloudflare worker/upload/reader tests pass.
close_reason: Cloudflare runtimes require streaming body surfaces and no longer call whole-body bytes/arrayBuffer fallbacks; tests and ratchet pass.

title: Bound CLI control success and error responses
description: Reproducer: core.cli sends requests to the user-selected --node endpoint and calls response.read() for successful JSON and HTTPError.read() for error JSON with no bound. A hostile endpoint can allocate an arbitrary response body before JSON parsing, on both success and failure paths.
design: Apply MAX_CONTROL_BYTES at the HTTP boundary. Reject declared Content-Length above the budget before reading; otherwise read at most MAX_CONTROL_BYTES+1 and reject an actual one-over stream. Close successful responses through the existing context manager and ensure error bodies are also closed. Keep command binding/JSON semantics unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Realistic fake success and HTTPError responses prove oversized Content-Length is rejected without body read, absent/lying length reads at most budget+1 and rejects one-over, exact-bound responses proceed to JSON validation, and responses close. A structural ratchet rejects raw unbounded HTTP read() calls in core CLI. CLI tests pass.
close_reason: CLI success and HTTP-error bodies use MAX_CONTROL declared/actual bounds and close responses; focused tests pass.

title: Validate provider LIST page cardinality and R2 keys
description: Reproducer: S3Store.list_page accepts Contents longer than the effective requested MaxKeys; R2BindingStore eagerly materializes every page.objects entry without checking count <= requested limit. A hostile or buggy provider binding can violate the mandatory bounded page contract. R2 also coerces arbitrary obj.key proxies with str() and returns logical keys without validate_key, so malformed, oversized, or non-string provider keys cross the ObjectStore boundary.
design: Treat the adapter response as untrusted. Reject a provider page as soon as it exceeds the effective request limit; do not deduplicate before cardinality validation. Require primitive string provider keys, configured-prefix membership, and the shared validate_key grammar after prefix removal. Preserve opaque advancing cursors and reject invalid truncation/cursor fields. Where the R2 FFI only exposes an iterable, consume at most limit+1 entries before failing instead of tuple-materializing an unbounded response.
acceptance_criteria: Adversarial S3 and R2 tests return limit+1 entries, duplicates, out-of-prefix keys, non-string/proxy keys, invalid logical keys, and repeated/malformed cursors; every case fails closed with StoreError after at most limit+1 iteration. Valid short/exact pages and opaque cursors still work. A response-count ratchet proves both production adapters enforce the caller's effective bound before deduplication/materialization. Focused adapter and provider-conformance suites pass.
close_reason: S3/R2 reject limit+1 LIST pages before deduplication; R2 boundedly iterates and validates primitive in-prefix provider keys/cursors.

title: Bound invite redemption HTTP bodies
description: Reproducer: facts.auth.user.accept downloads an invite URL selected by the invite link and calls urlopen(...).read() with no size argument. A malicious or misconfigured host can stream an arbitrarily large body into memory before decryption/JSON/pile validation applies any protocol ceiling.
design: Give the invite envelope an explicit response budget no larger than MAX_OBJECT_BYTES. Reject an oversized declared Content-Length before reading, then read at most budget+1 bytes and reject actual one-over streaming bodies. Always close the response. Keep cryptographic decryption, workspace binding, and closed-pile validation unchanged; the bound belongs at the network allocation boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Realistic fake HTTP responses cover an oversized Content-Length without reading, a lying/absent length whose stream returns budget+1, exact-bound bytes reaching normal decryption validation, and response closure on success/failure. A structural ratchet forbids raw unbounded read() in invite redemption. Auth/user tests pass.
close_reason: Invite redemption uses declared and actual MAX_OBJECT bounds, closes responses, and has one-over/exact tests.

title: Allow exact AWS ingress object missing-key probes
description: Reproducer: the AWS Applier configures its isolated ingress S3Store with probe_access_denied_missing=True and reads detached ingress objects by exact key. The SAM role grants ingress GetObject and pile-marker ListBucket but not an exact objects/* ListBucket probe. A legitimately missing detached object therefore produces GET 403 followed by denied LIST; apply_staged retains the pile, but can never classify the byte as currently unavailable and retries a permanent IAM mismatch noisily.
design: Add a separate least-privilege ingress missing-key ListBucket scope: only ingress/v1/workspaces/WorkspaceId/objects/*, expected bucket owner, and s3:max-keys <= 1. It is not discovery authority and must not widen marker listing, reads, writes, or deletes. Test the actual S3Store 403-to-exact-probe path while RepositoryApplier processes a staged pile with one missing detached object.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic fake-S3 staged-attachment test makes the declared detached object GET return 403 and proves the Applier records that exact oid as unavailable without treating IAM as broken or publishing bytes it lacks. The observed probe is exact and MaxKeys=1. Structural policy tests require only the workspace-scoped ingress objects/* probe with owner/max-keys constraints and forbid arbitrary ingress/canonical prefixes or mutation. Focused AWS Applier/S3 tests pass.
close_reason: AWS ingress detached-object 403 absence is resolved by an exact workspace-object MaxKeys=1 probe and staged unavailable test.

title: Grant AWS Applier operational cursor authority
description: Reproducer: every RepositoryApplier.turn() and drain_staged() first loads applier/cursor/internal or applier/cursor/staged from the canonical store and persists the next opaque cursor. The production S3Store converts a missing-key 403 through an exact ListBucket probe. The SAM role grants neither GetObject, PutObject, nor the exact missing-key probe for CanonicalPrefix/applier/*, so a fresh scheduled Lambda fails before it can discover work.
design: Grant the Applier compartment GetObject and PutObject only under CanonicalPrefix/applier/*, plus the existing exact-key MaxKeys=1 ListBucket missing-key probe on that prefix. Preserve the invariant that applier cursors are bounded fairness hints, not publication authority; grant no delete, root widening, or ingress authority. Exercise both internal and staged cold-start cursor paths through the actual S3Store/RepositoryApplier boundary with absent GET returning 403.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic fake-S3 cold turn and staged drain load absent cursor keys through exact one-key probes, complete bounded discovery, and persist canonical cursor bytes. Structural SAM tests require applier/* only in canonical probe/read/write statements with expected-owner and max-keys constraints, require both cursor kinds at runtime, and reject applier delete or ingress widening. Focused AWS Applier tests pass.
close_reason: AWS internal/staged discovery cursors now have exact canonical Get/Put/List-probe authority with cold-start tests.

title: Make root specifications state only enforced repository contracts
description: Final alignment review found root DESIGN claims that diverge from running/locked semantics: AuthorityTree was described as co-offer-keyed/fallback rather than base-winner-then-conjunctive-check; pile fact-count was stated bounded while aggregate count/memory remains open; staged intent overclaimed proof that uploader equals fact authors despite legitimate relay; all-retained suppression-slot reservation was stated but not implemented; and staged-object beads retained obsolete second-envelope/new-session-only clauses.
design: Correct root docs to distinguish running invariants from explicitly named open work. Keep one source of truth: base AuthorityTree selection with no co-offer fallback, byte-bounded piles with aggregate count under .17.2.7, broker-authenticated uploader attenuation plus independent Applier workspace/session/digest validation, fact-only retained markers, and all-retained SuppTree slots. Normalize conflicting active beads rather than preserving alternative designs.
acceptance_criteria: README/DESIGN contain no false current bound, co-offer fallback, uploader-author equality, second staging envelope, or new-session-only attachment claim; duplicated text is removed. Active beads .17.3.2, .17.2.6, ssk, .17.2.7, and the all-retained suppression regression have mutually consistent criteria. Documentation/layout tests, semantic keyword audit, bd lint, and dependency-cycle checks pass.

title: Reject unstaged raw RepositoryApplier commits
description: RepositoryApplier.apply(source, raw=bytes, retire=False) can currently compile and CAS a root when source was never created in the canonical internal pile namespace. Reproducer: cold store, valid genesis pile bytes, arbitrary valid-looking internal source key absent from the store; apply commits status=applied and root exists while source remains absent. This bypasses durable exact-work, restart, and F10 actor boundaries.
design: Remove the raw override from the semantic apply API. Every apply first bounded-reads the exact internal source and either processes those bytes or returns no work. Staged ingress must establish/recover the exact claimed internal generation, then call the same source-only apply method. Tests may not use a privileged raw shortcut.
acceptance_criteria: An absent, wrong-key, replaced, or source/raw-retargeted internal generation cannot compile objects or CAS root. A present exact generation applies normally; direct-upload staging first creates/recovers that generation and then uses the identical source-only path. Crash/restart, stale/unknown CAS, duplicate claim, rejection, and F10 retirement tests pass across FS and strict async stores. Structural tests reject a raw parameter on RepositoryApplier.apply and provider adapters contain no alternate raw apply call.

title: Reserve SuppTree slots for every retained candidate
description: Repository_snapshot.derived_rows currently creates selector and principal SuppTree rows only for projection.standing. A kernel-admitted dormant candidate remains root-reachable in FactTree but its explicit suppression IDs can be absent rather than authenticated CLEAR/ACTIVE, so a cold Reader cannot distinguish omitted state and later restoration changes the key universe. Reproducer: retain a valid candidate made dormant by authority competition/rewiring, then point-read each selector and principal ID from its FactRecord.
design: Build suppression and direct-action slot reservations mechanically from every checked retained candidate record and fact. Resolve the value from the canonical effective-action projection, so each reserved ID is CLEAR or ACTIVE(action_fid). Continue deriving AuthorityTree providers and FactOrder only from eligible standing candidates. Reconstruction must independently require this all-retained key set.
acceptance_criteria: Opposite-arrival and cold-restart tests retain a dormant candidate and prove every declared selector/principal ID has an authenticated CLEAR or ACTIVE SuppTree row; a required omitted or forged row makes reconstruction fail closed. Clearing/changing the condition restores the candidate without creating an unreserved suppression key. AuthorityTree and FactOrder still exclude dormant providers/facts, full-P2P and strict DB-free Applier roots are byte-identical, and structural tests prevent standing-only SuppTree construction.

title: Detect strict async RepositoryApplier stores by bounded contract
description: RepositoryApplier.async_store previously detected an async implementation by looking for a type-level get method. A conforming async S3/R2-style store may intentionally expose only mandatory get_bounded plus native list_page, so it was miswrapped as synchronous and could not apply a pile. Reproducer: pass a strict async store with get_bounded/read_versioned/put_if_absent/cas/list_page/delete and no get/list into a cold RepositoryApplier.
design: Classify the execution mode using the mandatory get_bounded method, then require every repository operation through the existing async contract. Do not restore whole-get/list compatibility surfaces or provider-specific detection.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic strict async store with no get or list stages, applies, CASes a genesis root, exposes the result through RepositoryReader, and retires its exact internal generation. A structural regression fixes detection to get_bounded; synchronous FS and existing async adapters still pass. Close only after focused tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed on design/push-pile-worker: async_store now detects the mandatory get_bounded contract, and the strict async no-get/no-list end-to-end test stages, applies, publishes a Reader-visible genesis root, and retires exact work (1 passed).

title: Remove remaining unbounded peer, file-proof, and Node discovery reads
description: Reproducers: RemoteStore exposes only whole get and cannot refine the mandatory get_bounded contract; sync therefore accepts peer bodies without a call-site budget. facts/content/file reads Bao proof objects through whole get even though bao.MAX_PROOF_BYTES is the protocol ceiling. Node.ingress_failures drains the entire failed/pile namespace with list(), bypassing mandatory bounded list_page and short-page behavior.
design: Make boundedness explicit end-to-end: RemoteStore.get_bounded forwards the caller limit into Peer root/object response reading; sync supplies the exact root/object ceilings; file-family reconstruction calls get_bounded(..., bao.MAX_PROOF_BYTES) for both proof reads; Node ingress failure reporting consumes native list_page under PAGE_BATCH with no compatibility whole-list path. Preserve repository semantics and keep pagination a bounded snapshot/hint rather than authority.
acceptance_criteria: Hostile peer tests prove root/object response readers receive exact explicit limits and one-over bodies fail before unbounded allocation. File tests use a store whose get raises and get_bounded records bao.MAX_PROOF_BYTES for both proof reads. A Node test supplies multiple short pages and proves ingress_failures processes the bounded native page contract without calling list; a structural ratchet rejects production whole-get/whole-list regressions at these call sites. Existing sync, attachment/file, ingress-hardening, and layout suites pass before closure.
close_reason: Remote peer, file proof, sync, and Node failure discovery reads now carry explicit bounds; hostile and structural tests pass.

title: Allow exact AWS Applier missing-key probes
description: Reproducer: the production AWS RepositoryApplier constructs S3Store with probe_access_denied_missing=True. For an absent canonical root or immutable page, S3 may answer GetObject with 403 until ListBucket proves that exact key is absent. The SAM role currently grants canonical ListBucket only for pile/* discovery, so a cold repository cannot bootstrap genesis and a missing obj/<oid> is misclassified as AccessDenied.
design: Add a separate least-privilege canonical missing-key probe statement. Permit ListBucket only on the canonical bucket for Prefix equal to <CanonicalPrefix>/root or matching <CanonicalPrefix>/obj/* and the Applier's required operational namespaces <CanonicalPrefix>/applier/* and <CanonicalPrefix>/staged/*; require s3:max-keys <= 1 and the expected resource account. Keep work discovery, object reads, conditional writes, and retirement authority separate. Exercise actual S3Store 403-to-exact-probe paths rather than policy strings alone.
acceptance_criteria: Realistic fake-S3 tests make absent root GET return 403 and bootstrap genesis; a missing referenced immutable page is distinguished by one exact obj/<oid> probe; cold discovery cursors and staged-state reads use only their exact operational prefixes. Structural policy tests require canonical root, obj/*, applier/*, and staged/* probe prefixes with s3:max-keys: 1 and expected-owner confinement, and reject arbitrary canonical, pile, failed, ingress, delete, or write widening. Focused AWS Applier/S3 tests pass before closure.
close_reason: AWS canonical root/object/applier/staged missing-key probes are least-privilege and covered by 403 runtime plus structural tests.

title: Index suppression targets and live authority selectors for bounded settlement
description: The database-free RepositoryApplier needs bounded authenticated routes to facts affected by explicit suppression actions and to authority providers whose family policy declares continuing authority_liveness_guards. The invalidated predecessor incorrectly proposed generic authorization-guard postings and retroactive guard-removal settlement, which would make one-time historical admission authority mutable.
design: Publish family-neutral routes only for explicit action target suppression IDs and family-declared continuing authority-liveness selectors. Path-copy those affected authenticated routes from the pinned root. Named Needs, exact resolved edges, and authenticated candidate admission proofs remain one-time admission evidence and produce no reverse liveness/deactivation posting. No SQL scan, family tag branch, action-specific tree, authorization-guard metadata, or second compiler.
acceptance_criteria: A cold database-free RepositoryApplier incrementally settles explicit delete/removal/suppression active/clear/fallback targets and continuing authority-liveness changes without a corpus/action scan. Removed current member/device authority and grantee-owned delegated-admin authority update through declared authority_liveness_guards. Historical admitted facts never lose eligibility solely because a one-time named authority provider is later suppressed or because the removal action key sorts before the fact. Opposite arrival orders yield byte-identical roots. Missing, duplicate, malformed, wrong-target, wrong-liveness, and one-over routes fail before mutation; full compilation remains the byte-identical oracle. Static coverage rejects authorization-guard metadata/routes and any family-specific settlement branch.

title: Do not retroactively screen admitted facts after author removal
description:
Reproducer: create a workspace with Alice and Bob. Alice authors a member-removal action for Bob whose fact key sorts before a later Bob-authored message. A peer that has Bob's still-valid historical membership witness but has not learned the removal admits the message. Reconcile that admitted candidate with the removal in both arrival orders. Current core/settlement.py applies action.key < fact.key against authorization_guards and deactivates the already-admitted message after convergence, making final state depend on whether removal was known at initial admission.

The product decision cancels post-removal screening: transport delay is the boundary. A fact validly admitted by an unaware peer is legitimate workspace history even when a prior-sorting removal arrives later. Removal still governs current mint/authoring authority and family-declared continuing authority liveness.
design: Separate immutable historical admission from current authority liveness. Named Needs, their exact resolved edges, and the authenticated candidate admission proof are the one-time evidence that authority existed when the fact was accepted. Settlement must not compare a later suppression action key with an admitted fact key to reconsider that judgment. Family-declared authority_liveness_guards generate authenticated current-use selectors; local family commands and remote Worker minting resolve those selectors through one pinned RepositoryReader root. Removed users/devices cannot author or mint now, while delegated-admin liveness follows the grantee. Keep this family-neutral and delete the redundant authorization_guards API rather than retaining dead metadata.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Opposite-arrival tests construct the same removal and Bob-authored fact, prove an unaware peer admits it, converge authenticated candidates in removal-first and fact-first order, and assert byte-identical roots with the message eligible. 2. No suppression/action ordering rule deactivates an admitted fact solely because its one-time named authority provider is later suppressed. 3. Current sync/upload mint and local family commands still reject a removed member/device through a pinned Reader. 4. A delegated-admin grant survives later removal of its historical grantor, but removal of the grantee disables that admin authority. 5. FamilyPolicy has no authorization_guards field or reverse route; named Needs and exact admission edges are the sole historical authority witness. 6. Focused candidate archive, suppression, Worker mint, device, admin, RepositoryApplier, and convergence tests pass. 7. DESIGN and README explicitly distinguish historical admission, canonical eligibility, suppression, and current authority liveness.

title: Remove whole-GET fallbacks from hosted read compartments
description: The shared serverless Gateway and upload broker accepted readers lacking get_bounded and fell back to whole-object GET followed by a length check. That can materialize an attacker-sized root/object before rejection and contradicts the mandatory bounded object-store contract. The Cloudflare Reader wrappers also exposed an unnecessary unbounded get surface.
design: Require get_bounded at each broker/gateway dependency boundary, call it directly, and narrow deployed Reader wrappers to that method. Missing bounded capability fails closed; no adapter may infer the guarantee by checking len after an unbounded read.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway, upload broker, Lambda sync wrapper, and Cloudflare Reader wrappers have no whole-get compatibility branch or unbounded get surface. A whole-get-only fake is never called and fails closed; exact and one-over bounded reads retain current statuses. A structural ratchet covers all hosted untrusted read boundaries, provider gates pass, and production LOC does not rise.
close_reason: Fixed during the final alignment audit: hosted Gateway and broker now require get_bounded directly, Reader wrappers expose no unbounded get, whole-only negative controls fail closed without a read, and 157 provider/reader/structural tests pass.

title: Preserve historical admission witnesses when batching sync piles
description:
PileSender coalesced independently verified candidate closures by first-fid deduplication and byte size only. When closures carry competing canonical offer providers, the union can remain kernel-valid while rewiring a deletion or authority edge and manufacturing a different admission proof/root; a Need.requires union can instead become jointly invalid and abort otherwise independent delivery.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create two valid device claims for one key, retain a deletion witness through the higher claim, then batch the lower-claim witness before the deletion witness and compare the destination admission proof/root. Also batch the independently valid founder conflict before a child device claim whose co-offer requirement it invalidates.
design: Strictly rejudge each selected historical closure, then coalesce only when the combined kernel judgment remains valid and its complete fid-to-named-ResolvedEdge map exactly equals the union of the isolated maps. Shared-edge conflict, valid-but-rewired union, invalid union, and byte overflow flush the current batch and restart from the full next closure.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic dual-device tests prove the source-selected deletion admission oid and full root survive batched delivery; the former one-batch counterexample becomes two ordinary piles. A realistic Need.requires conflict splits rather than aborting independent delivery. Compatible message closures still coalesce within MAX_PILE_BYTES. Objects are encoded/validated before mutation and sent before every pile; no alternate outbound path or synthesized witness remains.
close_reason: Fixed by 8405047: PileSender rejudges isolated and combined closures, coalesces only exact edge-map-preserving unions, splits valid rewires and invalid Need.requires unions, and preserves selected admission oids/root in deterministic device/deletion tests.

title: Finish the family-neutral command and mint-proof boundary
description: Core must not inventory concrete fact families. Remove the all-family core/cmds compatibility facade, route process commands through the checked facts registry or direct family APIs, and let peer/upload proof authorship resolve through a validated family-owned purpose hook. Keep family-neutral status/control outside the fact inventory.
design: Fact modules remain the owners of constructors, commands, queries, and ephemeral proof builders. The top-level facts registry validates unique CLI paths and proof purposes. Core transport asks that registry for an opaque proof closure; it never imports facts.auth or facts.content modules. Put node status assembly in a small family-neutral control helper rather than enlarging Node.
acceptance_criteria: core/cmds.py is absent. Tests and benchmarks call exact family functions or facts.COMMANDS, not a relocated compatibility facade. core/walk.py and upload mechanics obtain sync/upload proofs through one validated top-level facts hook; duplicate, malformed, and unknown purposes fail closed. A repository-wide AST ratchet forbids core imports of facts.auth.* or facts.content.*. Real CLI/daemon sync, upload authorization, and byte-level proof behavior remain equivalent, and total production Python LOC does not rise without an explicit measured reason.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in 5305765: removed core/cmds.py, added family-neutral core/status.py, routed command ownership to fact families, and retained proof dispatch through the facts registry; 151 focused tests passed across structural, CLI, family, daemon, authority, query, attachment, and host behavior.

title: Normalize active bead graph to locked Sender/Applier/Reader model
description: Audit the active poc-16 bead graph, close or supersede non-aligned work, rewrite every surviving affected bead to exactly the PileSender/RepositoryApplier/RepositoryReader capabilities and the hosted=A+R and full-P2P=S+A+R actor compositions, and correct dependency edges without changing implementation artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Done when every active affected bead has executable criteria consistent with exactly PileSender, RepositoryApplier, and RepositoryReader and exactly hosted=A+R and full-P2P=S+A+R. Criteria require direct retained ingress; a database-free sole pile-to-root/root-CAS/F10 Applier; a pinned database-free read-only Reader; PileSender-only SQL authorship over canonical facts plus one disposable combined generic index; family-owned deletion/suppression/authority semantics; thin provider/deploy adapters; and stale/unknown-CAS safety. Superseded work is closed with obligations folded into named survivors, searches find no live retired receiver/compiler or third-actor requirement, dependency cycles/orphans are absent, readiness is coherent, lint/export/diff checks pass, and only .beads changes are committed.
close_reason: Normalized every affected active bead to the exact PileSender/RepositoryApplier/RepositoryReader capabilities and hosted=A+R/full-P2P=S+A+R actor compositions; folded and superseded only kgp.10.1.1 and mjq; applied the audited dependency corrections; and verified lint, cycles, graph integrity, orphans, readiness, export, and semantic scans.

title: Bind ApplyProposal to its exact workspace and pile
description: RepositoryApplier.propose(raw_A) currently returns an unbound public ApplyProposal. commit(source_B, raw_B, proposal_A) can establish A's outbox/root, mint a receipt keyed to B, and retire B. This crosses the exact-pile F10 authority boundary even though normal apply() composes the calls correctly.
design: Bind every proposal to workspace, exact payload digest, and the minting Applier issuer. commit must reject any mismatch before immutable writes, root CAS, receipt registration, or retirement. Keep propose/commit public only for deterministic concurrency testing; apply remains the production transition.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-pile and cross-Applier proposals are rejected before any store mutation. Same-pile proposals still support two-cold-Applier stale-CAS tests. Proposal fields are canonical typed values, commit checks workspace, h(raw), source binding, and issuer before _establish_outbox. Tests inspect root, obj/, pile generations, and receipt state after each mismatch. Static authority ratchets prevent another unbound commit proposal.
close_reason: Bound proposals to workspace, exact pile digest, and minting Applier before outbox/CAS; added cross-pile and cross-Applier no-mutation tests (52 focused tests pass).

title: Bound detached-object completion after staged fact admission
description:
After a staged pile is admitted, turn every referenced detached object into independent bounded completion work. Fact/root completion must never wait for missing file bytes, and replay of a retained marker must not rescan all references or create new internal piles. Completion state is operational evidence outside the authenticated root and never grants root or ingress-delete authority.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Stage an exact-limit pile and a one-over pile with delayed, missing, corrupt, and surplus detached objects; restart completion between pages and record reference memory plus repeated scans.
design: Create deterministic marker and per-object work identities bound to workspace, exact marker key and digest, session, and object digest. Establish the next durable work page before retiring the current page. Process under explicit item, page, byte, and turn budgets. Missing or retryable reads retain only that object; hash or size poison records terminal evidence; canonical immutable collisions surface loudly. Provider lifecycle cleanup is separate and cannot be F10.
acceptance_criteria: A 65,536-reference staged pile is paged without all-reference memory or repeated full scans. Facts commit first; a late object is promoted on a cold later turn without changing root. Poison terminates with exact evidence, retryable failures remain pending, resolved objects are not reread, and canonical collisions fail loudly. Crash points before and after ticket creation, promotion, receipt, page handoff, and marker completion plus two cold appliers preserve every unresolved object exactly once logically. FS, fake S3, and fake R2 schedules agree, no ingress key is deleted, and completed operational evidence has a documented bounded lifecycle.

title: Put every inbound canonical object write behind RepositoryApplier
description: Peer page PUT, sync blob fetch, staged-object promotion, admission-proof creation, fact residence, and tree-page creation currently have or can grow independent canonical obj write doors. Route every inbound canonical immutable write through RepositoryApplier methods that hash, bound, conditionally create, verify collisions, and participate in the same exact-pile/F10 transition where applicable. PileSender writes only isolated ingress or sends through the recipient protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Done when every inbound canonical obj/* creation for local authoring, peer transfer, sync, direct upload, admission witness, fact residence, detached object, rejection evidence, and authenticated map page occurs only through RepositoryApplier semantic methods and the conditional-create adapter primitives they call. Valid, corrupt, collision, missing, duplicate, timeout, stale-token, and unknown-outcome tests run through FS, fake S3, and fake R2. PileSender writes or sends only isolated ingress/exact piles; RepositoryReader writes nothing. RepositoryApplier verifies content addressing and bounds before mutation, establishes all root-reachable objects before its sole root CAS, and retains exact work until an applied/confirmed/no-op or typed permanent rejection can authorize F10.
notes: The current violations to remove include daemon PUT /page, walk._fetch_blobs/peer object ingestion, and any staging promotion that calls ensure_object directly. Adapter storage primitives may implement conditional creation, but only RepositoryApplier owns the semantic call sites.

title: Make RepositoryReader the side-effect-free pinned read boundary
description: Wrap one pinned composite root and authenticated immutable-object fetch surface as the sole database-free read capability used by hosted recipients, full P2P receiving/query decisions, brokers, gateways, WorkerView, and CandidateView. A read never drains ingress, refreshes SQL, lists provider state, writes an object, or advances root.
acceptance_criteria: Done when RepositoryReader accepts one exact root byte string plus an authenticated immutable-object fetch capability and every answer remains explainable by that root after concurrent commits. It is database-free, read-only, and side-effect-free: no SQL, LIST, ingress drain, scheduling, projection refresh, object write, root CAS, rejection write, or retirement. WorkerView and CandidateView are constructed only through it in production. Root/page/mint/auth/suppression/candidate/family-query tests cover valid, missing, corrupt, foreign, stale, and concurrent roots under aggregate fetch, byte, depth, row, and work budgets. Identical bytes yield identical answers in hosted AWS/Cloudflare and full-P2P; static closure excludes Node/Catalog/sqlite3, RepositoryApplier mutation APIs, PileSender, and provider policy.

title: Extract one pure repository snapshot compiler
description: Replace the SQL-bound indexes builder and the candidate-archive mirror with one family-neutral pure function from workspace plus joined admitted candidates plus selected admission witnesses to canonical candidate records, all four authenticated map rows, immutable outbox, and root bytes. RepositoryApplier and archive verification must call this exact function; SQLite may consume its result only as a disposable projection.
acceptance_criteria: One family-neutral pure compiler maps workspace plus joined root-reachable candidates and selected admission witnesses to one canonical candidate record set, FactOrder/FactTree/SuppTree/AuthorityTree rows, immutable outbox, and root bytes. Every registered family, offer/co-offer canonical winner/rewire, reference, delete/removal action, suppression active/clear/fallback, dormant restoration, duplicate witness, and input ordering has byte-identical full and incremental results. Opposite post-removal arrival preserves historically admitted candidate standing/action effectiveness while current liveness rows disable removed-principal use. RepositoryApplier and archive verification call this exact implementation; the disposable SQLite client projection may consume its output but cannot feed it. Static transitive-closure and symbol tests exclude Node, Catalog/sqlite3, PileSender, daemon, provider modules, object-store mutation, authorization-guard screening, retired alternate receiver/compiler code, and any second row/root derivation.

title: Prove actor composition and uninterrupted direct-upload isomorphism
description: Replace seam-by-seam green tests with one product-boundary corpus that runs the two actual actor compositions. A full P2P node combines PileSender, RepositoryApplier, and RepositoryReader; a hosted recipient combines the same Applier and Reader with SQLite unavailable.
design: Drive a real family command into the resumable PileSender, the production RepositoryReader-plus-signer broker compartment, exact fake-provider PUTs, durable ingress marker, event or scheduled drain, RepositoryApplier root CAS, and a fresh RepositoryReader family query. Capture proposed immutable outboxes and root bytes before provider effects so FS, fake S3, and fake R2 executions can be compared exactly. The broker grants narrow upload capability only; it is neither an admission membrane nor another repository actor.
acceptance_criteria: One corpus runs unchanged through exactly hosted=RepositoryApplier+RepositoryReader with sqlite3 made fatal and full-P2P=PileSender+the same RepositoryApplier+the same RepositoryReader. It covers message plus multi-chunk file, missing detached data, family-owned delete/removal/suppression/current-authority transitions, opposite post-removal arrival, duplicate/replay, wrong workspace/member, poisoned bytes, two cold concurrent appliers, stale and ambiguous CAS, dropped notification, restart, and crashes before immutable creation, root CAS, and F10 retirement. An unaware peer's admitted fact and action remain effective after removal convergence in both compositions, while a new upload/mint by the removed principal is rejected from the pinned root. Same base root plus exact pile yields byte-identical immutable outbox/root and identical pinned Reader answers; no fact or file becomes visible before CAS. A real direct upload must travel retained ingress -> Applier-minted internal generation -> root commit -> exact F10, and broker-only or manually bridged tests cannot satisfy end-to-end acceptance.

title: Purge every competing pile-to-root artifact
description: After RepositoryApplier and RepositoryReader drive both actor types, delete the SQL-specific Publisher/AdmissionMembrane compiler, mixed WorkspaceRuntime receiver, Node rebuild republish, daemon read-triggered turns, provider publisher stubs, direct canonical page PUTs, manual staging-to-host test bridges, and documentation/deploy shapes implying a second semantic receiver. Preserve only PileSender, RepositoryApplier, RepositoryReader, pure compiler, and thin adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Done when the explicitly retired historical Publisher, AdmissionMembrane, WorkspaceRuntime, publisher_stub, core.mint compatibility facade, SQL receiver, Node republish, read-triggered turn, direct canonical page PUT, embedded-pile blob path, provider settlement/compiler, manual staging bridge, and unused compatibility mutation surfaces have no live production import, call site, deploy shape, or test authority. Ordinary piles contain exactly workspace plus facts; detached objects enter only through RepositoryApplier. The surviving surface is PileSender, database-free RepositoryApplier, pinned database-free RepositoryReader, one pure compiler, and thin adapters. Static inventory proves one root derivation/CAS owner, one F10 path, no side-effecting Reader or SQL receive, no canonical inbound object writer outside Applier, and active docs/beads name only hosted=A+R and full-P2P=S+A+R.

title: Route every full P2P receive path through RepositoryApplier
description: Compose the full P2P actor as PileSender plus the exact shared RepositoryApplier plus RepositoryReader. Route local authoring delivery, peer pile/object receipt, synchronization, restart recovery, and direct-upload work through RepositoryApplier; route root/page/mint/auth/query answers through a pinned RepositoryReader. SQL is allowed only inside PileSender closing and disposable local presentation after a committed root.
design: Normalize every accepted input into the canonical exact internal pile grammar and let RepositoryApplier commit it from one pinned root plus root-reachable objects. After confirmed root outcome, rebuild the optional SQLite facts plus combined generic index projection through RepositoryReader; projection failure cannot change canonical state or authorize F10. Remove compatibility receive/compiler paths instead of wrapping them.
acceptance_criteria: Done when local create/post/file/delete/removal, peer pile/object receipt, sync receive, restart, and direct upload all invoke the exact same database-free RepositoryApplier, while every read/auth/mint/query path constructs subordinate views through a pinned database-free RepositoryReader. A traced receive executes zero SQL and its outbox/root depend only on the pinned root, exact pile, root-reachable objects, kernel, and registered family semantics. PileSender alone may use the disposable SQLite facts plus combined generic type/dependency/offer/state/edge/action index to close outbound intent; projection refresh occurs only after a committed root and projection failure cannot alter root or authorize deletion. Static tests reject any alternate canonical-object writer, pile-to-root derivation, CAS, rejection, or F10 path, and stale/unknown CAS histories retain exact internal work without clobber.

title: Enforce the two actor compositions around one RepositoryApplier
description: Lock exactly two actor compositions around three capabilities. A hosted recipient is RepositoryApplier plus RepositoryReader and is database-free. A full P2P node adds PileSender and optional local SQL but invokes the exact same applier and reader for local, peer, sync, and direct-upload traffic. RepositoryApplier alone validates inbound canonical objects, derives repository state, creates root-reachable immutable objects, advances root by its one CAS, reconciles outcomes, and grants exact retirement. RepositoryReader is pinned and side-effect-free. No other component may perform any part of those authorities.
design: Define one provider-neutral RepositoryApplier over exact pile bytes, a pinned root with opaque CAS token, authenticated immutable fetches, and an immutable outbox. It reruns the running kernel and family policies, joins durable candidate witnesses, derives FactOrder/FactTree/SuppTree/AuthorityTree, ensures every reachable object, performs the only production root CAS, reconciles ambiguous outcomes, and mints exact F10 retirement evidence. PileSender may consult SQL only before the pile crosses this boundary. RepositoryReader consumes the same root and codecs. Provider entrypoints supply scheduling and ObjectStore effects only.
acceptance_criteria: Done when repository-wide static and runtime ratchets permit exactly three capabilities and two actor compositions: hosted=RepositoryApplier+RepositoryReader and full-P2P=PileSender+RepositoryApplier+RepositoryReader. PileSender may consult only the disposable combined facts/generic-index SQLite projection before delivery and has no canonical write, CAS, or retirement authority. RepositoryApplier and its one pure compiler are database-free; every local, peer, sync, S3, and R2 exact pile enters it; it alone establishes canonical objects, derives the root, performs CAS, reconciles outcomes, records typed rejection evidence, and mints F10. RepositoryReader is pinned to one root and performs zero SQL, LIST, writes, turns, or refreshes. Identical base-root and pile bytes yield identical outboxes, roots, and Reader answers with SQL absent, stale, deleted, or poisoned. Retired alternate receiver/compiler symbols may remain only in explicitly historical issue/commit notes, never in live imports, deploy artifacts, or acceptance paths.

title: Corroborate every composite-map descriptor at authenticated root decode
description: Independent review found composite-root map descriptors duplicated authenticated count/depth but point/range readers used depth only as a ceiling, full reconstruction fetched the root twice, and incremental map updates accepted forged outer metadata then silently rebuilt a canonical descriptor. Candidate sync, database-free Worker authorization, repair, and publication therefore did not enforce one canonical root envelope.
design: Make the generic Merkle Reader and path-copy update accept an optional expected root (count, depth). Validate it during the root-page decode each operation already requires, including explicit-known traversal, local diff decode, and equal-root pruning; do not add a second fetch. Pass every composite descriptor through CandidateView, WorkerView, FactOrder traversal/update, and Fact/Supp/Authority incremental publication.
acceptance_criteria: Forged count and forged depth fail closed for Candidate sync point/range reads, all three Worker maps through direct point reads and mint, cold reconstruction of all four maps, known-page enumeration, equal-root diff pruning, primitive update, indexes.build, and snapshot.update_fact_order. Incremental publication does not mutate or heal the forged root; no failed update emits pages. Expanded and full suites pass.
notes: Implemented and gated on codex/admission-proof-retention commit 5da386d. Reader validates expected count/depth on its first authenticated root-page decode across point/range/known/diff paths; update validates during its existing root fetch. Every production descriptor-backed Reader/update passes the expectation. Direct production-wiring tests prove indexes.build and snapshot.update_fact_order reject before emit; full suite 989 passed, 12 skipped.
close_reason: Fixed by 5da386d with count/depth hostile vectors across every read and incremental publication seam.

title: Reject present-but-empty roots during authoritative rebuild
description: Independent admission-archive review found Node.rebuild branched on truthiness of root bytes. A present zero-byte root was treated as absent, bypassing current/legacy decoding and same-snapshot-envelope validation; a populated local catalog could then republish itself over unauthenticated bytes.
design: Distinguish object absence (None/ABSENT) from every present byte string. Every present root, including b'', must pass current decoding, the finite v7 decoder, or exact known-envelope repair before any catalog state can publish. Never let local SQLite bless malformed shared root bytes.
acceptance_criteria: Parameterized realistic rebuild tests cover registered workspaces with empty and populated local catalogs, install a present b'' root, assert rebuild fails closed, and prove the exact root bytes remain unchanged. Full cutover, candidate-archive, and shared-bucket suites pass.
notes: Fixed on codex/admission-proof-retention commit 5da386d: Node.rebuild distinguishes absent None from every present byte string. Empty and populated catalogs both reject a present b'' root and preserve its exact bytes. Full suite 989 passed, 12 skipped.
close_reason: Fixed by 5da386d; present empty roots can no longer enter the absent-root repair path.

title: Enforce an aggregate two-root Merkle diff work budget
description:
Reader.diff_page bounds remote traversal but not aggregate work across both authenticated roots. RepositoryApplier and synchronization need one resumable paired traversal whose local and remote fetches, bytes, and CPU are all charged; otherwise a cold hosted recipient can redo or hide unbounded work.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Construct two valid worst-shape roots and hostile forged descriptors, then run each remote diff/traversal with cold fetch counters through full-P2P, fake S3, and fake R2 until completion or one-over rejection.
design: Make diff classify logical changes through one paired authenticated traversal or a bounded multiproof/frontier so both roots share one explicit aggregate fetch/byte/work ceiling. The continuation must authenticate its aligned routes and preserve current-root-only oid pruning; stale physically held pages remain non-authoritative. Plumb the derived budget through serverless callers rather than hiding local reads outside their fetch counter.
acceptance_criteria: Done when every remote authenticated-map traversal and two-root diff used by RepositoryReader, full-P2P synchronization, witness join, or RepositoryApplier affected-route discovery shares descriptor-aware aggregate unique-fetch, byte, depth, row, and CPU/work budgets across both roots and all four maps. Honest maximum descriptors complete; lying count/depth/range/cycle/missing/cross-class pages and a one-over budget fail closed before root CAS or read authorization. Hostile disjoint, value-only, insertion, deletion, stale-history, and maximum-prefix pairs paginate bidirectionally from authenticated resumable continuations without redoing an unbounded prefix. Fixed full-P2P/fake-S3/fake-R2 schedules assert exact ceilings and progress; no full enumeration, private-reader escape, SQL fallback, or provider-specific traversal exists.

title: Align cold mint fetch ceilings with bounded Merkle-map depth
description:
The bounded Merkle-map path ceiling and deployed recipient fetch/byte envelope currently disagree. A valid adversarial prefix can pass publication but make a cold RepositoryReader or RepositoryApplier fail before reaching the authenticated answer, violating availability for the hosted DB-free actor.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an admitted maximum-prefix repository at production map constants, clear all caches, and invoke mint plus apply under the deployed fetch/byte ceilings; repeat one unit below and with a one-over shape.
design: Derive one end-to-end request budget from the map descriptor depth, operation shape, fact/proof closure ceiling, and provider response limits. Do not merely raise a magic constant: either reduce the normative key/depth/page geometry, make the Worker operation explicitly resumable where semantics permit, or reject shapes before the committed root can require more than the deployed cold-read envelope. Keep provider-specific runtime caps outside the generic map and prove the adapter configuration covers the protocol bound.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a mechanically derived production ceiling covers the worst permitted Merkle geometry for cold pinned RepositoryReader mint/auth reads and database-free RepositoryApplier validation. Hostile-prefix exact-limit fixtures are admitted through RepositoryApplier and then complete within one shared fetch/byte/depth/row/work envelope; one-over shape is rejected before canonical mutation. Full-P2P, Lambda, and Cloudflare use the same protocol constants and code, configuration one-under fails, and measurements separate exact reads, postings, mint, and apply. No SQL cache, warm object assumption, provider-specific bypass, or side-effecting read may satisfy the bound.

title: Make AWS upload-broker stack creation atomic against name takeover
description:
The management command checks that a stack name is absent and then invokes generic sam deploy by name. Another principal can create that name between the check and deployment; SAM may then choose UPDATE and mutate a stack this deployment never owned. The update/remove paths use the observed exact stack ARN, but create lacks an atomic create-only primitive.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pause create after the stack-absence observation, create a foreign same-name stack, resume the original create, and inspect every provider mutation against the foreign ARN.
design: Do not close the race with a second describe. Package/build may remain SAM-driven, but the mutating control-plane call must encode CREATE versus UPDATE atomically at CloudFormation.
acceptance_criteria: Done when broker-stack creation uses a provider create-only operation tied to exact account/region/name and fails if the name becomes occupied; it never updates an observed or foreign stack. A deterministic barrier race installs a foreign stack after absence check and proves zero foreign mutation. Update/remove require exact tags, outputs, ARN, and ownership and preserve both ingress and canonical buckets. Deployment code changes only provider resources and never RepositoryApplier/RepositoryReader semantics.

title: Prove direct-upload retirement against pre-expiry requests still in flight
description: Review found that a signed PUT expiry usually limits request start, not completion. A request accepted just before expiry may finish after expiry+clock-skew, so deadline-only deletion of a client-writable session key does not prove that the same generation cannot reappear after retirement.
design: Keep client-writable staging separate from internal generations. RepositoryApplier copies a verified exact intent once to an internally fresh pile key; F10 retirement never targets a client capability. Before any staging delete, prove provider-enforced completion grace/tombstone safety or retain markers for lifecycle GC without a publication claim.
acceptance_criteria: Running direct-upload history distinguishes staging from canonical generation keys and demonstrates that no client capability can recreate a retired canonical pile. Any staging deletion has provider-backed evidence that pre-expiry in-flight writes cannot land afterward, or staging remains retained and docs state the lifecycle boundary. Include an accepted-before-expiry/completes-after-expiry adversarial schedule.
notes: Superseded during architecture normalization by poc-16-kgp.10. The surviving F10 checker criteria explicitly retain the accepted-before-expiry/completes-after-expiry schedule and require client ingress retention or separately proved provider lifecycle safety; no obligation was discarded.

title: Require exact S3 bucket ownership for the upload broker
description: The prepared AWS upload-broker stack permits ExpectedBucketOwner to be empty. Because canonical and ingress buckets are external inputs, bucket deletion/recreation or an incorrectly named cross-account bucket can silently change which provider principal supplies authorization state or receives bearer PUTs. Require an exact 12-digit owner in keyring creation, deploy validation, template parameters, runtime configuration, and provider binding before any stack mutation.
design: One deployment currently assumes canonical and ingress buckets share one AWS account. Make that assumption explicit and fail closed. A future cross-account deployment needs separate canonical and ingress owner parameters and a deliberate authority design.
acceptance_criteria: CLI and template reject an absent/malformed owner before provider mutation; runtime cannot construct a signer/store without it; keyrings remain bound to that exact owner; tests exercise missing owner and verify no optional unpinned path remains in the generated stack.
close_reason: AWS broker now requires a 12-digit bucket owner in both keyring creation and deployment, pins all S3 IAM statements with s3:ResourceAccount, signs ExpectedBucketOwner, rejects dotted virtual-host ingress buckets and empty prefixes before mutation, and makes signatureAge follow the configured TTL. Focused 69-pass provider gate and full 917-pass repository gate are green.

title: Bind RepositoryApplier receipts to the exact internal generation
description: Close the F10 ABA hole by making the unforgeable RepositoryApplier retirement receipt bind exact internal pile key, exact bytes/digest, fresh generation identity, base/result root evidence, and the apply outcome. A receipt is one-use authority local to the applier turn and cannot authorize deletion of a recreated or client-writable marker.
design: Carry an exact internal-generation witness from RepositoryApplier.stage through the applier-minted ApplyReceipt. RepositoryApplier alone checks current exact bytes, root outcome, workspace, source, digest, and generation before one-use retirement. Do not treat an opaque provider token as unique generation identity. Client-writable staging markers are outside F10 and are never retired by this receipt.
acceptance_criteria: Done when the RepositoryApplier-minted one-use ApplyReceipt binds workspace, exact internal pile key, exact bytes/digest, fresh generation identity, base/result root evidence, and outcome. Applied, exact-confirmed, token-checked no-op, stale, unknown, crash, replay, caller-forgery, source/raw retarget, and identical-key-and-bytes recreation schedules agree across FS, fake S3, fake R2, and the F10 checker. A stale receipt cannot delete a recreated generation; PileSender and RepositoryReader cannot mint or spend receipts; client-writable ingress is outside F10; no SQL row, provider ETag alone, retry count, or retired receipt mechanism grants deletion.
notes: Port caller-forgery, cross-process, source/raw-retarget, retry, bounded-capability, and identical-key-and-bytes recreation schedules to RepositoryApplier ApplyReceipt and remove every retired receipt mechanism.

title: Enforce the kernel closure bound after canonical provider rewires
description: Independent review found that kernel ingress and cold candidate projection bound each fact's transitive proof closure, but SQLite extend_proofs/rebuild_proofs can install a rewired proof whose current closure exceeds MAX_CLOSURE_FACTS. Hot settlement can therefore publish a root that cold reconstruction rejects.
design: Give the derived SQLite proof engine the same unique transitive-closure predicate as the running MemoryContext/kernel. Apply it on incremental extension and full rebuild, and keep the database-free projector identical. A provider-winner rewire may make a previously eligible candidate dormant; it must never create an over-limit proof row.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic canonical-provider rewire at the 256-fact boundary proves hot Catalog standing equals cold settlement.project before and after the winner changes. Incremental and rebuild paths reject closure size 257, accept size 256, and the focused admission/cold-reconstruction suites pass.
notes: Completed at branch tip 5da386d. The running SQLite proof engine and database-free settlement projector enforce the same unique transitive closure bound. test_provider_rewire_obeys_same_256_fact_closure_bound_hot_and_cold exercises the real 256/257 canonical-provider rewire boundary, and the independent full gate passed 989 tests with 12 skips.
close_reason: Running hot/cold proof engines now share the exact closure bound; realistic 256/257 rewire regression and full gates pass at 5da386d.

title: Bound pile count and RepositoryApplier peak memory
description:
A valid pile can contain many independent small candidates even when each closure is bounded. RepositoryApplier must bound aggregate decode, kernel receipts, witness construction, authenticated fetches, outbox bytes, and peak memory before any durable canonical mutation so a database-free hosted recipient cannot be exhausted.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Submit exact-limit and one-over piles independently for fact count, encoded bytes, witness work, object fetches, outbox bytes, and peak memory to a cold hosted RepositoryApplier, followed by a healthy pile.
design: Set one provider-neutral MAX_PILE_FACTS and measured peak-memory/work envelope below the smallest deployment, or implement a canonical bounded stream codec. Enforce at the earliest shared pile door before proof construction, canonical/outbox creation, staging promotion, or root proposal. Keep per-closure and aggregate limits distinct; adapters may narrow transport bytes but not semantics.
acceptance_criteria: N and N+1 tests exercise the real pile codec and RepositoryApplier; a near-limit pile of many independent valid facts is rejected under an explicit measured recipient-safe ceiling before canonical object/root mutation. Store protocols require bounded reads, and FS/S3/R2 plus deterministic fakes implement get_bounded without whole-object compatibility fallback; exact-limit and one-over untrusted reads prove over-limit bodies are not fully materialized. RepositoryApplier.stage rejects non-bytes and MAX_PILE_BYTES+1 before hashing, source generation, or any store mutation across Node, Lambda, and Worker wrappers. Aggregate and per-closure limits remain independent; later healthy work proceeds; the receiving path imports no SQLite.

title: Serve the upload broker through an isolated Cloudflare Worker
description: Deploy the RepositoryReader+signer broker compartment as an isolated Cloudflare Worker around UploadBrokerEndpoint. It uses the exact shared RepositoryReader facade over pinned canonical bytes, an isolated-ingress signer, trusted clock/nonce, and durable key ring; client object/pile bodies go directly to R2 and no second broker read implementation appears.
design: Expose only POST /upload/open, /upload/issue, and /upload/finalize. Preserve provider isolation: no canonical write credential and no RepositoryApplier binding in the broker. Whatever exact provider primitive backs RepositoryReader must be workspace-confined and hidden behind that facet; the only write-capable parent derives exact isolated-ingress PUTs. Bound streams, reject redirect/query/path ambiguity, redact authority, and retain exact ownership markers.
acceptance_criteria: Done when an isolated Cloudflare Worker implements only the shared pinned-RepositoryReader plus signer broker protocol for complete zero/multi-object OPEN/ISSUE/FINALIZE sessions. Workerd-compatible tests cover bounded streams, malformed/oversize inputs, hostile headers/path/method, cold key rotation, stale roots, R2 read/sign faults, and secret-free output. Artifact/config closure proves no mutation-capable canonical R2 binding, root CAS, F10, SQL, or RepositoryApplier semantic fork. Opt-in live smoke uploads attachment and exact pile bytes directly to retained R2 ingress without bodies crossing the Worker; update/remove preserve both ingress and canonical buckets and reject ownership takeover.
notes: The metadata-only Cloudflare broker, streamed membrane, R2 signer, provider-bound keyring, and clean packaging exist. Replace broker-specific canonical fetch logic with the shared RepositoryReader facet, pair it with the real RepositoryApplier compartment under .17.5, and complete live direct-PUT plus routed-front-door smoke. The broker never proxies bodies or gains canonical mutation.

title: Serve the upload broker through an isolated AWS Lambda
description: Deploy the RepositoryReader+signer broker compartment as an isolated AWS Lambda around UploadBrokerEndpoint. It uses the exact shared RepositoryReader facade over pinned S3 bytes, an exact isolated-ingress signer, trusted clock/nonce, and durable key ring; it never receives object/pile bodies or imports a second canonical reader.
design: Expose only POST /upload/open, /upload/issue, and /upload/finalize. IAM permits the backing adapter only the exact reads needed to implement RepositoryReader, plus its key-ring secret and exact ingress PutObject presigning. It has no canonical writes, ingress reads/LIST/DELETE, root CAS, RepositoryApplier mutation capability, or provider-policy authority. Bound hostile Function URL events before allocation, redact proofs/cursors/URLs, and pin exact deployment identity.
acceptance_criteria: Done when an isolated AWS Lambda implements only the shared pinned-RepositoryReader plus signer broker protocol for complete zero/multi-object OPEN/ISSUE/FINALIZE sessions. Production Function URL events and fake S3 cover malformed/base64/oversize bodies, hostile headers/path/method, cold key rotation, stale roots, read/sign faults, and secret-free logs under explicit budgets. IAM/SAM and artifact closure grant exact canonical reads and ingress PutObject signing only—no canonical write, LIST/DELETE, root CAS, F10, SQL, or RepositoryApplier semantic fork. Opt-in live smoke uploads an attachment and exact pile directly to retained S3 ingress without bodies crossing Lambda; teardown preserves ingress and canonical buckets.
notes: 2026-07-30 local implementation slice: Function URL v2 adapter, exact route/body normalization, durable exact-version Secrets Manager keyring loading, narrow canonical reader, isolated S3 signer, least-authority SAM role/alarms/logs, external-bucket/secret lifecycle, and safe update/remove ownership checks. Complete sessions are tested through HttpBrokerTransport -> Lambda event adapter -> shared broker, and tests prove provider bodies never enter Lambda. Full repository gate: 917 passed, 12 skipped. Remains open for live SAM/S3 smoke, browser/front-door choice, and atomic create-only CloudFormation mutation (children .1 and .4).

title: Bound adversarial RangeTree leaves without losing deterministic locality
description: RangeTree leaf cuts currently occur only when int(fid[:8],16) mod 64 is zero. That gives a useful expected density for honest hashes, but fact authors can vary signed fact bytes and grind arbitrarily long runs containing no boundary. The resulting home leaf is not deterministically bounded in row count, encoded bytes, object fetches, or Worker memory. Today an overlarge encoded pile can wedge publication; after one-residence reference leaves, the reference vector and its per-fact fetch fanout remain attackable.
design: Step back to the ordered-set partition problem. Define a history-independent authenticated partition with explicit worst-case row/byte/fetch bounds under adversarial keys while retaining bounded local path-copy updates. A simple position-count fallback is not automatically acceptable because insertion before the fallback shifts every downstream chunk. Evaluate a deterministic multi-level/key-interval construction, bounded-bucket trie, or another rule whose split/merge neighborhood and proof are explicit. The same pure partitioner must drive full build, incremental update, client, and DB-free publisher. Reject probabilistic-only claims and any range directory/SQLite dependency.
acceptance_criteria: A generated adversary grinds at least N consecutive non-boundary fids and cannot produce a leaf above the normative row, encoded-byte, fact-fetch, or memory ceiling. Arbitrary insertion/removal/restore histories yield byte-identical full and incremental RangeTree roots; one change touches only a proved bounded neighborhood plus tree depth. Tests cover keys at all split/merge edges, maximum-size fact blobs, a one-over attempt rejected before catalog/root mutation, cold Worker fetch budgets, and ordinary random distributions. Document the mathematical invariant and measured constant cost.
notes:
2026-07-30 architecture audit (bounded partition + btreap): a hard count fallback after a content cut is not local: across an adversarial run with no natural cuts, insertion before the first fallback shifts every later forced boundary, so it rewrites Theta(n/L) leaves. Recursive/content-defined hash cuts retain the same gap attack; a static prefix bucket is bounded only until an author concentrates keys in one prefix.

Recommended replacement: one canonical bounded radix/Patricia Merkle-map codec shared by FactOrderMap (the current wire RangeTree role), FactTree, SuppTree, and AuthorityTree. Map keys are canonically bounded byte strings; a node is the unique recursive partition of an ordered map: a leaf iff its complete sorted key/value rows fit BOTH LEAF_MAX_ROWS and LEAF_MAX_BYTES, otherwise it is a compressed radix branch at the first distinguishing byte with bounded-fanout children. A FactOrderMap leaf stores only sorted (fact-key, raw-oid) references, never fact bodies; generic index maps use the same codec with their bounded values. Child summaries carry the exact count/encoded-row budget needed to decide a bounded collapse. Full build and incremental path-copy call this same pure partitioner, hence yield byte-identical roots. An update reads/writes only the changed leaf/its bounded rows plus at most MAX_KEY_BYTES compressed branch nodes; a split/merge cannot cascade into a sibling interval.

This is also the concrete resolution of poc-16-xjk: btreap priority H(seed,key) is public and authors can grind a co-monotone key/priority sequence, so a direct one-row B-treap removes raw-leaf amplification but still has unbounded depth and publication DoS. A history-independent rank-balanced BST instead moves an insertion near the front into Theta(n) downstream rank changes. Radix geometry is fixed by the finite key universe, so it gives all three: canonical history independence, finite worst-case depth, and local path copying.

Costs/flow: a cold sync diffs map nodes by oid and obtains a bounded page of raw oids; it batches those immutable fact objects under the existing byte/request caps. The old range closure-sibling/two-wave routing disappears, but it must be replaced by the root-authenticated historical AdmissionProof/candidate route; raw point refs alone cannot reconstruct canonical dependency selection. This aligns with poc-16-x1p.17.11.2.1, which must bound that proof transfer. A direct one-row map is simpler semantically but creates one object/page per row and up to one map-page traversal per fact; bounded reference leaves retain a hard fanout while materially reducing objects/fetches.

Prerequisites already tracked: poc-16-x1p.17.12 must impose a canonical logical key/value budget before map construction; otherwise no finite radix depth/page bound exists. Current MAX_OBJECT_BYTES/MAX_PILE_BYTES = 64 MiB also means a separate ingress/deployment fact-object budget is needed before promising a smaller publisher-memory ceiling. Detached file blobs are not map-leaf bytes and remain demand-fetched.

Test plan: use tiny radix/leaf parameters to prove the universal shape law, then production constants. Generate N fact keys sharing arbitrarily long prefixes/non-boundary fids; assert every leaf row/byte/ref count and every node fanout/depth cap. Compare full build against random singleton/batch insert, remove, restore, and split/collapse-edge histories byte-for-byte.
