Count authenticated reads/writes for one change and prove the declared MAX_KEY_BYTES + bounded-leaf budget; reject N+1 key/value/row-byte inputs before catalog/root mutation. Diff two roots and assert bounded map-page/object batches plus admission-proof closure verification, including cold Worker caps. Retain ordinary random-distribution coverage, but do not use it as a safety proof. Add a regression showing the replacement has no priority function and the existing grounded-treap vector cannot create a deep map.
Protocol constraint found during audit: this codec only gives a whole-dial fetch bound if its oid-diff is resumable/paged. Current manifest.compare and action_rows call Reader.items() over a remote root with a one-million-page default (tracked by poc-16-mjq). The replacement must expose a bounded mismatch frontier (root oid pairs / continuation) and return no more than the declared node/reference/object-byte budget per turn; a caller resumes from retained local cursor/work. Merely replacing the tree shape while retaining whole-tree compare would not meet the Worker/sync acceptance criterion.
Implementation branch codex/bounded-merkle-map now provides the shared canonical bounded radix codec and migrates current RangeTree/FactTree/SuppTree/AuthorityTree callers. Independent hostile-page review found and fixed: late-label range overfetch, stale historical oid pruning, hidden-label nonmembership, ancestor-neighbor fallback loss, null/deletion ambiguity, short child bounds escaping ValueError, and same-oid forged child descriptors. The map primitive is green, but this bead must remain open until the admission branch replaces grouped pile leaves with direct fact.key -> raw_oid FactOrder rows and cold-worker acceptance is integrated. New blocker poc-16-x1p.17.16 tracks the discovered 770-page codec bound versus deployed 128-fetch/4 MiB mint envelope.
The direct FactOrder map and shared bounded radix codec are integrated on 5da386d. Independent review added canonical outer-descriptor corroboration: every Reader and path-copy update checks snapshot count/depth at the root decode, including known-page and equal-root-diff bypasses, Candidate/Worker reads, and all four incremental map call sites. Review child poc-16-x1p.17.14.1 is closed.
Completed at branch tip 5da386d. Grouped RangeTree leaves were removed, not patched: direct FactOrder fact.key->raw_oid rows use the same canonical bounded radix map as Fact/Supp/Authority. Full/incremental histories are byte-identical; hostile prefix/fanout/byte/split/collapse/diff vectors prove finite row, page, depth, and local path-copy bounds. Remaining aggregate-dial and deployed-mint envelope work stays isolated in .17.17 and .17.16.
close_reason: Resolved by the shared bounded radix map and direct FactOrder at 5da386d; distinct aggregate diff/mint envelope gaps remain tracked in .17.17/.17.16.

title: Bound cold admission-witness transfer and verification
description:
Bound cold admission-witness transfer and verification for RepositoryApplier and RepositoryReader. Historical proof DAGs, scattered candidate point reads, current dependency growth, and shared/diamond closures must fit an explicit hosted-recipient fetch/byte/memory/work envelope or be rejected before canonical mutation.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Generate maximum and one-over admission witnesses with scattered, shared, diamond, dormant, eligible, and action paths; verify them cold with missing/corrupt/delayed objects in all actor adapters.
design: Make the selected historical witness closure itself the bounded transfer/verification unit. Reuse stable content-addressed fact residences and proof nodes directly, and add only the authenticated candidate-membership evidence needed to bind them to the selected root; do not walk current rewired edges or enumerate the corpus. Prefer a shared-page Merkle multiproof/batched candidate lookup over 256 independent point paths. Define explicit fetch, byte, depth, and memory ceilings below both deployment limits, resumable cache-miss outcomes, and poison isolation. The running verifier used by host, Lambda, and Worker must enforce the same limits.
acceptance_criteria: Done when worst-shape maximum and one-over histories bound transfer and verification of the selected root-authenticated admission witness for scattered fids, shared/diamond paths, dormant/eligible/action candidates, missing/corrupt objects, delay, and current-edge growth. Hosted AWS/Cloudflare and full-P2P use identical RepositoryReader/RepositoryApplier proof code and aggregate budgets with no SQL, LIST, current-edge substitution, or corpus scan. Any over-budget or malformed witness fails before canonical mutation; no valid admitted pile later becomes untransferable, and RepositoryApplier cannot mint F10 for unsupported work.

title: Replace R2 temporary-credential detour with exact presigned PUT URLs
description: The generated Cloudflare boundary currently mints an exact-path temporary credential, which forces the client to become an S3 SigV4 implementation and creates a second transport shape. Current R2 documentation distinguishes presigned URLs for one operation on one object from temporary credentials for multi-operation SDK sessions. Our broker grants exactly one PUT, so the existing detour is unnecessary.
design: Add a small segregated R2 SigV4 presigner behind the provider-neutral AuthorizedPut to UploadCapability interface. It uses only the isolated-ingress parent access key, secret, account endpoint, bucket, and region auto; signs PUT, exact class-first key, Content-Type, exact Content-Length, If-None-Match star, fixed session-bounded expiry, and any R2-required unsigned-payload field. It never receives canonical credentials. Replace the temporary-credential response/tests and keep the client wire protocol identical to AWS. R2 staging remains untrusted: the publisher still verifies SHA-256 before canonical promotion because a presigned R2 PUT does not prove collision-resistant body binding.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic SigV4 vectors and mutation tests prove method, account endpoint, ingress bucket, exact key, signed headers, expiry, and parent/provider binding cannot change; the returned value is the ordinary UploadCapability HTTP PUT, not credentials. Wrong body/key/length/header, overwrite attempt, expiry, URL mutation, LIST/GET/DELETE/root/canonical paths, and broker-parent canonical access fail without canonical mutation. An opt-in live R2 check uploads exact staging bytes, rejects header/key substitution and create-only replay, and reads back through a privileged test observer. Cloudflare package tests prove the old credential-shaped client path is gone or retained only as a clearly unused conformance helper. Official basis checked 2026-07-29: https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/presigned-urls/ and https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/tokens/.
notes: Implemented on codex/upload-session-protocol: the 255-line temporary-credential module is removed in favor of a 219-line pure-stdlib exact R2 SigV4 signer returning UploadCapability. It binds path-style account endpoint, ingress bucket, class-first key, PUT, Content-Length, Content-Type, If-None-Match star, auto/s3 scope, full parent-access-id binding digest, and session not_after; payload remains UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD. Deterministic golden/independent mutation tests pass, the botocore differential passes with boto3 1.40.51, and an opt-in urllib live seam is checked in. Final local gates: 199 focused passed/4 skipped; 833 full passed/12 skipped. Live R2 and browser evidence remain on x1p.3.
close_reason: Exact R2 presigned staging PUT translator, deterministic/mutation coverage, opt-in live seam, docs, and credential-detour deletion are complete.

title: Apply facts independently of detached blob completeness
description: RepositoryApplier must implement the ordinary replica rule that detached attachment availability is not fact validity. It verifies and promotes each present same-session object as bounded best-effort work, while a missing object leaves the rooted file incomplete and cannot hold valid facts or unrelated messages hostage.
design: After staged-intent parsing and kernel admission, derive the finite blob refs. For each exact same-session key, a present body must pass the per-object bound and SHA-256 check before conditional canonical promotion; absence records incomplete progress but is not a permanent ingress rejection. Run settlement, archive every admitted candidate, build root-reachable pages, CAS root, and apply F10 to the facts. Retire the exact internal pile once all admitted facts are represented even if some blob refs remain absent. Do not materialize every object at once or make LIST authoritative. The retained client marker plus immutable per-object/page receipts lets a later cold Applier retry missing objects in bounded round-robin pages; a new sender session or peer blob sync may also complete them.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic multi-chunk direct intent with one missing detached object commits every valid fact through RepositoryApplier, retires its internal pile only after F10, and reads as incomplete. Ordinary piles are fact-only and reject an embedded blobs member; unreferenced bytes cannot be established by pile application. Detached bytes enter through RepositoryApplier.admit_object or exact staged references only. After the missing same-session object appears, a cold Applier revisiting the retained marker resumes from immutable object/page receipts and completes it without republishing facts; a later sender session or peer sync is also valid. Missing, delayed, corrupt, oversized, foreign-session, and surplus objects neither block unrelated facts nor grant deletion authority. Full-P2P and hosted recipient compositions produce byte-identical fact/tree roots.

title: Add exact async retirement for database-free publishers
description: The production F10 law and synchronous host path have retire_exact, but an R2/Lambda database-free publisher has no awaited equivalent. Calling delete directly cannot reconcile an apply-response-lost result and could treat a changed same-key value as discharged.
design: Add retire_exact_async beside retire_exact. It does not authorize deletion: callers must first supply the F10 publication or permanent-rejection witness. Strongly read and compare exact bytes before delete, reconcile an exception by a strong read, accept absence only, and refuse any surviving or changed value. Keep source key/bytes explicit; do not add ownership claims, locks, or provider branches.
acceptance_criteria: Realistic async fake and R2-binding tests cover absent source, exact success, changed source before delete, lost response after apply, failure before apply, surviving exact bytes, changed value observed during reconciliation, and read failure. The helper never deletes root/obj through adapters and no ambiguous outcome is mapped to success without a strong absent read.
notes: Implemented and pushed in 21e1c91. retire_exact_async mirrors the synchronous F10-gated mechanism and reconciles ambiguous delete through a strong exact read. Native R2-binding tests cover absence, success, changed source, apply-response-lost, failure-before-apply, no-op delete, authoritative-key refusal, and initial/reconciliation read failure. Focused object-store/direct-upload suite: 46 passed.
close_reason: Awaited exact-retirement mechanism and realistic R2 failure tests are on main in 21e1c91; F10 authorization remains the publisher caller's obligation.

title: Separate detached blob completeness from F10-governed pile retirement
description: The earlier design treated a missing staged attachment object as a reason to withhold every fact and retain its pile forever. That clashes with the running peer model: valid file/chunk facts may be published and relayed while a Bao object is absent, and queries report incomplete until another source supplies it. A second bug compounded it: the session-first ingress grammar made the generated provider lifecycle prefix match both loose objects and durable pile markers, so lifecycle could erase the sole work item without F10.
design: Resolved 2026-07-30: object bytes are detached completeness, not fact validity. A publisher verifies and promotes every present referenced object one at a time, but missing blob bytes do not block kernel admission, candidate retention, settlement, root CAS, or F10 retirement after every admitted fact is durably represented. Rooted chunk facts remain the authenticated demand; a staged object landing after marker retirement is an unreachable orphan and cannot create work. Change the physical grammar to class-first ingress/v1/workspaces/{ws}/objects/{session}/{digest} and ingress/v1/workspaces/{ws}/piles/{session}/{member}/{digest}. Provider lifecycle may cover only the objects prefix; pile markers are retired only by publisher or rejection paths after F10. This removes any need to prove future non-arrival of an in-flight PUT.
acceptance_criteria: The normative core grammar, AWS policy, R2 credential generator, README, and DESIGN use disjoint class-first prefixes. Generated lifecycle matches the workspace objects prefix and provably cannot match the piles prefix. Existing real sync tests continue to publish file/chunk facts with missing blobs and later complete them. The store publisher receives a separate implementation test: missing staged blobs yield published-but-incomplete files and never block or justify marker deletion before all admitted facts are rooted.
notes:
Decision implemented in the pending class-first grammar patch: lifecycle safety follows from prefix disjointness rather than timeout guesses. Existing tests/test_attachments.py::test_unchanged_root_retries_a_missing_proof is running evidence that facts are publishable independently of detached Bao bytes.
Implemented and pushed in 596c39b. Core, AWS IAM, R2 credentials, generated lifecycle, README, and DESIGN now share class-first object and pile prefixes. The object lifecycle prefix cannot match a pile marker. Focused direct-upload, F10, repository, and real attachment suite: 186 passed, 7 skipped. Actual missing-blob store-publisher behavior is isolated in child poc-16-x1p.17.2.6.
close_reason: Decision is encoded on main in 596c39b: detached blobs do not gate fact validity, and prefix-disjoint lifecycle cannot erase F10-governed pile markers.

title: Path-copy RangeTree removals, restorations, and edge refreshes
description: manifest.update performs bounded authenticated neighbor discovery for additions, but deactivation, dormant restoration, and rank or edge refresh still fall back to a Catalog-wide key scan and full rebuild. The database-free publisher has no Node.keys and cannot enumerate the range map, so these ordinary suppression and authority transitions lack a shared incremental primitive.
design: Generalize the existing authenticated RangeTree neighbor-window compiler to accept exact old and new reconciliation keys for add, remove, restore, and closure refresh. From the pinned RangeTree, perform bounded predecessor and successor reads, verify every touched old leaf pile, recompute only the minimal deterministic leaf window under the same content-derived boundary rule, and path-copy replacement rows. The function is pure over a pinned root, authenticated cache, candidate and edge callbacks, and immutable emitter; both client Publisher and store-only publisher call it. Full build remains repair and format-cut only.
acceptance_criteria: Randomized insertion, removal, restoration, winner suppression or fallback, and edge-rank refresh histories produce byte-identical RangeTree and composite roots between incremental and full builds for every delivery order. A one-candidate transition never calls Node.keys, scans Catalog facts, or enumerates RangeTree; object reads and writes are bounded by tree depth plus touched leaves. Tests cover first or last key, empty or singleton tree, simultaneous neighboring changes, split or merge boundaries, CAS rebase, missing or mutated pages, and N or N+1 turn budgets.
notes: Landed on main as cf9830c. RangeReplacement groups authenticated local windows for added, removed, restored, and edge/closure-refreshed keys. Removing a content-derived boundary joins only its home leaf and immediate successor; unrelated windows remain separate. Publisher no longer gates RangeTree incrementality on authority_changed/deactivated and calls no Node.keys on ordinary transitions. Randomized mixed transitions converge byte-for-byte with the full reference build; a deterministic member-removal boundary test hard-fails any Node.keys call. Full gate: 819 passed, 10 optional-provider skips.
close_reason: General transition path-copy compiler, publisher integration, design law, and realistic differential tests landed on main.

title: Index action targets and authorization guards for bounded settlement
description: Current SQL settlement finds action frontiers through proposal scans. The database-free RepositoryApplier needs authenticated family-neutral routes from suppression targets and authorization guards to every relevant eligible or dormant action proposal, so delete/removal/clear transitions can settle without a corpus scan.
design: Publish generic fact.action-target and fact.action-guard postings plus bounded FactRecord fields after running-kernel edge resolution, including dormant proposals without standing. The one RepositoryApplier queries changed ranges, folds eligible proposals by fact key, and follows reverse dependencies to the fixed point. Remove global SQL scans; any local projection is derived from the committed root.
acceptance_criteria: Done when the pure compiler mechanically emits bounded authenticated action-target and action-guard routes for every family-declared suppression/deletion/removal action, including dormant proposals. Author/admin delete, member removal, competing actions, guard removal, suppression active/clear/fallback, dormant restoration, and unrelated histories let a cold database-free RepositoryApplier settle the exact affected fixed point and match full compilation without enumerating actions/candidates or reading SQL. Missing, duplicate, wrong-target, wrong-guard, malformed, and one-over inputs fail before mutation. Active action rows in SQLite are only disposable projection rows; family policy owns semantics and no action-specific tree, branch, compiler, or alternate applier is introduced.
notes: 2026-07-30 alignment clarification: the replacement removes authorization_guards entirely. Named Needs plus exact resolved admission edges/proofs are the historical witness; only explicit suppression targets and authority_liveness_guards receive current-state routes under poc-16-x1p.17.2.9.
close_reason: Invalidated and superseded, not completed: authorization guards are immutable admission evidence, not retroactive liveness routes. Replacement poc-16-x1p.17.2.9 is limited to explicit suppression targets and declared continuing authority-liveness selectors.

title: Index declared-Need consumers for bounded canonical rewiring
description: A database-free RepositoryApplier can list providers at an offer address and reverse dependents of one exact resolved edge, but it cannot find every retained fact whose declared Need must be re-resolved when the canonical admitted provider winner changes. Publish a canonical family-neutral need-consumer route so the recipient never scans FactTree or consults a full-node database. This route is for changes in the canonical admitted dependency graph, not for suppression/removal liveness.
design: Mechanically derive a canonical base Need address from each registered-family Need after the fact passes the running shape door, and publish one generic need-consumer posting for every admitted candidate, dormant or eligible. The one RepositoryApplier compiler writes it and its bounded authenticated query reads it when candidate joins or canonical proof-rank/provider changes require edge recomputation. A later suppression action does not re-resolve a historical admission edge; explicit action targets and current authority-liveness selectors are handled by poc-16-x1p.17.2.9. SQLite may mirror rows for local queries but supplies no second answer.
acceptance_criteria: The pure compiler emits one bounded authenticated need-consumer route for every registered-family Need and every admitted eligible or dormant candidate. Seeded provider A/B joins, proof-rank winner changes, co-offer matches/mismatches, canonical edge rewires, dormant insertion/restoration, opposite arrival, and restart let a cold database-free RepositoryApplier discover exactly the affected consumers, recompute named edges/ranks under immutable family validation, and match the full compiler without corpus or SQL scans. Removal/suppression activation or clear alone never rewires a selected historical admission edge or changes candidate standing; poc-16-x1p.17.2.9 updates only current-use state. Exact limit and one-over malformed Needs fail before mutation. No family index, second compiler, second applier, or authorization-guard route appears.

title: Provision and rotate stateless upload-session keys across cold brokers
description: Stateless session cursors are correct only if every cold broker instance for one provider deployment sees the same authenticated key ring and provider or issuer binding for the full cursor lifetime. A module-local random key, destructive secret replacement, changed default TTL reinterpretation, or early removal of the old key strands valid uploads after Lambda or Worker restart.
design: Provision provider-bound key rings separately: AWS uses a generated Secrets Manager secret readable only by the upload-broker role; Cloudflare uses encrypted Worker secret bindings readable only by the broker Worker. Bind a stable deployment issuer and exact provider target into every cursor. Implement two-phase rotation: distribute old plus new verification keys everywhere, switch one active issuance key, wait maximum session TTL plus clock skew and deployment propagation, then remove the retired key. Cursor bytes carry key id, issued time, and fixed expiry, so later config changes do not reinterpret them. Deploy and remove commands pin secret identity, never print material, refuse takeover, and preserve secrets or explicitly confirm their deletion independently from canonical and ingress buckets. Cross-provider resume is not supported; starting on another provider creates another session.
acceptance_criteria: Done when fresh Lambda and Worker broker instances open, advance, and finalize the same provider-bound session using only durable deployment-managed signing-key rings. Seeded tests rotate at every protocol boundary, vary TTL, delay rollout, restart with old/new subsets, mutate key id/issuer/provider, and cross AWS/R2; only the declared overlap survives and every cross-scope or retired-key case fails closed. Generated policies grant the broker pinned canonical reads plus exact ingress signing but no canonical write, root CAS, RepositoryApplier/F10, or provider-policy mutation. Logs/config/argv contain no secret bytes, and removal preserves keys needed by in-window sessions plus both buckets.
notes: 2026-07-30 AWS slice adds an initial provider-bound Secrets Manager keyring creator that keeps bytes in a mode-0600 temp file, returns only exact ARN/version, and pins Lambda cold starts to that immutable VersionId. Runtime checks provider and issuer. Still open for two-phase distribute/activate/retire control-plane commands, cross-instance rollout evidence, Cloudflare rotation, and possibly-applied mutation reconciliation (.2).

title: Bind staged pile intent to its broker session and uploader
description: Bind an exact broker-authorized staging key and marker to one typed RepositoryApplier preparation door. The configured workspace, key workspace/session, final digest, pile envelope workspace, and every ordinary fact must agree before any canonical write. The key's member segment records the broker-authenticated uploader but is not required to equal every fact author: legitimate relay is part of the ordinary pile model. Verified present detached objects are promoted through RepositoryApplier; the exact fact-only pile is copied create-only to a fresh internal generation and then passed to the same apply transition. The client marker is never root or retirement authority.
design: Use the one provider-neutral StagedPileIntent parser in Lambda, Cloudflare, host, and fakes. It receives configured workspace, exact listed/notified marker key, and bounded bytes; strictly parses ingress/v1/workspaces/{ws64}/piles/{nonce32}/{member16}/{sha256}; validates lowercase canonical segments and h(raw); decodes the ordinary canonical closed-pile codec against that workspace; rejects embedded blobs and every workspace-less ordinary fact; and derives sorted unique facts.blob_refs under ingress/v1/workspaces/{ws64}/objects/{nonce32}/{sha256}. Member/session come only from the broker-derived path, never caller JSON. The path member records whose upload proof was attenuated; it does not forbid legitimate relay of valid facts authored by other workspace members. No envelope or second serializer is needed. Missing detached objects are file-completeness state, not invalid intent. Parent-credential compromise may erase/poison staging but cannot bypass fact signatures, workspace binding, object hashes, kernel judgment, canonical promotion, or root CAS.
acceptance_criteria: Done when one provider-neutral staged-intent parser validates the exact configured workspace, canonical marker key, broker-derived member/session segments, pile digest/bytes, fact-only envelope, every ordinary fact workspace, derived referenced-object keys, and explicit limits unchanged in full-P2P, AWS, and Cloudflare with sqlite3 fatal on receive. The broker, not RepositoryApplier, authenticates the uploader and binds that identity/workspace/session into exact create-only capabilities; the Applier never equates uploader with fact authors and preserves legitimate relay. RepositoryApplier fetches the exact retained marker itself, independently hashes and kernel-validates it, copies the pile behind a fresh internal generation, promotes only verified referenced same-session objects in bounded pages, and alone performs root CAS/F10. Cross-session/workspace/path/digest substitution, surplus/corrupt objects, replay, delay, dropped events, and concurrent claims fail safely; missing objects remain retryable completeness work. Broker, sender, and provider PUT receipts grant no admission/deletion authority, and client ingress is never deleted by F10.
notes: The provider-neutral staged-intent parser is implemented and shared. Keep open until AWS, Cloudflare, and full-P2P direct upload invoke RepositoryApplier on separate retained ingress and canonical stores with deterministic marker-to-internal claims, typed terminal evidence, and no client-ingress F10 deletion.

title: Resume one broker-minted upload session across bounded batches
description: The bounded upload broker safely caps one request at PAGE_BATCH descriptors and mints a fresh session per request. A file or closure with more than 255 objects therefore cannot upload multiple bounded object batches and then place one closed-pile marker in the same broker-pinned session.
design: Use a broker-authenticated fixed Merkle-vector commitment and a constant-size HMAC cursor token; do not add DynamoDB, Durable Objects, or another session database for integrity. OPEN first authorizes the upload-purpose closure and pins workspace, member, broker nonce, issuer/provider, protocol version, fixed expiry, object count/byte quota, pile digest/size, and a domain-separated root over the complete strictly digest-sorted unique (digest,size) vector. It returns next_index=0 and issues no PUTs. ISSUE accepts at most PAGE_BATCH contiguous leaves plus a range multiproof, proves them against the fixed root, and advances only a committed prefix. Reissuing an already-covered range is idempotent and returns no new authority; gaps, partial overlap, alternate leaves, rollback that seeks new authority, and any field/MAC mutation fail. FINALIZE requires the complete committed prefix and derives the sole precommitted pile key; exact replay can only reissue that same key. A rolling accumulator alone is insufficient because replay-forking can authorize unbounded suffixes. Provider state is needed only for exactly-once accounting or server-side recovery after the client loses its token, neither of which is a canonical-safety requirement. The client retains the latest opaque token plus its source manifest; loss starts a new session and lifecycle collects abandoned object staging. Capability TTL is bounded by the fixed session expiry, and object retention must exceed session TTL plus skew and retry margin. This protocol orders capability issuance, not network completion: FINALIZE is allowed after the entire descriptor vector has been authorized, even if some detached object PUTs are absent. The pile can publish and retire once all admitted facts have an F10 witness; missing attachment bytes leave the rooted file incomplete and may be supplied later by a new session or peer sync.
acceptance_criteria: Realistic 4,096-object and maximum-session vectors issue across randomized batches of at most PAGE_BATCH with constant-size tokens, bounded request/memory use, broker restart, and client restart from its retained opaque token. Every valid partition converges to the same final token and exactly the precommitted N object keys plus one pile key. Tests mutate workspace, member, session, issuer, key id, expiry, count, totals, vector root, proof nodes, digest, size, ordering, insertion/removal, duplicate, gap, future range, partial overlap, quota overflow, and provider request fields. Same-token forks, old-token replay, duplicate batches, lost ISSUE/FINALIZE responses, and exact FINALIZE replay are idempotently confined to the fixed authority set and can never mint alternate authority; literal replay rejection is not claimed without provider state. Tests cover HMAC key rotation, fixed-expiry and provider-TTL boundaries, client-token loss creating only abandoned object staging, and lifecycle retention longer than the active/retry window. Marker-before-object visibility, dropped/duplicate notifications, and missing attachments do not block valid fact publication: after F10 the pile may retire and file queries report incomplete. Present exact objects promote safely; corrupt, oversized, foreign, and surplus staged objects never become canonical or authorize deletion.
notes:
Analysis found that stateless lost-response retry and literal replay rejection are mutually incompatible. Acceptance now requires idempotent authority confinement. A fixed vector commitment prevents the unbounded replay-fork authority of a rolling accumulator. Initial finite limits should be selected from measured deployment bounds; 65,536 objects (Merkle depth 16) and a 24-hour session are candidate values, not yet normative. Decide whether to persist root/count/total in a versioned pile envelope for audit; canonical safety does not require the broker nonce in pile bytes because the session path binds it and the publisher independently validates every referenced object.
The publisher does not use object completeness as authorization or settlement state. OPEN and ISSUE still enforce objects-first capability ordering; after FINALIZE, any missing detached Bao object yields an incomplete rooted file rather than withholding valid facts. Class-first grammar is normative as of 596c39b.
Landed on main as 55dc756. The fixed-vector Merkle protocol, constant-size HMAC cursor, OPEN/ISSUE/FINALIZE broker, replay confinement, restart/key rotation, 4,096-object histories, and response/request budgets are executable. AuthorizedPut carries the fixed session deadline; the real S3 signer attenuates SigV4 expiry to it, rounds down whole seconds, and fails closed when less than one second remains. Full branch gate: 815 passed, 10 optional-provider skips. Authorization revocation staleness remains explicitly separate in .17.3.1.1; deployed endpoints/client/publisher remain .17.1/.17.3/.17.2/.17.5.
Alignment correction, 2026-07-30: retained client markers plus immutable per-object/page receipts also allow a later cold RepositoryApplier to promote delayed same-session objects. A new session or peer sync is optional, not the sole completion route. References to a publisher mean the current RepositoryApplier role.
close_reason: Fixed finite multi-batch session protocol and realistic tests landed on main.

title: Replace raw action-evidence piles with admission-proof DAG witnesses
description: Remove any raw action-evidence pile duplication by using the same content-addressed admission-proof DAG and canonical fact residence as every retained candidate. RepositoryApplier and RepositoryReader use the exact shared verifier; neither owns a parallel action proof format.
design: SuppTree remains exactly CLEAR or ACTIVE(action_fid). ACTIVE names only the immutable action fid. The action's authenticated FactTree record reaches its canonical fact residence and admission-proof DAG; the shared archive verifier follows those bounded nodes and reruns the running kernel. There is no raw action-evidence pile, action-specific proof codec, or proof-root field in SuppTree.
acceptance_criteria: No action evidence duplicates fact bytes and SuppTree values are exactly CLEAR or ACTIVE(action_fid). RepositoryApplier and RepositoryReader corroborate an active fid through the same FactTree candidate record, canonical fact residence, and admission-proof DAG used for every retained candidate. Altered, missing, cyclic, and cross-workspace witnesses fail reconstruction; full-P2P, AWS, and Cloudflare wrappers use the same verifier and format.
notes: Alignment correction: the earlier proposed action-slot proof-root field is invalidated. The running four-map compiler already satisfies this bead by storing only action_fid in SuppTree and retaining proof reachability in the ordinary FactTree candidate record.
close_reason: Implemented by the shared candidate FactRecord/admission DAG; superseded the non-aligned extra SuppTree proof-root field.

title: Seal durable candidate admission behind kernel Valid receipts
description: Node.merge currently accepts raw Fact values, so internal callers can place forged or unsigned inactive rows in the catalog without a kernel judgment. Rooting every catalog row would turn this bypass into durable admitted state. Durable candidate retention must begin at one kernel-mediated membrane.
design: Make the durable path consume kernel-minted Valid receipts carrying exact resolved edges. Catalog.stage records only such receipts plus an admission-proof reference. Remove or rename raw-Fact Node.merge; scratch/rebuild loading must use an explicitly non-durable path or rerun drain. Add a repository ratchet proving every production admission call is kernel-mediated.
acceptance_criteria: A forged raw Fact cannot create a catalog candidate, generic posting, proof object, or root change. Every durable candidate admitted by daemon, local authoring, peer sync, rebuild, and future serverless publication has a successful running-kernel Valid receipt and exact edge witness. Realistic tests exercise every call site and the full suite remains green.
close_reason: Implemented on main in c8b3204: Node.admit is the sole durable catalog door, it runs the production kernel and stores canonical exact-edge receipts; ScratchCatalog raw loading is in-memory-only and repository ratchets cover every caller. Full rebased suite: 707 passed, 2 skipped; focused main integration: 118 passed.

title: Bind retirement obligation checker to the canonical workspace pile format
description: The F10 retirement checker landed after the workspace-binding worktree branched and still decoded piles through the removed ambient-workspace API. Its fixtures also constructed ws-less ordinary facts. This made the two independently green branches fail when combined on main and, if merely shimmed, could classify rejection under the wrong workspace.
design: Pass the authenticated trace workspace into every immutable pile decode, construct hostile ordinary facts/piles with that workspace, and keep the static destructive-call inventory aligned with the running source.
acceptance_criteria: The retirement obligation, peer capability, workspace binding, and repository-layout suites pass together on main; typed rejection classification uses the same expected-workspace decoder as production.
notes: Fixed in 8cfe94a. Combined focused integration suite: 40 passed.
close_reason: Fixed in 8cfe94a; combined retirement/workspace suite passes.

title: Keep every recipient-restorable candidate root-reachable
description: A database-free RepositoryApplier can reproduce recipient state only when every kernel-admitted durable candidate, including dormant candidates that may regain standing, remains authenticated and root-reachable after exact pile retirement. No full-node SQLite row, ingress marker, object-store LIST result, or arrival-order cache may be the sole residence or admission witness.
design: The root authenticates a monotone join of kernel-admitted durable candidates. Each candidate has one stable obj/H(encode(fact)) residence, one FactTree record with selected historical admission proof/state/canonical edges/rank/routes, and one minimum complete content-addressed raw-free proof DAG. Canonical eligibility may change only when the admitted dependency graph/provider selection changes; suppression and current authority liveness do not rewrite admission standing. FactOrder contains only eligible fact.key -> fact oid rows. The shared verifier reruns the actual kernel. RepositoryApplier and RepositoryReader reconstruct only root-reachable objects; SQLite, ingress, arrival caches, and LIST are never authority. Candidate deletion waits for a separate proof.
acceptance_criteria: A cold recipient given only root plus reachable immutable objects reconstructs the same admitted candidate join, canonical standing, and current suppression/liveness answers as a full P2P node. Losing offers and canonical rewires cover dormant insertion/restoration. Suppression activation/clear and member/device removal leave historical admitted facts eligible while current Reader authoring/mint/authority answers change. Opposite post-removal arrival orders converge to the same retained candidate/root. Every durable candidate entered through a running-kernel Valid receipt, has exactly one canonical fact residence and selected complete proof DAG, and participates in mechanical postings. Same base plus pile yields identical roots in both actor compositions; malformed, missing, cyclic, mismatched, or cross-workspace data fails closed.
notes: The admission archive and one-residence FactOrder layout landed. Cold verification covers anchor identity, descriptors, candidate/witness joins, dormant restoration, and full projection. Remaining work is bounded incremental RepositoryApplier use, the legacy local-cache format cut, and proof-transfer budgets. Prior RangeTree, embedded-pile, and dormant-blob-only alternatives are retired history.

title: Prevent broker-parent mutation from erasing acknowledged ingress
description:
A dedicated ingress bucket protects canonical integrity, but today's broad R2 parent token can still DELETE an acknowledged staged object or pile. That destroys the only durable work item before publication and violates the ingress retirement obligation under broker-parent compromise.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Begin an authorized ingress PUT immediately before expiry, delay completion past expiry and skew, acknowledge the marker, then attempt deletion with every broker-parent credential before RepositoryApplier can copy it.
design: Decide the explicit availability threat boundary. If broker-parent compromise is in scope, obtain a provider primitive or upload gateway whose broker parent can create but cannot delete acknowledged ingress, or move acknowledgement behind a separate verifier-controlled durable boundary. Bucket lifecycle may collect abandoned sessions but must not impersonate witnessed retirement.
acceptance_criteria: Done when provider policy makes every acknowledged client-writable ingress object and exact pile marker unavailable to broker-parent deletion until independent lifecycle criteria are proved; documentation-only acceptance of erasure is not sufficient. Adversarial generated-policy and live-provider tests compromise every broker-held parent credential, race delete with a pre-expiry in-flight PUT, restart cold brokers/appliers, and prove acknowledged ingress remains fetchable for RepositoryApplier or is protected by a provider-enforced tombstone/grace law. No client key is retired by F10, no broker receipt is commit evidence, and canonical integrity isolation remains separate from ingress availability.
notes:
The direct-upload method now separates the two claims: a broad ingress parent passes canonical isolation but fails exercise_ingress_retirement_boundary because it can DELETE acknowledged stage object/pile keys; an abstract PUT-only parent passes. No claim is made that current R2 can issue the latter. Resolve this bead before treating broker-parent compromise as F10-safe.
Provider-doc check 2026-07-29: temporary child credentials can name actions=[PutObject], but the broker parent Object Read & Write token remains the broad authority under test. README/DESIGN now distinguish canonical integrity from acknowledged-ingress availability and keep the latter decision open.
The .17.10.1 running history found the exact-value retirement precondition: provider DELETE has no compare-by-value guard, so get/exact-DELETE/read-back is safe only while every accepted same-address write is create-only and body-bound. The model's broker-parent overwrite control is retained and refuses retirement; resolve this bead for both overwrite and DELETE authority, not DELETE alone.
Executable negative schedule: test_parent_replacement_between_exact_get_and_delete_is_rejected pauses retire_exact after its exact GET, uses the broad broker-parent PUT to replace the acknowledged value, then resumes unconditional DELETE. The helper necessarily removes the replacement because providers expose no delete-if-value; check_stage_cleanup rejects the first overwrite with a deterministic replay prefix. This is why .17.9.1 must remove/accept that parent authority rather than treating read-back as atomic conditional deletion.

title: Validate invite bootstrap before mutating local workspace state
description: Invite redemption decoded a second raw fact-list format, selected the last invitation by tag, and called add_workspace before proving that the outer link workspace, encrypted blob workspace, closed bootstrap workspace, genesis anchor, and every bootstrap fact agreed or that the complete bootstrap passed the kernel. A hostile or truncated invite could therefore mutate node-local keyring/workspace state before authoritative validation.
design: Carry the canonical base64 pile codec inside the encrypted invite. Require link W == blob W == pile W; run the database-free kernel over the complete bootstrap and require exactly one valid invitation before constructing the member or calling add_workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Foreign-inner-pile and incomplete-proof invite vectors both fail before node.workspaces or keyring bytes change; a valid invite still joins through the ordinary pile path.
notes: Implemented canonical encrypted invite piles and validated link W == blob W == pile W. core.kernel.drain must accept the complete bootstrap and yield exactly one valid user_invite before member construction or Node.add_workspace. Regression vectors cover foreign inner W and incomplete proof with byte-identical keyring/workspace state before and after. Full suite: 576 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Fixed and covered by invite-before-keyring adversarial tests.

title: Reject foreign receipts during catalog reopen and reindex
description: Catalog.stage is not the only receipt door. Existing canonical blobs are replayed by schema upgrade, explicit reindex, and Node reopen/rebuild. Without an expected anchor on those paths, a foreign receipt already on disk can regenerate generic routes and reach eligibility/publication under the wrong workspace.
design: Make upgrade_schema and _reindex require the workspace anchor and reject every blob not canonically bound to it. Node.idx supplies the path/keyring workspace; Catalog.reindex uses Catalog.anchor. Keep the kernel and catalog agreement exact.
acceptance_criteria: Direct staging, explicit reindex, legacy relational upgrade, and realistic Node reopen reject foreign or ws-less ordinary receipts without publishing them; bound legacy relational receipts still migrate.
notes: Implemented anchor-required Catalog.stage, explicit reindex, legacy-schema replay, Node.idx upgrade/reopen, and root rebuild paths. Foreign canonical blobs and ws-less ordinary legacy receipts fail closed; bound legacy relational receipts still migrate. Realistic reopen/reindex negatives and full suite pass (576 passed, 2 skipped).
close_reason: Fixed and covered by stage/reindex/legacy-upgrade/reopen anchor tests.

title: Choose uniform ingress staging versus provider-native canonical PUTs
description: AWS can bind SHA-256 and create-only semantics on a presigned canonical object PUT. R2 currently has both a payload-binding question and a broad parent-token boundary, making a separate untrusted ingress bucket attractive. We must choose whether physical provider differences remain behind one logical upload interface or whether both providers use the same session-scoped staging-and-promotion protocol.
design: Use one logical isolated-staging protocol on AWS S3 and Cloudflare R2. The broker chooses exact session, workspace, member, size, digest, and header-bound PUT capabilities; clients upload detached objects directly to the ingress bucket and write the closed pile intent last; a DB-free publisher validates facts and any present object bytes, conditionally promotes immutable objects, advances the authenticated root by CAS, and retires staging under F10. Missing detached objects do not invalidate or delay an otherwise valid fact pile. Provider-specific signing, wakeup, and lifecycle mechanics stay under deploy/adapters; the client and publisher state machines remain provider-neutral. Canonical raw PUT body-binding work is related hardening, not a prerequisite for isolated staging.
acceptance_criteria: DESIGN and README state one direct-to-isolated-object-store protocol for S3 and R2, with exact capability boundaries, objects-optional/pile-last durable intent, publisher validation, CAS publication, and F10 retirement. Provider-neutral crash and poison traces cover validation, promotion, root publication, retirement, foreign paths, missing authorization, missing objects, and canonical collision. Focused bounded tests prove the shared protocol; larger provider benchmarks are not required for this architecture decision. Provider adapters and opt-in live conformance remain implementation beads.
notes:
The x1p.17.6 model runs one logical staging/promotion/F10 state machine under both S3 and R2 labels, including poison plus crashes after validation, canonical promotion, and root publication. It intentionally does not choose uniform staging versus AWS-native canonical PUT; physical adapters and measured deployment limits remain this decision bead's work.
The provider-neutral abstract corpus now covers 12 cases: clean; crash after validate/promote/root/pile-delete/object-delete; poisoned staging bytes; foreign workspace/member; missing member authorization; missing object; and preexisting canonical collision. Exact bucket/key/declared-digest binding is checked for every state transition. Real competing root CAS and ambiguous delete results remain child .17.10.1.
Direction selected 2026-07-30: use one logical isolated-staging protocol on AWS and R2 unless measured provider limits falsify it. Broker mints an exact nonce-bound session; clients PUT ingress/v1/workspaces/<ws64>/sessions/<nonce32>/obj/<sha256> objects first, then .../pile/<member16>/<sha256> last as the sole durable intent committing the session/object digests. Publishers verify and promote; direct-to-object-store still holds because bytes do not transit broker/publisher functions on upload. This keeps untrusted bytes out of canonical storage, matches the R2 authority boundary, and removes provider-specific client recovery. Keep this decision bead open only for bounded request/runtime measurements and opt-in live confirmation.
Normative staging grammar (angle-bracket placeholders were lost in an earlier CLI rendering): ingress/v1/workspaces/<ws64>/sessions/<nonce32>/obj/<sha256> and ingress/v1/workspaces/<ws64>/sessions/<nonce32>/pile/<member16>/<sha256>. Direct means client bytes go straight to the isolated S3/R2 ingress bucket; broker and publisher functions do not proxy upload bodies. The fixed-manifest stateless multi-batch protocol is specified by child poc-16-x1p.17.3.1.
Grammar correction in 596c39b: class precedes session. Object keys are ingress/v1/workspaces/{ws}/objects/{session}/{digest}; durable markers are ingress/v1/workspaces/{ws}/piles/{session}/{member}/{digest}. This is required, not cosmetic: provider lifecycle can collect only loose objects and scheduled publishers can list only piles, so lifecycle never impersonates F10.
Decision closed 2026-07-30. The provider-neutral trace suite and bounded upload-session tests support the uniform isolated-staging state machine. Per project direction, no larger benchmark gate is required. R2 exact presigned PUT URLs are child poc-16-x1p.17.1.1; isolated bucket policy is poc-16-x1p.17.9; raw canonical body-binding poc-16-x1p.17.7 is related hardening only.
close_reason: Selected and documented uniform isolated ingress staging for S3 and R2; provider-neutral traces and bounded tests establish the decision, while concrete adapters and deployments remain separate implementation beads.

title: Isolate the R2 upload broker from the canonical workspace bucket
description: The R2 broker holds a long-lived bucket-scoped Object Read and Write token. Exact presigned PUT URLs narrow the authority returned to clients, but they do not narrow that parent token, which can still read, list, write, and delete inside its bucket. The broker parent must therefore target only a separate untrusted ingress bucket and must never address the canonical workspace bucket.
design: Use the dedicated ingress bucket as the provider-enforced authority boundary. The broker has no native R2 binding and uses its ingress-only parent solely to sign one exact session-bounded PUT URL. A distinct read-only credential supplies canonical DAG reads; only the publisher has ingress and canonical mutation bindings. Publisher verification hashes staged bytes before canonical promotion. Successful staging PUT is a retryable receipt, while observed root publication is the durable workspace acknowledgement; pre-root parent erasure remains tracked by .17.9.1.
acceptance_criteria: Generated Cloudflare policy/config and adversarial tests prove that the broker parent credential itself, not merely a returned child credential, cannot read/list/delete or address any canonical workspace key. Exact child credentials cannot change action, bucket, path, body contract, or expiry. Publisher crash during staged-object verification/promotion/root CAS retains a recoverable obligation; abandoned staging expires only under a bounded ingress-bucket lifecycle and never deletes canonical data. One-command deploy/remove owns both bindings and preserves both buckets.
notes:
The x1p.17.6 model now attacks the broker parent itself with canonical root GET/PUT, workspace LIST, object/pile PUT, and object DELETE. A dedicated ingress-bucket parent passes for both provider labels; the one-bucket broad parent is a seeded first-failure negative control. Staging poison and validate/promote/root crash histories preserve F10. This remains a design oracle, not generated Cloudflare policy or live evidence.
Promotion traces now serialize and parse a symbolic staged intent carrying workspace, member, declared object digests, and member authorization; exact candidates retain foreign/unauthorized/missing/poisoned work and the oracle rejects any promotion outside that closure. Production decode_pile and mint.stateless are explicit refinement seams. The newly discovered ingress DELETE availability gap is tracked by child bug .17.9.1.
2026-07-30 generated boundary slice: deploy/cloudflare_upload now emits (1) a broker Worker with zero native R2 bindings, an exact canonical-bucket Object Read-only policy input, and a distinct exact ingress-bucket Object Read & Write parent policy input; (2) a publisher-only INGRESS+CANONICAL binding config; and (3) an ingress-prefix-only seven-day lifecycle input. The locally signed HS256 child JWT fixes bucket, exact objectPath, actions=[PutObject], issuer/audience, iat, and exp. The selected provider-neutral grammar is ingress/v1/workspaces/<ws64>/sessions/<nonce32>/obj/<sha256>, with the closed pile uploaded last at .../pile/<member16>/<sha256> as the sole durable ready marker. Credential-free tests attack canonical GET/LIST/PUT/DELETE from the ingress parent, child bucket/key/action/expiry, lifecycle scope, and compute-only deploy/remove preservation. The checked-in roles are non-public 503 stubs and provider_claim.live_verified=false. Keep this bead open: R2 live policy/JWT conformance is unproved; lifecycle is rendered but not installed; the real broker/publisher are .17.1/.17.2; staging-body verification remains publisher work; parent overwrite/delete availability is .17.9.1; shared-bucket canonical read confidentiality is .17.9.2.
Rendered grammar spelling (angle-bracket placeholders may be hidden by terminal formatting): ingress/v1/workspaces/{ws64}/sessions/{nonce32}/obj/{sha256}; sole ready marker ingress/v1/workspaces/{ws64}/sessions/{nonce32}/pile/{member16}/{sha256}. The broker mints nonce32 and paths; the client never supplies a free-form object key.
Final schema gate: R2 bucket names are validated at the documented 3..63 character bound (2/3/63/64 ratchet). The upload package now pins uv/Workers locks and  runs the credential/config corpus plus real pywrangler/Wrangler dry-runs of both generated configs. The observed broker artifact had no R2 binding; the publisher artifact had exactly INGRESS and CANONICAL. This is artifact/config evidence, still not live R2 credential-policy conformance.
Correction: the package command is python3 -m deploy.cloudflare_upload.manage test; it runs the credential/config corpus and both real pywrangler/Wrangler dry-runs.
2026-07-30 correction: exact presigned PUT URLs replace locally signed child credentials. The separate-bucket law is unchanged: the broker parent is scoped only to ingress and cannot address canonical data. A successful staging PUT is a retryable receipt; observed root publication is the durable workspace acknowledgement, leaving .17.9.1 as the explicit pre-root availability boundary.
close_reason: Separate ingress-bucket provider policy plus exact R2 presigned PUT capabilities now prevent the broker parent and returned client authority from addressing canonical data. Pre-root staging erasure remains explicitly tracked by .17.9.1.

title: Compile authenticated routes required by RepositoryApplier
description: A cold database-free RepositoryApplier must derive the same settlement as a full P2P recipient without scanning object-store LIST or consulting SQLite. Publish family-neutral candidate, offer, dependency, explicit suppression-impact/action-target, current authority-liveness, and admission-witness routes in the authenticated maps so one affected transition can discover its complete bounded closure.
design: Use the current bounded Merkle maps only. FactTree is the authenticated generic index: candidate record/residence, key, type, explicit refs, offers, suppression selectors, current authority-liveness selectors, reverse dependencies, explicit action targets, and bounded canonical-rewiring routes. FactOrder is the direct eligible key-to-fact-oid ordering projection. SuppTree carries explicit suppression state; AuthorityTree caches canonical base offer winners. Named Needs and exact admission edges receive no reverse deactivation route. The one pure repository compiler builds all rows; RepositoryApplier path-copies affected rows and no SQLite/range directory/family tree supplies authority.
acceptance_criteria: The one pure repository compiler mechanically emits bounded, family-neutral candidate, type, key, reference/dependency, offer/co-offer, reverse-edge, explicit suppression-impact/action-target, current authority-liveness, and admission-witness routes into the existing authenticated maps. A cold database-free RepositoryApplier uses only those routes plus root-reachable objects to match full settlement for canonical provider joins/rewires and dormant restoration, and to update delete/removal/suppression active/clear/fallback plus current liveness without changing historical admission standing. Opposite post-removal arrival retains admitted facts but disables current removed-principal authority. It never scans LIST, SQLite, or the whole corpus. Full P2P uses the same Applier and produces byte-identical outboxes/roots. Static ratchets reject authorization-guard routes, family-specific trees, range directories, actor-specific compilers, alternate root writers, and SQL authority.
notes: The eligible generic index, strict records, paged ranges, and direct FactOrder are implemented. Remaining work is bounded need-consumer/action routes and production RepositoryApplier incremental use. Dormant candidates are root-reachable through stable fact residences and admission-proof DAGs. Historical RangeTree/treap language is obsolete and cannot justify another write or sync path.

title: Prove collision-resistant body binding for direct R2 PUTs
description: A direct uploader is untrusted but obj and pile keys are SHA-256 addresses. Exact-key permission plus If-None-Match prevents overwrite yet does not prove that the uploaded body hashes to the granted key; a malicious member can win creation of a not-yet-present legitimate oid with different bytes and permanently wedge immutable publication. AWS presigned PutObject supports a provider-checked SHA-256 checksum. Cloudflare currently documents R2 PutObject conditionals and Content-MD5, while its presigned examples use unsigned payloads; MD5 is not an acceptable substitute for the content-address invariant.
design: First test whether an R2 S3 SigV4 presigned PUT can bind and enforce the exact SHA-256 payload digest, create-only header, and exact content length even though the compatibility table does not advertise flexible checksum fields. Inspect the actual signed-header/query set and run opt-in live positive and body/header substitution cases. If R2 enforces the collision-resistant binding, ratchet the exact presigner form and SDK versions. If not, do not issue raw R2 PUT URLs: use a narrowly isolated upload-only Worker or another provider primitive that streams with a byte ceiling, computes SHA-256, and conditionally stores only the matching key. It still receives no root/list/delete authority.
acceptance_criteria: A replayable fake and opt-in live R2 test show that changing one body byte, body length, digest/key, create-only condition, or any signed header cannot create or replace the target, while an exact request succeeds and an equal replay is safely classified. The test examines bytes at the target after every result including timeout. The chosen path has a documented hard request ceiling and cannot occupy an immutable key with nonmatching bytes. README and deployment policy distinguish raw direct PUT from the upload-verifier fallback.
notes:
The x1p.17.6 model now ratchets the provider-independent oracle: an exact-key same-length wrong body must be rejected without occupying the oid; MD5 and unsigned profiles are explicit failing controls; an applied-but-lost exact write must retry as equal. The signed body-SHA condition is deliberately symbolic and is not live R2 evidence. This bead remains open for adapter refinement and opt-in live proof.
The final abstract oracle separates provider response from privileged state observation: raw create-only replay is a generic precondition failure, while only an upload verifier may classify equal replay. Same-length byte mutation, zero-length binding-algorithm mutation, wrong-byte incumbent preservation, and MD5/unsigned planted profiles are ratcheted. Live provider proof remains open.
Provider-doc check 2026-07-29: R2 Workers API R2PutOptions accepts one supplied sha256 checksum plus onlyIf conditional, so a streaming upload-only Worker is a concrete collision-resistant verifier fallback. The S3 compatibility table still advertises PutObject conditionals and Content-MD5 but not flexible SHA-256 checksums; this is not evidence for raw presigned canonical PUT.
close_reason: Not applicable to the selected uniform isolated-ingress protocol: client R2 PUT payloads remain explicitly unsigned and untrusted, and the publisher hashes staged bytes before any conditional canonical create. Provider SHA-256 binding is optional defense in depth, not a correctness blocker.

title: Method: mutate direct-upload capabilities and notification histories
description: Reusable problem-finding method for direct bucket ingress. Generate one valid exact upload request and systematically mutate each authority-bearing dimension: provider, endpoint, operation, bucket, workspace, member, object class, key, digest, size, content type, signed headers, expiry, condition, and body. Separately generate histories that lose, duplicate, reorder, and replay notifications, responses, and retries while tracking the durable pile obligation.
design: The oracle is capability attenuation plus the publication invariant, not provider success text. A mutation must either be rejected without changing protected keys or produce the one exact authorized immutable value. Every acknowledged pile creates an F10 obligation; a notification never does. Run the same corpus against the in-memory verifier, S3 SDK/presigner, R2 S3 presigner, local wiring environments, and opt-in live providers, recording semantic gaps as concrete defect beads.
acceptance_criteria: A seeded corpus with shrinking finds intentionally planted weak policies such as unsigned conditional headers, prefix rather than exact-key grants, body/checksum substitution, workspace/member swapping, URL replay after expiry, overwrite on replay, event-as-work, and notification loss without scan recovery. CI is credential-free and deterministic; live runs are opt-in and prefix-safe. Every novel provider or implementation gap emits a replay fixture and a linked defect bead.
notes:
Credential-free design corpus implemented in tests/direct_upload_method.py with focused tests. It reuses ConformanceRun only for deterministic seeds/history and Obligation for F10 vocabulary; diagnostics explicitly call this a contract model, not provider evidence. The body-SHA condition is symbolic pending live adapter refinement. Cases cover exact capability dimensions, create/collision/outcome-unknown retry, notification faults and fair scans, broker-parent compromise, provider-neutral staging/promotion crash boundaries, budgets, first-failure prefixes, and concrete integration seams.
Adversarial re-review found and fixed additional oracle escapes: cold retries previously retained process-local root state; abstract events were mislabeled as F10 evidence; extra signed constraints were rejected; raw PUT replay assumed privileged readback; typed staged authority/closure and canonical collision/delete crashes were absent; and promotion/root/delete events were not exact-bucket/key bound. Planted negatives now catch cache-only roots, foreign workspace/member/unauthorized intents, poisoned bytes, canonical overwrite, wrong-bucket state transitions, undeclared cross-workspace promotion, and unknown operations. Broader mint-vs-wire, shrinking, and real CAS ambiguity are tracked in .17.6.3, .17.6.4, and .17.10.1.
close_reason: Credential-free seeded direct-upload method implemented and adversarially reviewed: exact attenuation, abstract retirement ordering, notification recovery, broker-parent boundaries, typed staging/promotion, crash erasure, budgets, replay traces, integration seams, and planted weak controls. Remaining runtime/provider refinements are explicit linked beads.

title: Deploy hosted Applier+Reader recipients on AWS and Cloudflare
description: Package the one RepositoryApplier and RepositoryReader as each logical hosted recipient, together with its capability-broker front door, provider-native event/queue/schedule adapters, policies, CORS, alarms, and safe removal. Separate entrypoints or identities may compartmentalize broker, apply, and read permissions, but they are one recipient over one canonical root and may not contain separate semantic or pile-to-root implementations.
design: AWS uses S3 ingress plus event/SQS/schedule Lambda drivers and one canonical S3 ObjectStore. Cloudflare uses R2 ingress plus event/Queue/scheduled Worker drivers and one canonical R2 ObjectStore. Both import the same core RepositoryApplier and RepositoryReader. Provider packages construct stores, translate events, enforce budgets, and expose routes only; core owns pile grammar, kernel judgment, tree construction, CAS reconciliation, and retirement authority.
acceptance_criteria: Done when one-command test/package/deploy/update/smoke/remove flows produce exactly hosted=RepositoryApplier+RepositoryReader on AWS and Cloudflare, with a separate Reader+signer broker compartment and no third semantic actor. Artifact closure proves the exact shared database-free Applier/Reader code, no SQL/Node/Catalog or provider semantic branch, and one root-CAS/F10 owner. Policies confine sender to create-only retained ingress, broker to pinned canonical reads plus exact signing, Reader to reads, and Applier to canonical object/CAS/internal-retirement operations but not provider policy. /readyz performs a bounded pinned-Reader read of the root-reachable workspace anchor and returns 503 for missing/corrupt required objects, not merely a shallow root parse. Live smoke sends a realistic attachment objects-first/pile-last, survives dropped events via scheduled bounded discovery, observes commit only through RepositoryReader, exercises stale/ambiguous CAS, and removes compute/queues without deleting either bucket.
notes: Replace every fail-closed or provider-local receive stub with the real shared RepositoryApplier compartment and construct every read/gate view through RepositoryReader.

title: Wake RepositoryApplier without making notification delivery authoritative
description: Connect S3 object-created notifications and R2 event notifications to the hosted recipients RepositoryApplier, add an authenticated low-latency poke, and retain a bounded scheduled pile-marker scan as the progress path. Events, pokes, queue messages, and LIST results are hints; only an exact durable pile object establishes work.
design: Filter notifications to the pile prefix and deduplicate only as an optimization. A handler may receive duplicates, stale events, reordered events, or no event. It validates the named key against the same listing/drain path, performs bounded fair work, and schedules continuation when the turn budget ends. Scheduled scans use provider pagination correctly and eventually revisit every durable pile despite insertions. No notification handler may delete or claim a pile by ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded tests drop, duplicate, delay, reorder, and replay notifications; deliver object events before pile events; lose poke responses; insert keys between list pages; throttle turns; and run concurrent scheduled and event drains. Every valid durable pile eventually enters the one RepositoryApplier under fair provider recovery, poison piles cannot wedge later work, no hint creates work absent an exact pile, and F10 rejects every unsupported deletion. Opt-in live AWS and R2 tests prove notification plus scheduled recovery wiring without a host daemon.

title: Implement the PileSender objects-first, pile-last upload path
description: The SQL-permitted PileSender authors and closes an ordinary workspace-bound pile, journals its immutable upload source, obtains exact capabilities from the recipient broker, uploads detached objects first, and uploads the exact pile marker last. It never validates on behalf of the recipient, derives repository trees, or receives root-CAS authority.
design: Keep broker HTTP and provider PUT details behind narrow transports. Reuse UploadVector, canonical object digests, staged key grammar, and the ordinary closed-pile codec. The client attempts objects first in bounded batches and requests the pile capability only after every descriptor has been issued; this is a delivery preference, not a fact-validity theorem. A missing or ambiguous detached object may leave the eventual rooted file incomplete, but cannot hold valid facts hostage. Retry exact capabilities safely, preserve the most advanced authenticated cursor across replayed responses, and start a new session after cursor loss/expiry. No provider response may authorize overwrite, LIST, DELETE, or root.
acceptance_criteria: A full P2P node with SQL and a credential-free lightweight sender both upload the same canonical source through bounded resumable sessions and produce identical staged bytes. Crashes at every issue/PUT/journal boundary resume without skipping data or broadening authority. Static tests prove PileSender cannot list ingress, read or CAS root, write canonical objects, or invoke a second pile-to-root path. Completion is observed only through the recipients RepositoryReader after RepositoryApplier commits.
notes: Completion is observed only through RepositoryReader after RepositoryApplier commits. PileSender owns local authorship/upload progress but never receive, root, or retirement authority.

title: Build the database-free RepositoryApplier
description: Implement the one database-free receiving transition from a pinned authenticated repository root plus one exact internal pile to an immutable outbox and proposed composite root. Both hosted recipients and full P2P nodes invoke this exact RepositoryApplier; it replaces every other pile-to-root compiler and imports no SQLite, Node, Catalog, daemon, PileSender, or provider package.
design: RepositoryApplier verifies the exact pile through the running kernel and family registry, joins canonical fact bytes and minimum complete admission witnesses with the root-reachable candidate archive, derives canonical standing/actions and all four authenticated maps, ensures the immutable outbox before one opaque-token root CAS, reconciles stale and ambiguous outcomes, and produces exact F10 retirement evidence. Historical named Needs/edges remain admission evidence; explicit suppression and authority-liveness rows govern current use without retroactive candidate screening. Synchronous and asynchronous drivers execute the same proposal and state-machine semantics; an adapter may cache fetched objects but cannot supply semantic answers.
acceptance_criteria: One database-free RepositoryApplier consumes a pinned root plus one exact internal pile and, through the running kernel, registered family policies, root-reachable candidate witnesses, and one pure compiler, produces the immutable outbox and proposed four-map root. Filesystem, full P2P with arbitrary or absent SQLite, fake S3, and fake R2 produce byte-identical results for genesis, append, offers/co-offers, references, deletion/removal, suppression active/clear/fallback, canonical rewires/dormant restoration, duplicates, and missing detached blobs. Opposite arrival proves a fact admitted by a removal-unaware peer remains eligible after convergence, while pinned Reader mint/authoring rejects the removed principal. It establishes every referenced object before the sole opaque-token root CAS, cannot clobber a stale winner, reconciles unknown outcomes by exact readback, and grants F10 only for applied, confirmed, or token-checked no-op exact internal generations or durable typed rejection. sqlite3, Node, Catalog, PileSender, daemon, provider policy, authorization-guard screening, and alternate root/CAS/retirement logic are absent from its semantic closure; RepositoryReader supplies all post-commit answers.
notes: Selected flow: retained typed client intent -> verify present same-session objects and exact pile marker -> create fresh internal pile generation -> pin one root plus opaque token -> join root-reachable candidate/witness archive -> run one pure four-map compiler -> establish immutable outbox -> sole root CAS/readback reconciliation -> exact F10 internal retirement. Missing detached bytes yield incomplete files but do not block facts. Provider entrypoints construct stores, normalize wakes, and schedule bounded turns only. SQL is never a semantic input.

title: Let recipient brokers issue exact conditional ingress capabilities
description: The hosted recipients broker composes RepositoryReader with a capability signer. It authorizes one PileSender against a pinned canonical root and returns exact, short-lived, create-only S3/R2 ingress PUT requests for a finite object vector and one pile marker. It is not admission authority and cannot write canonical objects or CAS root.
design: The broker is exactly RepositoryReader plus a capability signer. It pins canonical state through RepositoryReader, validates upload authority, and returns short-lived exact PUT capabilities into isolated ingress. It cannot read canonical state through a second store/view, cannot write canonical objects, and cannot CAS root. The PileSender can use only returned exact requests. RepositoryApplier independently reads/verifies present staging bytes under hard bounds, promotes them into canonical immutable state, copies the exact pile to a fresh internal generation, and alone compiles/CASes/retires.
acceptance_criteria: Done when the AWS and Cloudflare broker compartments are exactly RepositoryReader plus a provider signer, subordinate to the hosted recipient whose actor composition is RepositoryApplier plus RepositoryReader; the broker has no receiver capability. The same bounded OPEN/ISSUE/FINALIZE protocol pins one root and returns exact create-only provider requests for isolated ingress without proxying bodies. Wrong root/workspace/member/session/provider/digest/size/type/origin, replay, fork, expiry, and current family-authority changes fail closed. Policies and artifact closure prove the broker has read-only canonical access, no RepositoryApplier mutation import, no canonical write/root-CAS/F10 permission, and no SQL. RepositoryApplier later fetches and independently verifies every exact marker, copies it to a fresh internal generation, and never treats broker authorization or client PUT success as admission or retirement evidence.
notes: RepositoryReader verifies the current committed authority view; the broker signs confined ingress operations only. RepositoryApplier independently verifies staged bytes and is the sole admission/root/F10 boundary.

title: Direct uploads into database-free hosted recipients
description: Deliver closed fact piles and detached objects from a PileSender directly into isolated S3/R2 ingress, then let the receiving repository drain and commit them without SQLite. There are two actor types and three capabilities: a hosted recipient combines RepositoryApplier plus RepositoryReader; a full P2P node combines PileSender plus the exact same RepositoryApplier plus RepositoryReader and may keep SQL only for sender-local intent or presentation. The recipient builds the authenticated sync trees, owns the one root CAS, and gates access from the committed root.
design: PileSender uploads objects first and one exact pile marker last but never receives root authority. The recipient broker composes RepositoryReader with an exact capability signer; its authorization is not admission. RepositoryApplier revalidates workspace, uploader, closure, family policy, witnesses, detached objects, and the pinned root; writes immutable facts, proofs, blobs, and map pages; CASes the one composite root; and retires exact internal work only under F10. RepositoryReader answers auth, suppression, sync, type, dependency, and content questions from that same root. Events, queues, pokes, and LIST are work-discovery hints only. AWS, Cloudflare, filesystem, and full-node adapters may differ only in scheduling and ObjectStore effects.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a credential-free sender writes detached objects first and one exact pile marker last only into isolated, client-writable ingress; acknowledged ingress is retained and is never F10 authority. The database-free RepositoryApplier fetches the marker itself, copies the verified exact pile behind a fresh internal generation, reruns the kernel and registered family policies, establishes every root-reachable immutable object, performs the sole opaque-token root CAS, reconciles stale or unknown outcomes, and retires only that exact internal generation under F10. A pinned database-free RepositoryReader exposes the committed result without mutation. Hosted Applier+Reader and full-P2P Sender+Applier+Reader produce byte-identical outboxes, roots, suppression/deletion/authority answers, and incomplete-file behavior from the same root and pile. Lost, duplicate, delayed, reordered, poisoned, oversized, cross-workspace, 429, crash, concurrent-CAS, and dropped-notification histories retain or quarantine exact work safely; live S3/R2 and clean deployment tests cover both hosted recipients.
notes: Locked authority: PileSender sends and may use disposable local SQL; RepositoryApplier receives and alone mutates canonical objects/root and grants exact F10; RepositoryReader reads one pinned root without effects. Hosted recipient is A+R. Full P2P is S+A+R. Host-daemon, SQL, broker, and provider code cannot become alternate receiving mechanisms.

title: Method: re-close valid facts under a second workspace authority graph
description: Reusable cross-tenant confusion probe: create two workspaces sharing one user/device signing key, author a valid ordinary fact in W1, then replace only its surrounding closure with W2's valid membership/authority facts. Also build a pile that declares W2 but contains one W1 fact and a request whose uploader token is for W1 while the URL/path names W2. This distinguishes cryptographic fact binding from ambient-context validation.
acceptance_criteria: The probe covers every fact family, detached author evidence, suppression actions, file descriptors/chunks, invite redemption, mint request piles, sync, and direct ingress. It fails if any byte-identical ordinary fact is accepted in both workspaces or if request, uploader, pile, and fact workspace can disagree. Every exposed family gets a concrete defect bead and regression vector.
notes:
Reusable construction ratchet added: parse every facts/**/*.py Fact(...) call and fail if it omits the fifth workspace argument, passes literal None outside the unique workspace genesis family, or if the compiled registry has anything other than exactly one GENESIS family.
