This turns the audit method into a permanent family-addition tripwire rather than a one-time grep.
Completed vectors: same signing key and same fact form across W1/W2 produce distinct fact/signature ids; foreign outer pile, mixed/re-closed facts, W1 grant at W2 route, uploader/path mismatch, CF Worker/Gateway/Lambda mint, invite bootstrap, catalog stage/reindex/reopen, sync push, suppression evidence, files/chunks, and no-dual-decoder format cutover. Hostile mixed bytes are rejected before any family dispatch or Catalog.stage call. Full suite: 576 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Reusable cross-workspace re-close probe and construction ratchet implemented across all families and runtimes.

title: F10 follow-up: run obligation checker through F2 seeds and provider adapters
description: Run the one F10 obligation checker through the fixed N-RepositoryApplier seeds and S3/R2 adapter-conformance traces. Normalize provider events to acknowledged create, root CAS, exact readback, and exact delete while preserving opaque tokens and paginated discovery hints.
acceptance_criteria: Done when fixed 2-6 RepositoryApplier CI seeds and deterministic FS/S3/R2 schedules emit the same F10-checker history for direct internal piles and retained direct-upload ingress. Every internal-generation DELETE cites a committed authenticated representation, exact readback-confirmed/no-op outcome, or exact durable typed rejection; client-writable markers are never discharged by F10, including accepted-before-expiry/completes-after-expiry schedules. Stale/unknown CAS, crash, restart, duplicate, poison, and ABA histories report the first unsupported DELETE plus replay seed/provider trace. No Node/SQL oracle, provider-specific receipt, or alternate retirement implementation exists.

title: Bind every fact and closed pile to one workspace
description: Fact envelopes currently contain type, timestamp, atoms, and body hash but no workspace anchor. The daemon authenticates an uploader for ambient ws and drain(stream, ws) rejects a foreign genesis root, yet an ordinary fact authored by a key that belongs to two workspaces can be re-closed under the second workspace's member/authority chain because its fid and author signature are identical. The engine therefore cannot prove the invariant that every fact in an uploaded closed pile belongs to the request workspace.
design: Make workspace identity canonical before family dispatch. The workspace genesis fact is the sole exception: it has no ws field and its fid defines W. Every other fact carries ws=W in bytes covered by its fid and signatures. The closed-pile envelope also names W. The ingress door checks request workspace equals authenticated uploader workspace equals pile workspace and checks every ordinary fact workspace before staging. Bump the format cleanly rather than retain an ambiguous dual decoder.
acceptance_criteria: Create two workspaces sharing one signing key. Equivalent ordinary facts have different fids, a W1 fact re-closed with W2 authority is rejected, a W1 pile uploaded under W2 is rejected before staging, and a mixed-workspace pile is rejected even if every individual signature is valid. The sole workspace-genesis exception has no ws field and is accepted only when genesis.fid equals the expected anchor. The authenticated uploader/path member must be eligible in the same W. Invite redemption, sync, files, suppression actions, database-free mint, rebuild, and versioning hydration use the same rule; realistic full tests and cross-runtime vectors pass.
notes: Implemented clean workspace-bound fact/pile format. Genesis is the registry's unique ws-less fact and genesis.fid defines W; every ordinary fact and signature includes ws=W in hashed bytes; every pile carries W. Expected W is mandatory at decode across ingress, leaves, sync, mint, invite, suppression evidence, and rebuild. Layout v6 and catalog v26 force clean rebuild; prior ambient facts/piles/catalogs have no dual decoder. Added deploy vectors, hostile before-dispatch/stage tests, construction source ratchet, docs, and benchmarks. Full suite: 576 passed, 2 skipped in 140.14s.
close_reason: Workspace-bound fact/pile format, all trust paths, clean format stamps, docs, and full regression suite complete.

title: F10 defect: aliased delete reference evades production-site inventory
description: The initial production deletion inventory visited only Call(Attribute(..., attr='delete')). Refactoring to deleter = st.delete; deleter(source) leaves the destructive capability in production but silently disappears from the claimed exhaustive ratchet. Inventory every delete attribute reference, distinguish direct calls from aliases, flag dynamic getattr(..., 'delete'), and require the sole reference to remain the reviewed direct retirement call.
acceptance_criteria: An alias mutation fixture is reported as a delete capability reference even though the later call target is a Name. Production has exactly one direct delete reference in Node._retire_ingress_exact; dynamic delete getattr references are also surfaced.
notes: Fixed before handoff: production_call_sites inventories every matching Attribute reference and literal getattr, classifies direct vs alias, and its mutation fixture catches both store.delete aliasing and getattr(store, 'delete').
close_reason: Delete capability references, aliases, and literal getattr are inventoried; production remains one reviewed direct site.

title: F10 defect: forged rejection type name satisfies destructive witness
description: The first obligation checker authenticated failed/meta bytes and schema but trusted the error string's PermanentIngressRejection subclass prefix as the classification proof. A writer can forge exact/hash-bound InvalidPile metadata for a valid pile, or KernelRejected metadata for bytes whose family handler raises a program exception. Durable syntax is not a demonstrably input-local verdict. Reclassify the exact bytes deterministically through decode_pile + drain and require the recorded type to agree; program failures and valid piles must fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: Forged InvalidPile metadata over a valid pile and forged KernelRejected metadata during a family/program exception both fail at the DELETE. Real exact InvalidPile and KernelRejected production paths pass. itm.8 remains open for bounded/authenticated status presentation.
notes: Fixed before handoff: exact rejection bytes are deterministically re-run through decode_pile + drain and metadata type must agree. Valid-pile/InvalidPile and family-program-failure/KernelRejected forgeries are negative controls; real InvalidPile and KernelRejected pass. poc-16-itm.8 remains open for status presentation budgets/authentication.
close_reason: Rejection witness now requires deterministic exact-byte classification agreement; both forged semantic substitutions reject.

title: F10: bind publication proof to the root current at classification
description: The first ghost-obligation checker draft searched every historical committed root for publishable fact ids. That is unsound: an obsolete good snapshot could mask the current authoritative root being malformed or no longer representing those facts. A publication retirement witness must validate the latest applied root at or before the runtime's post-settlement classification event; historical roots are diagnostic history, not current authority.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation schedule publishes a formerly valid then malformed/excluding current root and proves the checker rejects a DELETE even though an older root contains the claimed fids. Positive winner, CAS-loser identical-root reconciliation, and lost-response reconciliation still pass.
notes: Fixed before handoff: publication proof now selects the latest applied root at each post-settlement observation, never an arbitrary historical root. A malformed-current-root mutation with an older good root is rejected.
close_reason: Current-root binding implemented with obsolete-root mutation control.

title: Method: test revocation across DAG and provider control planes
description: Reusable problem-finding method for the RepositoryReader-to-provider-controller boundary: first prove pinned DAG state no longer returns the service, then exercise its formerly valid raw provider credential, endpoint token, and grant material directly. Any surviving path is a concrete external-revocation defect even when in-band reads deny.
acceptance_criteria: The matrix covers voluntary leave, authorized removal, provider outage, lost response, cache delay, administrator interference, and fresh-identity rejoin. It reports which pinned DAG/controller/provider plane remains live and creates a concrete defect bead for each stale path. Fake AWS/R2 and opt-in live variants use the same one Reader derivation and controllers never mutate repository state.

title: Reconcile infrastructure DAG state into provider capabilities
description: Build an idempotent effect controller that reads active infrastructure bindings only through RepositoryReader and realizes isolated AWS Lambda/S3 or Cloudflare Worker/R2 capabilities. It revokes credentials, rotates grant material, and removes exact deployment bindings after leave/removal; it never becomes a repository actor.
design: Pinned DAG roots are desired state; provider APIs are effectful reconciliation with explicit observed outcomes. Use stable identities/exact ownership and reconcile ambiguous responses. A fact commit does not prove external revocation. The controller has no pile ingress, canonical object promotion, tree compiler, root CAS, or retirement authority.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded provider tests cover create/update/noop, crash/unknown response, concurrent controllers, leave/removal, credential/secret rotation, and exact teardown without data deletion. RepositoryReader pins both inputs; changed roots restart cleanly. Opt-in live tests prove old credentials fail and surviving service continues. Static tests reject RepositoryApplier/CAS/pile logic in the controller.

title: Define infrastructure offer, acceptance, binding, leave, and removal facts
description: Implement infrastructure membership as fact-family handshakes across an operations workspace and target workspace. RepositoryApplier admits them through ordinary offers/needs/suppression rules; RepositoryReader derives the active link from both pinned roots. Do not overload human/content membership or add an infrastructure state engine.
design: Reuse fact-family/device-link patterns while binding both anchors, infrastructure principal, provider class, deployment identity, logical prefix, endpoint identity, and bounded capabilities. Cross-workspace proofs remain explicit. Core sees generic refs/offers/suppression/policy; the one Applier and Reader execute the same handlers.
acceptance_criteria: Simple handlers cover admission, invitation, acceptance, wrong community/workspace/provider/deployment, replay, voluntary leave, admin removal on either side, suppression, and fresh rejoin. Full-P2P and hosted actors invoke the same RepositoryApplier/Reader and agree without a second SQL judgment. No infrastructure fact grants content author/member authority.
notes: Core kernel contexts are intentionally single-workspace. Do not model the link as an ordinary hard dependency that resolves a foreign workspace fid. Each side records a locally authorized, anchor-bound half (or a signed portable offer/acceptance receipt); the infrastructure reconciler joins the two pinned DAG projections and requires both halves live.

title: Model infrastructure nodes as in-band service members
description: Infrastructure authority is in-band DAG state, not an implicit provider role. An operations community governs infrastructure principals; a target workspace invites an exact live principal; that service accepts a workspace-scoped link. The exact shared RepositoryReader derives active bindings from pinned roots. A provider controller realizes or revokes external IAM/R2/deployment effects but cannot ingest piles, derive repository roots, create canonical objects, or CAS.
design: Separate three authorities: the operations workspace defines live service principals; each target workspace defines the exact invited scope; the provider controller realizes external effects from RepositoryReader answers. RepositoryApplier commits both communities facts through the ordinary path. Either DAG can end the link, but provider revocation is a separately observed/retried external effect.
acceptance_criteria: One RepositoryReader derivation over both pinned DAGs identifies active service bindings; AWS/R2 controllers consume that answer without a parallel database-backed judgment. Add/invite/accept/leave/remove histories work through normal RepositoryApplier facts. Every removal drives tested credential/secret/deployment revocation; stale capability probes fail afterward. Controllers cannot apply piles, derive/CAS roots, or confer content membership, and other workspaces/prefixes remain inaccessible.

title: Make shared rejection reason records retry-idempotent
description: The content-addressed rejection record included now_ms(), so its key changed for every worker and every retry. A permanently invalid pile whose exact DELETE repeatedly fails could create an unbounded failed/meta/* object stream even though payload, source, and typed reason never changed; the two-worker race only asserted that at least one record existed.
acceptance_criteria: The shared record identity is a deterministic function of exact payload id, exact source key, and typed permanent reason, with no wall clock or worker identity. Concurrent workers and repeated pre-apply delete failures produce exactly one immutable metadata object for the same rejection obligation; optional observation time stays node-local.
notes: Removed wall-clock time from durable reason identity. The two-worker barrier race now requires exactly one shared record, and repeated delete-before-apply failures remain at one record.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Do not promote arbitrary codec ValueError to permanent rejection
description: decode_pile wrapped every ValueError raised anywhere inside decoding as InvalidPile. A programming ValueError from from_json or a helper would therefore become a typed permanent verdict and justify exact pile retirement, contradicting the rule that generic exception classes are not proof of bad input. Give immutable JSON/fact shape and integrity failures their own InvalidEncoding subtype and translate only that known input-local vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed JSON, pile shape, fact shape/integrity, blob shape/integrity, recursion, encoding, and size failures remain total ValueError-compatible codec failures and typed permanent pile rejections. An injected arbitrary ValueError from a fact-decoder program path escapes unchanged and runtime retains its exact pile with no rejection evidence.
notes: Implemented InvalidEncoding at the bounded JSON and fact shape/integrity doors; decode_pile translates only explicit input-local exception types. Added a direct negative-control regression.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Bound CPU from legally fragmented S3 response bodies
description: Contiguous accumulation fixes retained-object memory, but a legal or hostile stream can still return one byte per read. At the 64 MiB host ceiling that drives roughly 64 million Python calls before completion, creating a CPU denial of service.
acceptance_criteria: S3Config imposes a validated finite read-call budget with a conservative production default and hard maximum. Bounded reads fail closed and close the body when the budget is exhausted; exact/short/N+1 behavior below the budget remains correct; a one-byte-fragment probe proves calls never exceed the configured budget.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit e200a1b is e6a1987 on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit e200a1b: contiguous reads now have a default 4,096-call budget and validated 65,536 hard maximum across S3 and R2-host configs; a 64 KiB one-byte stream fails closed after exactly 4,096 calls and closes. 128 focused tests pass.

title: Preserve family programming failures through ingress judgment
description: The generic resolve_edges() and accepts() helpers caught every family exception and returned ordinary invalidity. That erased the distinction between an immutable input-local rejection and a validator/needs programming failure, allowing runtime ingress to quarantine and retire exact input for a code bug. Add a strict streaming-judgment path that preserves unexpected exceptions for retry/status while existing projection/read callers remain fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic family needs/validator exception retains the exact pile, produces no failed/ quarantine evidence, does not publish its candidate, and does not wedge a healthy independent pile; ordinary invalid facts remain typed permanent rejections.
notes: Implemented strict exception preservation only for the streaming ingress judgment. Generic projection/read helpers retain their existing fail-closed behavior.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Preserve bounded R2 reads through the Worker read-only wrapper
description: Cloudflare ReadOnlyStore exposed get/has but hid R2BindingStore.get_bounded. Gateway therefore fell back to generic get, allowing route ceilings below the core adapter ceiling to allocate an oversized ArrayBuffer before rejection.
acceptance_criteria: ReadOnlyStore exposes only read capabilities including get_bounded, every gateway route passes its route-specific ceiling to R2, mutation methods remain unavailable, and request-level allocation-failing sentinels prove no oversized body allocation.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945 after review: strict R2 size/token validation, bounded capability preserved through ReadOnlyStore, and allocation-failing root/invite/page/batch/selective-mint probes. The focused R2/Worker/Gateway gate passes 46 tests and the integrated suite passes 496; real FFI shapes remain poc-16-x1p.5.14.

title: Avoid per-fragment object retention in bounded S3 reads
description: The bounded S3 reader retains every legal short fragment in a Python list until join. A provider/body returning one byte per read can therefore allocate millions of Python objects even though the byte ceiling is enforced.
acceptance_criteria: Bounded reads accumulate into contiguous bounded storage rather than retaining one object per fragment; ContentLength, N+1, early-EOF, exact-limit, and close semantics remain intact; a realistic one-byte-fragment body completes within the byte ceiling.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 1f9e645 is 408f72e on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 1f9e645: contiguous bounded accumulation plus a 64 KiB one-byte-fragment probe; 106 focused tests and the 496-test integrated suite pass.

title: Classify definitive ObjectStore rejection as permanent StoreError
description: F1 review found that the new adversarial harness mapped Fault.REJECTED to RetryableStoreError alongside throttling and explicitly retryable service rejection. A permission, policy, invalid-request, or configuration rejection known to occur before mutation is definitive but not necessarily retryable; collapsing it into the retry class can teach consumers to spin on permanent failure and makes the failure-taxonomy oracle unsound.
acceptance_criteria: Fault.REJECTED raises exact StoreError before any history event or mutation; THROTTLED and RETRYABLE_SERVICE raise exact RetryableStoreError; TRANSPORT on a mutation remains OutcomeUnknown; realistic tests assert exact types and unchanged data/history so subclasses cannot silently collapse categories.
close_reason: Corrected F1 fault taxonomy: permanent pre-mutation rejection is exact StoreError; throttle/service are exact RetryableStoreError; transport mutation remains OutcomeUnknown. Focused realistic gate: 76 passed.

title: Make rejection evidence immutable under shared-worker races
description: Host store_factory gives every worker the same workspace prefix, but Node describes failed/ as node-local and writes mutable failed/meta/<payload-hash> records containing timestamps. Two workers rejecting the same pile can overwrite one another's metadata while racing deletion. The exact payload is already content-addressed, so the proof surface should be deliberately shared and immutable; node-local retry/program presentation must remain separate.
acceptance_criteria: Exact rejected bytes use one shared immutable payload key; each typed-reason/source record uses a content-addressed immutable metadata key and is read back before retirement. Two independent Nodes over one shared store may reject the same pile concurrently/in either order without clobbering evidence, losing the ghost obligation, or retaining a false local-only claim. Status reads all immutable records deterministically while retryable/program attempt errors remain node-local.
notes:
Reusable probe: instantiate two Nodes with the same store_factory, barrier both after evidence persistence and before delete, and verify one idempotent retirement plus immutable records from both workers. Never infer node locality from a key prefix when the store factory itself is shared.
Implemented shared immutable evidence keys, exact readback, idempotent same-pile retirement, and concurrent real-Node coverage. Retry/program presentation remains node-local.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Protect authoritative S3 object ACL and tag metadata
description: The storage-law bucket guard denies deletion and unsafe PutObject but still permits PutObjectAcl, PutObjectTagging, and DeleteObjectTagging on authoritative root/object keys. These mutations can change access or governance metadata without changing bytes.
acceptance_criteria: The bucket guard denies authoritative ACL/tag mutation under both threat profiles, tests assert exact actions/resources/principal scope, and operator documentation requires auditing pre-existing ACLs/tags and recommends BucketOwnerEnforced ownership controls.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945; exact provider/policy negative controls pass in the 192-test focused gate and the 496-test integrated suite. Live endpoint/provider semantics remain separately tracked by poc-16-x1p.3.

title: Reject fabricated R2 version tokens from malformed FFI results
description: R2BindingStore._token str()-coerces arbitrary etag values, so None aside an integer or object becomes a fabricated CAS token. Provider results must supply an actual strong string token; malformed result types must fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: R2 read_versioned and successful CAS accept real non-empty strong string ETags, reject None, integer, object, weak, and empty values without coercion, and size remains mandatory/type checked before arrayBuffer. Workerd FFI shape validation remains tracked separately.

The focused R2/Worker/Gateway gate passes 46 tests and the integrated suite passes 496; real FFI shapes remain poc-16-x1p.5.14.

title: Exercise native R2 result shapes through real workerd FFI
description: Host Python fakes model R2Object.size as int and etag as str, while the deployed Python Worker receives JavaScript binding values through Pyodide FFI. The current workerd smoke calls only /healthz and never proves a local R2 get exposes size, etag, arrayBuffer, head, conditional put, or list page/cursor in the Python shapes the adapter validates.
acceptance_criteria: Done when local workerd seeds a real R2 binding and validates native result shapes through two explicitly separated capabilities: RepositoryReader exercises only pinned root/object read and ArrayBuffer/size/etag/error behavior, while RepositoryApplier adapter tests exercise conditional immutable create, opaque-token root CAS, and bounded list_page ingress discovery. Python-side types for null conditional results, objects, truncated, cursor, and oversized metadata are checked before allocation. The Reader artifact cannot import or receive mutation/LIST methods; compatibility normalization stays in the provider adapter and malformed host fakes fail closed.
notes:
Reusable discovery method: cross the actual language/runtime FFI boundary for every provider field before ratcheting its Python type. Pure Python lookalikes and import-only health checks do not establish binding semantics.
Host fakes now reject malformed size and non-string ETag metadata, and every Worker route has a zero-arrayBuffer oversized sentinel. Actual workerd R2 FFI result types remain unobserved, so this method bead intentionally stays open.

title: Exclude failed staged candidates from later pile settlement
description: A pile merge commits durable candidate/staged rows before root CAS. On a publication failure, _restore_authoritative_state rebuilds proofs from the root but deliberately retains staged receipts. A later independent pile can trigger a full canonical rebuild; without an explicit allowed-staged boundary, the failed pile's candidates join that settlement and can change offer winners or become published even though their own unit is still pending.
acceptance_criteria: Each pile settlement admits non-staged receipts plus only that pile's staged fact IDs; disallowed staged receipts force the filtered rebuild path and cannot supply offers, dependencies, actions, or winners. A realistic conflicting-offer test fails the first pile after merge, processes a healthy pile behind it, proves the failed candidate remains staged but ineligible, then retries it without loss. Restart and post-CAS failure paths remain correct.
notes:
Reusable probe: make two independently closed units offer the same canonical address, fail the lower-fid unit after its SQLite merge but before publication, then force a rebuild with the higher-fid unit. Assert the pending lower-fid receipt cannot leak into the later root.
Implemented allowed-staged settlement filtering and restart coverage: a failed pile remains durably staged but cannot become eligible through a later independent pile's rebuild.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Prove exact rejection evidence before ingress retirement
description: Node._quarantine_ingress writes failed/pile and metadata, then unconditionally deletes the live pile without reading either record back or reconciling an ambiguous DELETE. A fake/provider can acknowledge a wrong or missing evidence write, or apply deletion and lose the response, leaving no locally checked ghost-obligation proof. Quarantine also accepts raw=None and can manufacture metadata for bytes it never read.
acceptance_criteria: Only a typed input-local permanent rejection enters quarantine; raw bytes are required; the content-addressed rejection payload and metadata are read back byte-exact before retirement; retirement checks the exact source bytes and reconciles an ambiguous applied delete; any evidence/read/delete failure leaves either the live source or a verified exact rejection payload and never blocks a later independent pile. Real-Node and injected store-boundary tests cover wrong/missing evidence, metadata failure, delete-before/after-apply failure, and restart visibility.
notes:
This is the concrete runtime slice of poc-16-ilr and poc-16-kgp.10's ghost obligation: a destructive event must cite exact committed-root representation or exact durable typed-rejection bytes.
Implemented exact immutable payload and content-addressed typed-record readback before exact-source retirement, including ambiguous delete reconciliation and two-worker races.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Declare serialization boundary for Lambda stack creation
description: A describe-absent preflight followed by sam deploy is not one atomic CloudFormation operation. Another actor can create the same friendly name between those steps, and SAM does not expose a caller-selected create-only changeset mode through this wrapper.
design: Treat this as a trusted deployment-administrator boundary, not as a proved atomic create. Exact StackId removes the analogous update/delete target race.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation states create mode requires external serialization for a chosen name and recommends high-entropy names for automation. Tests prove known collisions fail before SAM; a future implementation evaluates direct CREATE change sets if hostile same-name concurrency must be eliminated.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Bind Lambda management to one stable deployment identity
description: The component marker is identical across every POC-16 Lambda stack, so selecting another legitimate stack by typo passes type checks. Updates and removals need a caller-supplied stable non-secret deployment identity distinct from component type.
design: Keep one component-type marker and add a separate poc16:deployment-id value. Do not infer ownership from the friendly stack name.
acceptance_criteria: Create requires a validated deployment ID stored in a stack tag plus template parameter/output. Update and remove require the exact caller ID to match both tag and output before using StackId. A negative control with two otherwise-valid POC-16 stacks proves the wrong deployment ID invokes no mutation.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.

title: F10: check destructive operations with ghost obligations
description: Turn every destructive shared-bucket operation into a history-checkable proof obligation. Assign each immutable internal pile generation a ghost obligation at acknowledged creation; a DELETE may discharge it only when a committed root authentically represents every durable Valid from those exact bytes or durable content-addressed typed permanent-rejection evidence binds those exact bytes. RepositoryApplier alone can mint the exact root/outcome receipt. Record retained client ingress, internal generation creation, immutable outbox creation, root CAS/readback, rejection evidence, bounded LIST pages, crashes, retries, and deletes.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a reusable history checker assigns a ghost obligation to each acknowledged immutable internal generation and permits RepositoryApplier F10 retirement only after an applied root, exact readback confirmation, token-checked no-op, or durable typed permanent rejection represents the Valid facts from those exact bytes. It rejects delete before root evidence, stale-generation/ABA receipts, retry-count quarantine, unknown CAS without reconciliation, rejection without exact bytes, and every attempt to retire client-writable ingress. Direct-upload traces include a request accepted before capability expiry but completing afterward: client ingress remains retained or is removed only by separately proved provider lifecycle safety, never by F10. Full-P2P, FS, S3, and R2 histories use the same checker; failures shrink to the first unsupported DELETE and a static inventory covers every non-lifecycle delete site.
notes: Follow durable exact-generation obligations, not worker ownership, retry counts, SQL catalogs, LIST, or provider PUT success. Existing deterministic traces cover winning root commit, stale/unknown CAS, typed rejection, pagination, restart, and reused keys and must run through RepositoryApplier. Completion requires the same checker in F2 and S3/R2 adapter histories under poc-16-kgp.29.

title: Handle legal short reads in bounded S3 response bodies
description: One bounded StreamingBody.read(n) call may legally return fewer bytes before EOF on a generic stream. Treating the first short read as ContentLength truncation can reject valid bodies, while retrying without a total bound risks over-allocation.
design: Track remaining budget and declared ContentLength separately; require one EOF observation when length is absent and never exceed the allocation ceiling.
acceptance_criteria: A bounded loop reads at most limit plus one bytes, accepts deterministic one-byte chunks through exact EOF, rejects true early EOF and one-byte-over bodies, closes every stream, and never calls read without an amount.

title: Preserve mint provider faults across verifier exceptions
description: The mint path can record a provider fetch failure and then return 403 from an exception branch before inspecting that record, making a provider outage look like invalid authorization and bypassing 5xx telemetry.
design: Keep authorization details opaque while separating infrastructure failure class from a deterministic denial.
acceptance_criteria: Every return and exception path after provider fetch checks the recorded provider error first. A raising verifier/consumer probe plus ordinary invalid-proof control show provider faults return 503 and invalid proofs remain 403.

title: Bind Lambda removal to the exact CloudFormation stack identity

title: Refuse Lambda deploy takeover of unrelated stacks
description: sam deploy accepts an arbitrary stack name and may update or tag an existing unrelated stack. Deployment must distinguish a caller-declared create from an update and bind updates to an already-owned stack identity.
design: Expose mutually exclusive explicit create/update CLI modes. Treat only the documented CloudFormation not-found ValidationError as absence; permission, transport, and parsing errors fail closed.

title: Clean up a unique smoke Worker after partial deploy failure
description: The live smoke marks deployed only after pywrangler returns successfully. If Cloudflare applies the upload but the CLI loses its response or exits late, the unique Worker is leaked. Once absence of the generated name is established, treat invocation as potentially applied and attempt bounded unconditional deletion in finally, while preserving the original error and reporting cleanup failure.
acceptance_criteria: Failure injection applies a fake deployment then raises before returning; smoke still invokes deletion for the exact generated name. A failure before ownership/absence preflight performs no deletion. Cleanup errors remain observable without hiding the primary error, and R2 is never mutated.
notes: Implemented in source commit c331d25: smoke establishes absence of a 128-bit random Worker name, marks upload possibly applied before Wrangler, and deletes only the exact generated config with a 60-second bound. Apply-then-error and dual-failure tests pass.

title: Reject oversized R2 objects before arrayBuffer allocation
description: The Worker config advertises a 4 MiB object ceiling, but R2BindingStore currently calls R2ObjectBody.arrayBuffer() before Gateway checks length. A valid 64 MiB core object or corrupt provider response can allocate beyond the deployment budget. Use the documented R2Object.size metadata to fail before body consumption, retain a post-read length/size check, and let the Worker translate the explicit over-limit result consistently.
acceptance_criteria: R2 store configuration has a validated read ceiling no larger than the core maximum; the Worker selects 4 MiB. A fake object above the limit has an arrayBuffer method that raises if invoked and the request is rejected without invoking it. N and N+1, missing/malformed size, short body, root, invite, single object, and batch paths are covered.

The focused R2/Worker/Gateway gate passes 46 tests and the integrated suite passes 496; real FFI shapes remain poc-16-x1p.5.14.

title: Refuse Cloudflare deploy/remove against an unowned Worker
description: manage.py accepts an arbitrary CF_WORKER_NAME and can overwrite or delete a pre-existing unrelated Worker. Give each deployment a stable non-secret ownership marker, inspect current Worker settings through the direct Cloudflare API before mutation, refuse absent/mismatched ownership except for explicit first creation, and verify ownership after deploy. Keep credentials out of generated config and logs.
acceptance_criteria: Negative controls prove deploy and remove refuse an existing Worker with missing or different ownership, malformed API responses, and ambiguous API failures. First creation is explicit, updates/removal require exact ownership, generated configs carry the non-secret marker, and a post-deploy check verifies the target. Live smoke uses a unique name and never weakens ordinary removal.
notes: Implemented in source commit c331d25: stable POC16_DEPLOYMENT_OWNER binding, bounded direct settings API preflight, exact-owner postflight, explicit first creation, and owned-only removal. This prevents accidental targeting under the documented single trusted/external-serialization boundary; the unsolved concurrent-admin TOCTOU is poc-16-x1p.5.10.

title: Make direct S3 endpoint selection immune to ambient SDK overrides
description: S3Store._sdk_clients leaves Botocore's configured-endpoint lookup enabled. Even when the host JSON rejects endpoint_url, Boto3 officially honors AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, and endpoint_url entries in the selected shared profile before falling back to the AWS service endpoint. A production host can therefore route authoritative GET/CAS/LIST through an emulator, cache, proxy, or other non-S3 endpoint by ambient process/profile configuration. R2 passes its direct account endpoint explicitly and is not displaced by these lower-precedence settings.
acceptance_criteria: Set Botocore's supported ignore_configured_endpoint_urls option explicitly for SDK-created S3 clients while retaining explicit S3Config.endpoint_url as the deliberate test/emulator escape hatch and R2's explicit account endpoint. Unit tests capture both read/mutation Botocore Config values under hostile endpoint environment/profile settings; an integration-level resolved-endpoint check rejects or proves no ambient override. Existing injected-client and explicit-endpoint tests remain green.
notes:
Found while adversarially reviewing poc-16-x1p.6. AWS's current official service-specific-endpoint documentation says Boto3 supports global/service endpoint environment variables and shared-profile endpoint_url, and that ignore_configured_endpoint_urls=true suppresses them while explicit constructor endpoint_url still wins. Reusable probe: run host selection with hostile AWS_ENDPOINT_URL/AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 plus a shared profile and inspect both clients' resolved meta.endpoint_url before any operation.
Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.

title: Define and enforce the S3 bucket-policy publisher threat profile
description: The generated deny policy applies only to one publisher principal. A second permitted writer or lifecycle administrator can bypass authoritative-key immutability, so the renderer must not claim a bucket-wide invariant without defining who may write.
design: Prefer bucket-wide explicit denies scoped to the configured object prefix when AWS condition keys allow it. If shared administration cannot be safely constrained, enforce and name a single-publisher profile and validate the complete allowed-writer set.
acceptance_criteria: The renderer explicitly selects either a bucket-wide guard or a single-publisher deployment profile. Policy tests include a second-principal negative control and lifecycle mutation. Documentation states residual trusted administrators and never overclaims what AWS policy conditions enforce.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945; exact provider/policy negative controls pass in the 192-test focused gate and the 496-test integrated suite. Live endpoint/provider semantics remain separately tracked by poc-16-x1p.3.

title: Smoke the built Lambda artifact with reproducible dependencies
description:
The package smoke uses the invoking host Python and a fresh target directory instead of importing the SAM-built Lambda artifact under the declared Python 3.13 Lambda runtime. Direct pins alone do not lock transitive wheels or hashes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build from a cache-cold checkout, execute the produced Lambda artifact in the declared runtime, and exercise pinned root/object reads plus missing, malformed, and over-budget responses.
design: Keep lock, build, and smoke boilerplate under deploy/aws_lambda. Permit a clearly reported local structural fallback only when the container runtime is unavailable; it cannot count as target-runtime evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a cache-cold reproducible build produces one declared AWS RepositoryReader artifact and smoke executes that exact artifact in Lambda Python 3.13 or equivalent SAM local runtime. Hashed dependencies, PyNaCl, root GET, immutable object GET, malformed/missing responses, and aggregate budget behavior are exercised. The artifact has no conditional-write/CAS/LIST surface, SQL/Node/Catalog, RepositoryApplier implementation, or provider settlement code; lock drift fails closed.
notes:
Source commit 542b945 replaces host-only smoke with SAM artifact execution in the Lambda Python 3.13 x86_64 image and commits a hash-locked full dependency closure. The closure installed successfully and the assembled artifact passed SDK/PyNaCl/endpoint tests on host Python 3.13 x86_64, but SAM is absent and this environment cannot access the Docker daemon, so target-image evidence remains outstanding and this bead stays open.
Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf. The exact hash-locked artifact again passed provider-free SDK capability execution on host Python 3.13 x86_64 with boto3 1.43.51/botocore 1.43.51; cfn-lint and the 551-pass integrated suite are green. SAM remains absent and Docker daemon access denied, so target-image execution is still the sole blocker.

title: Refuse removal of unowned CloudFormation stacks
description: The remove command accepts any stack name and invokes sam delete without verifying account, region, template identity, or ownership, so an operator typo can delete an unrelated stack.
design: Put an explicit deployment marker and component version in the template outputs/tags and require the marker in a read-only preflight. Provide no implicit broad-delete fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Removal first describes the exact stack and checks immutable POC-16 ownership outputs or tags plus expected account and region. Missing, ambiguous, or unrelated stacks are refused in negative-control tests and no delete subprocess is invoked. Live-smoke teardown still removes its generated owned stack.

title: Validate Lambda template inputs and gate deploy on health
description: CloudFormation accepts bucket and prefix values that S3Config rejects during cold initialization, and the normal deploy command can report success without checking the Function URL.
design: Share validation constraints mechanically where possible, cap physical key length for the longest gateway namespace, and separate liveness from provider readiness if both are exposed.
acceptance_criteria: Every CloudFormation-accepted bucket/prefix value is accepted by S3Config and known invalid or overlong examples are rejected before deployment. A normal deploy resolves the owned stack URL and runs a bounded health/readiness check; failure makes deploy fail.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.

title: Observe handled Function URL failures
description: The handler converts gateway and provider failures into HTTP 5xx responses, but the template alarms only on Lambda Errors, which does not count handled responses, and application failures have no structured log.
design: Retain an invocation budget alarm, replace the ineffective application-error alarm with Url5xxCount, and accept optional alarm action ARNs as deployment parameters.
acceptance_criteria: IaC alarms on Function URL Url5xxCount, handler failures emit bounded structured logs without secrets or request bodies, alarms expose notification configuration, and an injected provider failure proves a 503 is both returned and observable.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Fit AWS SDK deadlines inside Lambda timeout
description: S3 and Secrets Manager socket/retry defaults can outlive the 15 second Lambda timeout, causing hard termination before fail-closed response and telemetry paths run.
design: Configure separate read-only clients for a finite connect/read budget and no hidden long retry envelope. Validate the budget against the template constant in tests.
acceptance_criteria: Template timeout and every configured SDK connect/read/retry budget have a tested cleanup margin. S3 reads and Secrets Manager use explicit low bounded attempts and timeouts; injected timeout failures return or log deterministically before the Lambda deadline.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.

title: Make Lambda missing-object semantics least-privilege correct
description: The Lambda role lacks ListBucket, so S3 returns AccessDenied for absent keys and the gateway converts ordinary misses into 503 responses. Preserve the rule that arbitrary 403 is never absence while granting only the exact listing visibility needed to distinguish missing gateway keys.
design: Use bucket-level s3:ListBucket constrained by s3:prefix to the exact root, obj, and invite namespaces. Do not weaken adapter 403 classification.
acceptance_criteria: A semantic IAM/template test and an execution-role-equivalent provider probe show absent root, object, and invite keys produce the intended missing result, while a denied existing key still fails closed. The role cannot enumerate outside the configured deployment prefix.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Enforce S3 read ceilings before body allocation
description: The S3 adapter currently calls StreamingBody.read without an amount and gateway size checks run only after the provider body is fully downloaded. Oversized or corrupt objects can consume memory and time before central limits reject them.
design: Add a provider-neutral bounded reader surface or an S3-specific bounded read method used by Gateway. Keep provider SDK imports outside core and preserve the generic ObjectReader behavior at its declared absolute cap.
acceptance_criteria: ContentLength is checked before reading when present; streaming reads consume at most limit plus one byte; exact-limit bodies pass, one-byte-over bodies fail, truncated/inconsistent bodies fail, and the body is closed. Negative-control bodies fail the test if read is called unboundedly.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Adaptive batching stalls the 3 MiB black-box attachment transfer
description: After the byte-bound/adaptive-batch change on main, tests/test_blackbox.py::test_alice_bob_carol repeatedly times out waiting for Alice's 3,000,000-byte file to reach Bob and Carol. The full suite failed once after 45 seconds (391 passed, 2 skipped) and an immediate isolated rerun failed identically in 46.81 seconds, so this is reproducible rather than a one-off timeout. Text convergence succeeds before the file phase; the scenario also sends a concurrent 100,000-byte file from Bob. Investigate the separated facts-pile/blob-fetch path, batch 413 splitting, sync-cache blob state, and daemon byte ceilings.
acceptance_criteria: The isolated black-box scenario passes repeatedly with exact hashes for both 3,000,000-byte and 100,000-byte files, the transfer remains separated from the facts pile and within every request/response ceiling, an instrumented regression fails at the actual stalled seam rather than only timing out, and the full ordinary suite is green.
notes: Root cause reproduced from daemon logs and retained stores: the fact-only push changed Bob->Alice's root, but no blob moved; Alice has no outbound peer, while Carol only dials Alice. Carol's _fetch_blobs repeatedly hit HTTP 404 on a Bob-owned proof and aborted before completing Alice's proofs. Repair: every locally available referenced immutable object is hash-verified and PUT idempotently before its fact-only pile; failed object transport prevents the fact delivery, while replicas missing an object may still relay the fact for another source to satisfy. Real HTTP tests reject wrong-addressed objects and pull-only grants; the 3 MiB/100 KiB star black box passed twice. Reusable finding method split into the F9 bead: enumerate directed rather than merely connected replica graphs and schedule object availability independently from fact/root convergence.
close_reason: Objects-first, fact-only push ordering is implemented with hash-verified immutable PUTs; wrong-address/read-only/failure-before-fact tests pass, the directed star black box passed repeatedly, and the full suite is 399 passed with 2 live-provider skips.

title: Keep the Cloudflare package inside edge imports and centralized response ceilings
description: Integrating the host R2 S3 adapter made adapters.r2.__init__ eagerly import adapters.s3 whenever the direct Worker binding module was imported, pulling a host-only graph into workerd. The initial Cloudflare config also allowed an 8 MiB single object while the shared gateway's deployment response envelope is 4 MiB. Make host R2 exports lazy and derive every Worker budget from the core ceilings, with the single-object and batch responses both capped at 4 MiB.
acceptance_criteria: Importing deploy.cloudflare_worker.runtime does not import adapters.s3 or adapters.r2.s3; public from-adapters.r2 R2 S3 exports still work; staged workerd imports the direct binding; all configurable Worker budgets are no greater than core.limits and MAX_OBJECT_BYTES/MAX_BATCH_BYTES are at most 4 MiB; package, dry-run, workerd, and repository tests pass.
notes: Fixed on codex/x1p-cf-package: adapters.r2 keeps R2BindingStore eager but resolves R2S3Config/R2S3Store lazily, preserving public imports without loading host adapters in the Worker graph. Runtime ceilings are derived from core.limits; checked-in Wrangler vars are tested byte-for-byte against runtime, with both object and batch bodies capped at 4 MiB. Import, staging, dry-run, and request-level workerd tests pass.
close_reason: Edge import isolation and centralized 4 MiB response ceilings are implemented and covered by focused repository/package/build/workerd tests; the sole unrelated full-suite attachment regression is separately owned as P0 poc-16-x1p.13.

title: Choose the root CAS threat model for provider strong ETags
description: The ordinary S3/R2 deployment profile can use the providers' direct conditional-write APIs and explicitly assume their RFC 9110 strong ETags obey the provider register contract: one comparison token must not identify two different observable root byte strings. This is a provider axiom, not a mathematical injectivity proof. Decide whether POC-16 also promises correctness against a maliciously engineered ETag collision. If it does, use an independent linearizable generation register (AWS DynamoDB and a Cloudflare Durable Object are the leading constructions) because R2's unique version is not currently accepted by conditional puts. Keep content hashes, provider comparison tokens, and any generation capability separate.
acceptance_criteria: DESIGN.md names the supported threat profile. Both adapters reject missing, empty, and weak ETags and conformance tests include a deterministic token-alias negative control. If malicious validator collisions are in scope, implement and test independent generation registers for both providers; otherwise document provider strong-validator semantics as an explicit deployment axiom and keep the stronger construction as a future profile.
notes:
Found while implementing poc-16-x1p.3's token ledger and A->B->A conformance schedule. The ledger permits token reuse for byte-identical A but rejects the same token for distinct bytes and prints its seed/history. Do not conflate this with value ABA, which is safe under today's immutable closure model.
2026-07-29 provider-contract review: RFC 9110 defines a strong validator as changing whenever representation data changes; AWS documents object ETags as unique and content-change-reflecting and If-Match as comparing the current ETag; R2 exposes strongly consistent ETag conditional operations. Those statements justify an ordinary direct-provider profile, but do not prove cryptographic injectivity against an adversary. Added hostile provider responses for W/ weak validators: reads fail closed and mutation successes become OutcomeUnknown. Reusable finding method: exercise each adapter with missing, empty, weak, and deliberately aliased validator tokens; keep a token-to-bytes ledger across an A->B->A schedule so safe value ABA is allowed but token aliasing across distinct bytes is rejected.
Decision: POC-16's production profile assumes direct S3/R2 APIs honor documented RFC 9110 strong-validator semantics, rejects missing/empty/W/ ETags, and does not claim correctness against deliberately engineered validator collisions. DESIGN.md now states the axiom and the stronger DynamoDB/Durable Object generation-register profile. The deterministic alias negative control remains the executable boundary.
close_reason: The threat model is chosen and documented: ordinary direct-provider strong-ETag refinement, explicit weak-validator rejection and alias negative control; deliberate validator-collision resistance is outside this profile and has a named generation-register construction.

title: Rootless publication stamps an unverified absent base during bootstrap races
description: Publisher.publish has a no-anchor branch that calls stamp(None, received) whenever settlement.base_root is None, without rereading or conditionally verifying that root is still absent. Another publisher can create root after base() and before this stamp. The loser then records an exact-root stamp for absence it did not win; later _sync_index may repair it, but the Publisher.stamp contract and one-snapshot reasoning are already false. Represent absence as an explicit conditional version and run the same no-op/base verification before stamping a rootless settlement.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic two-publisher bootstrap schedule pauses the rootless writer after reading absence, lets another writer create a valid root, and proves the first raises RootChanged/retains intent rather than stamping None. The ordinary single-writer rootless case still stamps absence without a CAS, and restart repair remains correct.
notes: IMPLEMENTED ON MAIN (awaiting vpf/sgg dependency closure): rootless publication rechecks absence and a concurrent-bootstrap regression test fails the old behavior.
close_reason: Running Publisher rechecks absent root before rootless stamp and the deterministic two-publisher bootstrap regression passes; former vpf blocker is closed.

title: Bound R2 RepositoryApplier root hot-key contention and 429 recovery
description: Cloudflare R2 may throttle concentrated conditional writes. The R2 adapter must classify 429/retry metadata without changing CAS semantics, while the hosted RepositoryApplier retains exact work, yields under a bounded turn, and resumes with fair backoff. Throttling cannot become rejection or retirement authority.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic native-binding tests inject 429 before apply and provider-supported ambiguous outcomes at immutable create, root read/CAS, evidence write, and retirement. Exact piles remain durable; two or more cold appliers eventually converge after recovery; readers remain available on the last committed root; retry scheduling is bounded and has no SQL or alternate root writer. Opt-in live probing records safe rate behavior without asserting an undocumented quota.

title: Byte-bound batched object reads and adapt peer page splitting
description: The /page batch route limits only object count (256), not encoded bytes. A legal batch of large blobs can exceed AWS Lambda Function URL/API Gateway or Cloudflare Worker response limits and can allocate unbounded JSON/base64 memory. Define an aggregate raw and encoded response budget, reject or truncate only at object boundaries with an explicit continuation, and make Peer.objs adaptively split requests without changing order or miss positions. Tree pages remain individually capped; blob fetches should prefer direct single/ranged reads where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Tests construct 256 individually valid large objects, prove handlers never exceed the configured response/body budget, and prove Peer reconstructs the exact ordered result through adaptive batches including misses and one object near the limit. Oversized single objects fail explicitly rather than loop; Lambda and Cloudflare limits are represented by deployment-specific configuration.
notes: IMPLEMENTED ON MAIN (pending commit): daemon and shared serverless Gateway enforce exact compact-JSON/base64 aggregate response budgets as well as count, request, object, and root ceilings. Peer.objs recursively halves only on HTTP 413, preserves order/misses, and turns singleton 413 into an explicit ValueError. Exact-at-limit and one-byte-over tests cover the base64 envelope; a 256-valid-object test proves the responder stops fetching before exceeding its configured budget. The first draft exposed a separate valid-file failure: _push embedded every referenced Bao proof, making one facts pile proportional to file size and incompatible with a finite pile cap. Fixed by sending only the closed facts pile and using the existing hash-verified _fetch_blobs object path; a realistic attachment test proves separation and completion. Reusable probe: shrink only the configured byte ceiling while retaining 256 content-address-valid objects, which tests boundary logic without allocating production-sized buffers.
close_reason: Byte-bounded batch serving, exact envelope accounting, adaptive client splitting, singleton failure, and separated attachment transfer are implemented and tested.

title: Negotiate read-only peer capability for serverless authorization gateways
description: The Lambda and Cloudflare deployments are database-free authorization/read services, but core.sync assumes every authenticated peer accepts pile PUTs and can publish. When local state is ahead it pushes, so a read-only edge endpoint otherwise fails or misleadingly acknowledges work it cannot settle. Add an authenticated capability/version signal to mint or the root protocol and make sync choose pull-only behavior for a read-only peer. Unknown old peers retain today's full-peer behavior. The edge must reject unsupported mutation routes explicitly and never return a delivery receipt for unserviceable ingress.
acceptance_criteria: Black-box tests run existing Peer/sync against a read-only fake edge: behind clients pull, ahead clients do not PUT or lose intent, equal clients idle, capability tampering fails closed, and full peers retain bidirectional convergence. Lambda and Cloudflare handlers advertise the same capability bytes.
notes:
Assigned to poc16_audit on branch codex/x1p-readonly-cap from contract commit 7681d04.
Integration review found that the original daemon checked only whether a capability string was known, so a valid READ_ONLY grant could still authorize direct pile PUT if a client ignored negotiation. Fixed on main during merge: pure grant verification has require_push, daemon PUT enforces it, serverless gateway mints the canonical READ_ONLY profile, and a real HTTP regression sends a valid read-only token directly to the push door and gets 401.
close_reason: Landed a shared canonical full/read-only mint profile, HMAC-bound and sealed with the grant; Peer caches it fail-closed, sync retains pending local fact/action intent without PUTs to read-only edges, remint upgrades resume delivery, and real-HTTP coverage proves full, legacy, read-only, tampered, cold-cache, and remint behavior.

title: Add an async memoized WorkerView for awaited object stores
description: Cloudflare R2 binding calls are awaited, while core.worker.WorkerView and btreap.Reader synchronously fetch one data-dependent page at a time. Add a provider-neutral asynchronous authorization driver that reuses the one facts registry, kernel judgment, canonical codecs, and family authorize hooks rather than mirroring policy. It must perform hash/order/depth validation identical to btreap.Reader, memoize immutable objects per request, batch independent keys when possible, and enforce both aggregate byte and unique-subrequest budgets. The root is fetched and pinned once; a concurrent root update cannot alter the decision.
acceptance_criteria: Generated real-root/request fixtures yield identical decisions in synchronous and async views across valid, suppressed, removed, expired, malformed, missing/corrupt-page, and concurrent-root schedules. Tests count unique fetches and bytes, enforce configured budgets below the chosen Workers plan limits, and prove repeated tree paths hit the request cache. No async policy registry or family mirror is added.
notes:
Implemented core.mint.async_stateless as a provider-neutral awaited driver around the existing stateless/WorkerView/btreap path. A private BaseException cache-miss sentinel crosses existing Exception fail-closed boundaries; the driver memoizes bytes and missing objects per request, enforces explicit unique-fetch and aggregate-byte budgets, and never reads or repins root. Real Node snapshot tests cover differential allow/suppressed-history/removed/expired/malformed decisions, missing/corrupt pages, repeated-path memoization, budget boundaries, and a root change during an awaited fetch. Full suite: 269 passed.
Merged to main as f21e610. The shared async gateway now consumes async_stateless for both Cloudflare and Lambda, so awaited authorization has one policy path.
close_reason: Provider-neutral async_stateless uses the canonical WorkerView/policy path with per-request memoization and byte/fetch budgets; both deployments consume it and the full suite passes 399 tests.

title: Prove Cloudflare Python Worker packaging and remove POSIX imports from the read path
description: The preferred Cloudflare implementation reuses the authoritative Python facts/kernel rather than creating a second TypeScript security core, but it is not deployable until proven. core.mint -> core.worker -> core.manifest currently imports core.store, whose top-level fcntl import is unavailable in Python Workers. Split pure object-integrity/contract helpers from FsStore so the read-only graph imports no fcntl, sqlite3, or nonfunctional concurrency module. Build the actual repository modules with pywrangler, prove the selected Pyodide version supplies compatible PyNaCl, and complete an Ed25519 verification plus sealed-grant round trip in workerd. If this fails, stop and record the concrete incompatibility before choosing TypeScript/WASM.
acceptance_criteria: A pywrangler dry-run packages the actual core/ and facts/ modules without copies, imports the complete mint path in workerd, exercises PyNaCl signing verification and sealed-box round trip, and has an import-graph test forbidding POSIX/SQLite modules on the edge path. The resulting language decision and compatibility date are recorded in DESIGN.md.
notes:
Problem-finding method: a pywrangler dry-run is necessary but not sufficient. Inspect the emitted artifact for the canonical core/facts modules and forbidden host modules, then start local workerd and make a request that executes cryptography. This exposed accidental virtualenv bundling and a PyNaCl/libsodium EM_ASM load failure that dry-run alone missed. Stable Python 3.13/PyNaCl 1.5.0 and experimental Python 3.14/PyNaCl 1.6.2 were both tested; the exact-layout compatibility patch and request-context entropy path are covered by build and workerd tests. Upstream removal is tracked in poc-16-x1p.5.3.
Final evidence on branch codex/x1p-cf-package: 14 host-fake/package tests pass; Wrangler 4.115.0 clean dry-run emits 155 modules/1445.16 KiB including canonical core/mint.py, core/worker.py, core/limits.py, core/peer_capability.py, full facts, direct R2 binding, shared gateway, and patched PyNaCl while excluding POSIX/SQLite and host S3 graphs; local workerd accepts a request that completes Ed25519 sign/verify and sealed-box interoperability. Language/config decision is recorded in DESIGN.md at compatibility date 2026-07-29.
close_reason: Actual canonical Python Worker import path, PyNaCl compatibility, Ed25519/sealed-box request self-test, forbidden import ratchet, and dated design decision all pass in pywrangler/workerd.

title: Differential-test Python, Lambda, and Cloudflare authorization runtimes
description: Generate canonical provider-independent fixtures from the real RepositoryApplier and exact piles, then run them through the one RepositoryReader/family authorization path as plain Python, AWS Lambda, and Cloudflare Worker wrappers. Cover suppression, principal liveness, delegation, expiry/malformed input, corrupt/missing pages, root pinning under concurrent commit, opaque provider tokens, budgets, and sealed grants.
acceptance_criteria: Done when the pure Python, packaged Lambda, and packaged Cloudflare authorization runtimes consume identical root bytes, immutable objects, request pile, trusted time, and purpose through the exact pinned RepositoryReader and return identical allow/deny plus limits for valid, stale, malformed, corrupt, cross-workspace, suppressed/removed, and budget-edge cases. Fixtures originate from RepositoryApplier roots/outboxes, not Node/SQL state or hand-maintained JSON. Artifact closures are database-free/read-only and contain no alternate policy, compiler, root mutation, or provider-specific authorization semantics.

title: Inject remote stores without provider dependencies in core
description: Node currently hardcodes FsStore in Node.store(), so an adapter can exist yet be impossible to select. Add a provider-neutral store factory/composition seam and configuration loader outside core provider logic. Preserve FsStore as the zero-config local default. Support one bucket plus a collision-safe workspace prefix mapping, validate keys/prefixes, keep secrets out of keyring/logs, and make daemon/CLI startup select S3 or R2 without importing provider SDKs unless requested. The edge deployments construct their own read-only stores directly and do not instantiate Node or SQLite.
acceptance_criteria: Tests run two independent Nodes over one injected scripted/provider store, default local startup is unchanged, invalid provider/prefix config fails before mutation, absent optional SDKs affect only the selected provider, and CLI/daemon help exposes reproducible S3/R2 configuration. No facts/family/core policy code branches on provider names.
notes: Implemented on codex/x1p-conformance: adapters/host.py owns strict versioned S3/R2 JSON, credential-field rejection, lazy optional SDK selection, full-workspace-id namespace mapping under one bucket/base prefix, and pre-client physical-key validation against the longest current node key (pile/<16>/<64>). CLI help gives reproducible provider examples; core CLI/daemon pass only the generic store_factory seam and the zero-config FsStore path imports no provider adapter/SDK. Tests run independent Nodes over one fake bucket, rebuild/query across processes, prove exact disjoint workspace key sets, exercise the real CLI->daemon->Node path, and cover malformed/duplicate/oversize/secret/non-finite/missing-SDK cases. Audit findings recorded separately: ambient Boto endpoint redirection is P0 poc-16-x1p.1.2; random manifest geometry makes a warm-sync cost test flaky in poc-16-npz. Full suite: 399 passed, 2 skipped, with only the already-filed 3 MiB transfer stall poc-16-x1p.13 and newly filed poc-16-npz failing; focused provider/host/layout gate: 100 passed.
close_reason: Provider-neutral host selection is composed outside core policy, filesystem remains the no-config default, strict isolated S3/R2 configuration and lazy imports are covered by realistic tests, and all review blockers were resolved. Forced only because the bead's adapter prerequisites remain open for live evidence, not because host-selection work is incomplete.

title: Deploy the pinned RepositoryReader compartment within Cloudflare hosted recipients
description: Package the exact side-effect-free RepositoryReader plus family authorization hooks as the read compartment of a Cloudflare hosted recipient. It pins one root per decision and serves mint plus minimal authenticated root/object routes. It has no SQLite, ingress drain, canonical write, root CAS, LIST, or read-triggered turn. The hosted recipient separately invokes the shared RepositoryApplier from its apply compartment.
design: RepositoryReader remains the sole semantic read boundary. WorkerView and CandidateView are subordinate implementations constructed only by RepositoryReader. Because native R2 bindings carry write authority, the strict read compartment uses a provider-enforced read-only R2 S3-compatible credential or a separately fenced read service; a code wrapper alone is insufficient. One shared awaited miss/fetch driver may adapt asynchronous I/O but cannot implement policy or tree semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Done when workerd and opt-in live tests construct the exact shared database-free RepositoryReader from one pinned root plus provider-enforced read-only R2 fetches and cover allow/deny, stale/concurrent roots, malformed/corrupt/missing pages, and aggregate budgets against the full-P2P/AWS golden repository. Artifact/config closure proves zero mutation, LIST, SQL, turn, projection refresh, Node/Catalog, RepositoryApplier implementation, or provider policy in the read compartment. Identical bytes yield identical answers. It composes inside hosted=Applier+Reader (and may support a Reader+signer broker), not a separate actor; deterministic deploy/remove retains R2 data.
notes: Do not ship a generic async WorkerView as a parallel read boundary and do not treat a native read-write R2 binding wrapped in code as least privilege. The allowed async layer only fetches bytes for the exact RepositoryReader. Hosted Reader, Applier, and broker remain separate deployment compartments composing one logical recipient.

title: Deploy the pinned RepositoryReader compartment within AWS hosted recipients
description: Package the one side-effect-free RepositoryReader plus family authorization hooks as the read compartment of an AWS hosted recipient. It pins one root per decision and serves mint plus minimal authenticated root/object routes from S3. It has no SQLite, ingress drain, canonical write, root CAS, or read-triggered turn; the hosted recipient separately invokes the shared RepositoryApplier from its apply compartment.
acceptance_criteria: Done when the AWS read/gate compartment constructs the exact shared database-free RepositoryReader from one root GET plus provider-enforced read-only immutable fetches and performs only pinned auth/mint/query answers. Local events and opt-in live smoke cover allow/deny, stale/concurrent roots, malformed/corrupt/missing objects, and aggregate budgets against the same golden repository as full-P2P and Cloudflare. Artifact/IAM closure permits only required GetObject, secrets, and logs and proves zero SQL, LIST, write, CAS, turn, projection refresh, or RepositoryApplier implementation import. It is a read compartment inside hosted=Applier+Reader (and may support a Reader+signer broker), not a separate actor; clean deploy/remove preserves bucket data.
notes:
Use a stable Secrets Manager-generated HMAC key shared across cold sandboxes; never generate a module-local secret. Target Python 3.13 x86_64, pinned boto3/botocore and PyNaCl, and a SAM container build from an explicit allowlist of core/, facts/, adapters/, and handler files. Function URL is public at the AWS layer and application-authenticated, so configure reserved concurrency, request/fetch limits, logs, metrics, and cost alarms. Return explicit 405 for pile/poke/control routes in the read-only slice.
Lambda integration must pin and smoke-test a boto3/botocore version whose modeled PutObject accepts IfMatch; unit-level fake calls are insufficient evidence of the packaged SDK model.
IMPLEMENTED ON MAIN (pending commit/docs/live evidence): isolated Function URL v2 handler around the shared database-free Gateway; direct S3 reader, stable Secrets Manager grant key, read-only capability, request/root/object/batch/fetch ceilings, explicit mutation 405s, pinned boto3 1.43.51 + botocore 1.43.51 + PyNaCl 1.6.2, allowlisted staging, SAM Python 3.13 x86_64 template, read-only IAM, log retention, error/invocation alarms, reserved concurrency, deploy/remove/policy commands, and generated-stack live-smoke that mints, reads root/object, rejects an invalid proof, and attempts teardown without touching bucket data. Local event/packaging/SDK tests pass; package-smoke proves the exact PutObject IfMatch/IfNoneMatch model and sealed-box wheel. cfn-lint passes. SAM CLI/provider credentials are absent here, so no live stack was created and the bead remains open until root docs and live evidence are completed.

title: Build deterministic and live S3/R2 conformance environments
description: Provide two deliberately different test layers. CI uses the seeded adversarial in-memory contract harness plus provider fake clients to force rare and ambiguous outcomes. Opt-in live tests use dedicated S3 and R2 buckets/prefixes to verify the provider claims we actually depend on: atomic body/token reads, If-None-Match creation, one-winner If-Match replacement under concurrent independent clients, immediate direct visibility, paginated LIST, opaque token handling, and safe recovery after a deliberately dropped client response where feasible. LocalStack, moto, MinIO, Wrangler local R2, or Miniflare may test SDK/package wiring but must never be cited as evidence of AWS/Cloudflare semantics. Live cleanup is restricted to a generated test prefix and validates the prefix before deletion.
acceptance_criteria: Done when one credential-free CI command runs deterministic FS/fake-S3/fake-R2 adapter conformance and separate explicit opt-in commands run live S3/R2 with unique generated prefixes. The adapter contract covers immutable conditional create, opaque-token root CAS, exact readback, bounded list_page cursors for Applier ingress discovery, read-only fetch capabilities for RepositoryReader, collision, stale, timeout, throttling, and ambiguous outcomes. Provider adapters contain no kernel/family/settlement/compiler/F10 policy. Live tests mutate only generated test prefixes, skip cleanly without credentials, print replay seed/history, and distinguish contract, emulator, and live evidence.
notes:
Required live/fake cases discovered by provider audits: A->B->A token reuse; apply then discard the conditional PUT response; insertion between LIST pages; missing S3 object under a role without ListBucket (403 vs 404); quoted/non-content ETags; SDK conditional mutation with retries accidentally enabled; 412 vs 409 vs 429/5xx classification; R2 same-key throttling; two cold Lambda sandboxes sharing one secret; response batches immediately below/above front-door limits; and root changing while a mint decision holds its pinned bytes. Wrangler/local R2, moto, LocalStack, and MinIO prove wiring only, never provider semantics.
Provider evidence must also cover atomic same-response body/token pairing, conditional mutation SDK retry configuration, absent S3 GET under no-ListBucket IAM, stable signing secrets across cold instances, and front-door batch sizes immediately below/above limits.
S3 adapter audit contributed reusable deterministic probes: barrier-backed conditional bucket for one-winner races, broken streaming bodies, SDK retry-config capture, subprocess provider-import guard, apply-then-discard response, pagination insertion, and 403-without-ListBucket. Preserve these in the shared harness; live runs remain required for provider claims.
Implemented on codex/x1p-conformance: tests/provider_conformance.py is a seeded reusable sync/async schedule shared by FsStore, the S3 adapter, the R2 S3-host adapter, and the native R2 binding. It checks atomic version/token pairs, conditionals, immediate visibility, independent-handle one-winner replacement, bounded pagination, immutable collisions, and permitted A->B->A token reuse while a token ledger rejects aliasing across different bytes. Provider fakes preserve the reusable probes: atomic body/token mutation hook, applied-response discard, insertion between LIST pages, no-ListBucket 403, broken streaming body, quoted non-content tokens, and 409/429/5xx outcome classification. pytest markers separate ordinary/live/soak runs. Opt-in live S3/R2 tests reject endpoint overrides, require explicit flags and credentials, use only validated generated poc16-conformance/run-<128-bit> prefixes, cap cleanup, and remove current objects plus S3 versions/delete markers. Live execution was not possible in this worktree because no explicit provider opt-in/credentials were supplied; the tests skip cleanly, so the issue remains open pending live evidence. Reusable discovery method added: record every observed token->bytes association across a schedule and fail if one token aliases different bytes; this exposed poc-16-x1p.12. A second audit probe (unique cursors forever) exposed the native R2 LIST page-cap gap now recorded on poc-16-x1p.2. Commands: python3 -m pytest -q -m 'not live' tests/test_provider_conformance.py tests/test_provider_live.py; provider commands are in tests/test_provider_live.py's executable module docstring and should be copied into root README during integration.
