Define a bounded provider-neutral at-least-once delivery-queue contract, implement Google Cloud Pub/Sub as the selected deployment adapter, and create one reusable behavioral conformance suite that can be run against memory/fake and future cloud adapters. Cover publish acceptance, pull leases, ack, retry/redelivery, malformed input, identity preservation, and emulator/live wiring. Update README.md and DESIGN.md to select Pub/Sub and FCM for both Android and Apple delivery, while retaining Apple's APNs-key requirement.
design: Use Google Pub/Sub pull subscriptions as the managed at-least-once delivery queue. Queue jobs are already-resolved notification intents with deterministic delivery ids. FCM is the provider gateway for Android and Apple clients; Apple delivery still requires APNs credentials configured in Firebase. Keep cloud SDK imports behind the adapter so core tests remain dependency-light.
acceptance_criteria: A family-neutral queue contract and bounded delivery-job codec exist; a Google Pub/Sub adapter implements it without embedding subscription state; the same conformance assertions exercise the reference adapter and can exercise the official Pub/Sub emulator; live tests are explicitly opt-in and credential-safe; FCM/APNs design text is accurate; realistic hostile-input and retry tests pass; full pytest, latency gate, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented the bounded delivery-queue contract and push-job codec, Google Pub/Sub adapter, reusable memory/fake/emulator/live conformance schedule, hostile and ambiguous-outcome tests, and Pub/Sub plus FCM-for-Apple/Android documentation. Full pytest, official Pub/Sub emulator, latency, compile, and diff gates pass.

title: Keep broker canonical-read capabilities out of Worker observability
description:
The Cloudflare brokers RepositoryReader backing fetch currently uses a short-lived presigned bearer query while observability is enabled. Application redaction does not prove provider tracing or future fetch instrumentation cannot record the URL and disclose canonical read authority.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inject successful, missing, oversized, timeout, corrupt-object, and provider-error RepositoryReader fetches, capture every response/log/metric/trace field, and scan for credentials, signatures, URLs, and canonical bytes.
design: Prefer SigV4 Authorization headers behind the shared RepositoryReader adapter so bearer authority is absent from URLs. Otherwise prove/enforce that tracing, logs, exceptions, analytics, and future config cannot record outbound query strings. Do not fork Reader semantics; upload PUT URLs remain explicit client bearer capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: Done when success, missing, oversized, timeout, corrupt-object, and provider-error instrumentation around broker RepositoryReader fetches exposes no access id, signature, scope, secret, canonical object bytes, or reconstructable bearer URL. Mutation tests cannot enable query capture or pass a mutation-capable canonical binding to the broker; real workerd/provider smoke proves the exact pinned Reader still answers within budgets. Observability remains a provider adapter concern and cannot write ingress/canonical state, run RepositoryApplier, or influence authorization semantics.

title: Prove exact deterministic Cloudflare hosted-recipient artifact closure
description: Generated Cloudflare Reader, broker, and RepositoryApplier artifacts must contain only the declared transitive source closure. Whole mutable trees, stale/untracked files, and copied security-core forks are forbidden; two clean builds must be byte-identical for the same inputs.
design: Derive an exact import/asset manifest from reviewed canonical sources, reject every unexpected artifact path, build twice from independent clean inputs and compare hashes, and run a complete zero-object OPEN through the real workerd entrypoint with a controlled canonical R2 fetch seam. Preserve DB-free and family-neutral boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Done when AWS and Cloudflare broker, RepositoryApplier, and RepositoryReader artifacts consume one shared provider-neutral exact role-manifest definition, while provider assets remain segregated; explicit non-overlapping manifests equal the measured transitive import closure. Two cache-cold builds produce identical hashes; injected extra source/vendor/build files fail closure and intended changes alter the manifest. Local workerd and staged Lambda imports cover broker OPEN, retained-ingress upload, one shared Applier root CAS/F10 turn, and pinned Reader mint/read. Static closure rejects SQL/Node/Catalog, body proxying, secrets, provider-local semantics, retired mechanisms, or any actor beyond hosted=A+R plus its Reader+signer broker.

title: Isolate concurrent Cloudflare hosted-recipient builds and deploys
description:
Reader, broker, and RepositoryApplier compartment managers must not reuse package-global staging, generated config, vendored dependencies, or secret-file paths across concurrent local operations. Each invocation owns one unique validated build directory and remote target plan.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Barrier two Cloudflare build/deploy processes with different workspace/account inputs at dependency sync, render, deploy, smoke, failure cleanup, and remove, then compare all local and remote mutations.
design: Give each invocation a private temporary artifact root derived before configuration rendering, pass exact immutable paths through sync/stage/render/deploy, and retain only explicitly requested non-secret diagnostics. If a shared dependency cache remains, protect its installation with a real cross-process lock and publish it atomically.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a deterministic two-process barrier interleaves dependency sync, source staging, render, Reader+signer broker deploy, RepositoryApplier/RepositoryReader hosted deploy, smoke, failure cleanup, and remove for distinct workspace/account inputs. Each process observes only its own manifests, configs, dependencies, secrets, ingress/canonical buckets, and remote targets and cannot replace or delete the other. Both artifacts import the one shared database-free Applier/Reader core, retain exact ingress across failure, preserve opaque-token CAS safety, and contain no provider semantic fork.

title: Pin Wrangler and enforce immutable Cloudflare tool locks
description:
Both Python Worker managers pin uv/workers-py but pywrangler 1.16 invokes 'npx --yes wrangler' without a repository npm lock, so the actual deploy compiler silently changes over time. Plain 'uv run' can likewise resolve a stale Python lock instead of failing closed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the documented Cloudflare install/build from an empty cache with each lock absent or stale and with an unversioned npx target available, then record the resolved tool versions and artifact hashes.
design: Check in one exact Wrangler dependency/lock at the provider package boundary, install it deterministically, prove pywrangler resolves that local binary only, and use uv's locked mode for test/build/deploy/remove paths. Keep provider tool boilerplate out of core.
acceptance_criteria: Done when cache-cold installation uses exact committed npm and Python lock graphs, records versions/hashes, fails on stale/missing locks, never reaches an unversioned npx/package target, and deterministically builds the broker, RepositoryApplier, and RepositoryReader Worker artifacts. Tooling and lock code remain deployment-only and cannot import or fork repository semantics.

title: Make clean Cloudflare Python dependency sync reproducible
description:
A cache-cold Cloudflare Python dependency sync must reproducibly build every hosted-recipient compartment: RepositoryReader, broker, and RepositoryApplier. Interrupted sync cannot leave a false success token, and no component may depend on ambient user caches or an unpinned source build.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run dependency sync and all Cloudflare artifact builds from a cache-cold temporary checkout with no ambient packages or token, then run the command again and compare the module tree and manifests.
design: Reproduce from empty ignored .venv/.venv-workers/python_modules directories with the pinned uv/workers-py versions. Decide whether to pin a native-compatible test dependency, explicitly permit and hash-lock the native cffi build, or separate host-test and Pyodide install plans. The same helper and gate must cover deploy/cloudflare_worker and deploy/cloudflare_upload without committing vendor trees.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a cache-cold temporary copy runs one documented command that creates a nonempty lock-matching Pyodide module tree, builds the Reader+signer broker plus the exact shared RepositoryApplier and RepositoryReader hosted artifacts, and passes workerd smoke/isomorphism tests on the first attempt; a second run is byte-identical and idempotent. No unpinned source, ambient package, prior token, fail-closed semantic stub, copied compiler, SQL/Node dependency, or provider-specific receive path appears.

title: Preserve broker safety headers on provider-adapter errors
description: The shared UploadBrokerEndpoint returns body-free errors with Cache-Control: no-store and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, but the AWS Function URL adapter constructs bare Response values for malformed events, oversize bodies, and handler failures. Those pre-membrane failures therefore violate the documented common HTTP boundary.
design: Export the existing membrane error shape instead of copying its headers into each provider adapter. Keep status selection in the adapter; keep response bytes/headers in upload_broker_http.
acceptance_criteria: One public provider-neutral error constructor owns the safe body-free error shape. AWS adapter 400/413/503 paths and endpoint errors use it; realistic event tests assert identical no-store/nosniff headers and empty bodies without exposing exceptions or request authority.
close_reason: The provider-neutral membrane now exports one body-free safe error response and the AWS adapter uses it for malformed, oversize, and internal-failure paths. Event tests ratchet identical no-store/nosniff headers; focused gate remains 69 passed, 8 skipped.

title: Confine broker KMS decrypt to its exact keyring context
description: When a customer-managed KMS key is configured, the broker role currently grants kms:Decrypt on that key without a service or encryption-context condition. The function needs decryption only when Secrets Manager retrieves the one external upload keyring; unconstrained decrypt is wider than that authority.
design: Use kms:ViaService, kms:CallerAccount, and kms:EncryptionContext:SecretARN. Do not pin SecretVersionId at KMS policy level because warm old and new Lambda generations must overlap during two-phase rollout; GetSecretValue remains pinned to the environment's exact VersionId.
acceptance_criteria: Generated IAM permits KMS decrypt only via Secrets Manager in the deployment region/account and only when the SecretARN encryption context equals UploadKeyringSecretArn. Static policy tests ratchet all conditions, while the no-custom-KMS path emits no decrypt statement.
close_reason: SAM role now allows decrypt only through Secrets Manager in the stack region/account and only for the exact keyring SecretARN encryption context. It deliberately does not pin version context so old/new rollout generations can overlap. Focused provider gate remains 69 passed, 8 skipped.

title: Define provider-safe lifecycle cleanup for client-writable upload staging
description: Direct upload leaves client-writable objects and exact pile markers in isolated ingress even after RepositoryApplier copies verified intent to a fresh internal generation and commits or rejects it. Define provider-safe lifecycle cleanup that cannot race pre-expiry writes, erase acknowledged work, or masquerade as RepositoryApplier F10.
design: Keep ingress cleanup outside RepositoryApplier and F10. Terminal admitted, rejected, marker-claim, attachment-work, promoted, poisoned, and done evidence needs its own bounded retention and observable garbage-collection protocol. Establish successor work before reclaiming predecessor evidence. Determine provider lifecycle and in-flight completion bounds from official S3/R2 behavior; retention is the safe default when no proof exists.
acceptance_criteria: Done when lifecycle policy distinguishes active, acknowledged, copied-to-internal, committed, permanently rejected, expired-unacknowledged, and abandoned client ingress and removes only a class with provider-backed grace/tombstone evidence. An accepted-before-expiry/completes-after-expiry schedule, cold restart, dropped event, delayed Applier, stale/unknown CAS, replay, and broker compromise cannot erase work or recreate a retired internal generation. F10 never targets client keys; lifecycle deletion is separately named, bounded, auditable, and tested in fake/live S3/R2. Hosted and full-P2P use the same RepositoryApplier/Reader semantics, and teardown preserves both buckets.

title: Unify AWS upload deployment validation with runtime provider shapes
description: The deploy manager and SAM template accept some configuration that the runtime S3 signer rejects: in particular dotted ingress bucket names (incompatible with the checked virtual-host signer) and an empty canonical prefix (accepted by S3Config but rejected by the template). This converts local validation into late CloudFormation/readiness failure.
design: Keep general-purpose canonical S3 bucket syntax distinct from the stricter virtual-host-only ingress signer syntax. Export/reuse exact validators or constants rather than maintaining silently divergent approximations.
acceptance_criteria: One checked ingress-bucket shape and one checked non-empty canonical-prefix shape are used consistently by management validation, SAM parameters, and tests. Dotted ingress and empty/invalid prefixes fail before build/deploy mutation; accepted examples construct both runtime configs.
notes: Review also found the SAM IAM policy hard-coded a 15-minute signatureAge ceiling even when the configured presigned PUT TTL was shorter. The current fix binds that condition to PresignTtlSeconds and pins s3:ResourceAccount on all three S3 statements; tests ratchet both generated-policy properties.
close_reason: AWS broker now requires a 12-digit bucket owner in both keyring creation and deployment, pins all S3 IAM statements with s3:ResourceAccount, signs ExpectedBucketOwner, rejects dotted virtual-host ingress buckets and empty prefixes before mutation, and makes signatureAge follow the configured TTL. Focused 69-pass provider gate and full 917-pass repository gate are green.

title: Reconcile possibly-applied upload keyring secret mutations
description:
AWS Secrets Manager create-secret/put-secret-value may apply while the CLI response is lost or times out. The initial keyring command uses a stable client request token only within one invocation; without durable plan/reconciliation, retry can choose a new token, leave an unknown secret generation, and strand the exact version ID required by Lambda. The same ambiguity applies to distribute/activate/retire rotation phases.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inject timeout-before-apply, timeout-after-apply, lost response, duplicate retry, foreign same-name secret, mismatched bytes, and wrong scope at each distribute, activate, and retire transition.
design: Persist or require the proposed secret name, provider binding, canonical document digest, and client request token before the first provider call. After timeout/error, read the exact named/ARN secret metadata and bounded value, verify ownership tags plus byte equality, and classify applied/absent/foreign without printing secret material. Every rotation phase creates one immutable version, updates compute to that exact VersionId, verifies propagation, then advances; never overwrite or delete an uncertain version.
acceptance_criteria: Done when timeout-before-apply, timeout-after-apply, duplicate retry, foreign same-name secret, wrong tags/account/region, mismatched bytes, and lost response at distribute/activate/retire reconcile against exact ARN/VersionId and intended key-ring state. Equal applied state is idempotent; foreign or ambiguous state fails before broker-stack mutation. No active or overlap-required key version is removed, no secret appears in logs/stdout/argv, and the operation changes only deployment secrets—not RepositoryReader, RepositoryApplier, ingress, root, or canonical objects.

title: Choose a rate-limited front door for the public upload-broker Lambda
description: The metadata-only Function URL is application-authorized but AWS-public. Reserved concurrency and cost alarms cap blast radius after the fact, while hostile OPEN proofs can still consume Lambda, Secrets Manager/S3 reads, and kernel verification before rejection. Direct object bodies do not cross it, but authorization metadata remains a cost and availability surface.
design: Measure and select an AWS-enforced front door such as API Gateway/WAF or a tightly scoped Function URL protection that preserves the shared UploadBrokerEndpoint bytes and body-free errors. Bound request rate, burst, body size, and cost before Lambda without introducing a second authorization theorem or proxying provider PUT bodies. Keep exact CORS and client transport compatibility explicit; generated ownership/remove must include the chosen resources without touching buckets or the external key ring.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a deployable AWS front door rejects excess rate and oversized broker metadata before Lambda while preserving exact OPEN/ISSUE/FINALIZE bytes under quota. Hostile and opt-in live probes measure invocation, secret/canonical-read work, throttling, recovery, alarms, and cost without ever receiving S3 object or pile bodies. Throttling cannot delete or strand acknowledged ingress, broaden signer scope, mutate canonical state, or trigger RepositoryApplier/F10; safe teardown preserves buckets.

title: Validate every Cloudflare broker secret before the first role mutation
description: The publisher is deployed before the broker, but broker secrets were validated only inside the later broker deployment step. A missing or malformed durable upload key ring could therefore leave a half-installed publisher even though the overall deploy command failed before installing the broker.
design: Resolve and structurally validate the complete broker secret set, including the canonical upload-session key ring, before rendering or performing either provider mutation. Keep values only in the ephemeral secrets file used for the broker and never in generated configuration or logs.
acceptance_criteria: A deployment test supplies a noncanonical key ring and proves no runner/provider mutation occurs. The normal two-role deployment still installs publisher then broker, generated artifacts contain no secret bytes, and realistic boundary/key-ring tests pass.
notes:
Implementation validates the entire broker secret set and exact provider-bound canonical key ring before rendering/preflight/provider mutation. Tests prove malformed and cross-provider key rings produce zero runner calls; the normal path keeps all secret bytes out of generated artifacts.
Landed and pushed on main as f9b8b85; full repository gate: 875 passed, 12 skipped.
close_reason: Cloudflare deploy now validates all broker secrets and the exact provider-bound key ring before either role mutation; hostile tests prove zero mutation on failure.

title: Make resumable upload journals discoverable, single-writer, and collectible
description: The direct client durably retains immutable source bodies plus session.json, but a command that dies before returning leaves the upload id discoverable only by inspecting the node directory, completed sources have no explicit safe collection policy, and two concurrent resume commands can replace one another's locally advanced journal even though broker authority remains safely vector-confined. These are availability/storage/UX gaps, not canonical-state corruption.
design: Give the family command surface a bounded status/list view over locally validated source manifests, serialize or monotonically merge writers for one source so cursor_index/delivered_index/pile_delivered never move backward, and add an explicit cleanup command/policy. Cleanup may remove only a completed source or an explicitly abandoned source after its session expiry/retry window; never infer publication from a provider PUT receipt. Preserve the no-database option and keep provider credentials out of the journal.
acceptance_criteria: Done when PileSender journals immutable local upload sources and bounded resumable cursor state without acquiring recipient authority. Two concurrent resumes preserve the maximum authenticated cursor, delivered object prefix, and pile-last completion bit; killed commands are discoverable without guessed paths; active, completed, expired, and abandoned sources are distinct. Cleanup refuses active or merely acknowledged remote ingress and removes only an exact selected local source after durable completion or explicit local abandonment. Bodies stream, journal replacement is crash-safe, and no journal row can authorize canonical writes, root CAS, RepositoryApplier F10, or RepositoryReader answers.

title: Merkle-diff candidate witness joins without full FactTree scans
description: The replicated candidate join selects the minimum complete historical admission witness per fid. Replace correctness-first full candidate-range enumeration with one bounded resumable authenticated diff over FactTree records; eligibility/Four-map equality alone is never a shortcut for witness equality.
design: Give selected candidate and witness records a collision-free range in the existing bounded Merkle map and compare shared page identities recursively. Reuse the authenticated Merkle-map diff walker and candidate postings. Do not add LIST, SQL, a range directory, a treap, or a parallel tree unless measurements prove the current keyspace cannot expose a bounded diff. Exchange only differing records and their bounded witness closures, preserving eligible and dormant candidates.
acceptance_criteria: Done when full-P2P synchronization and RepositoryApplier affected-route discovery share one bounded authenticated witness-diff primitive without assigning sync or receive authority to PileSender. Two repositories with identical eligible FactOrder and one differing eligible or dormant selected witness discover exactly that record without corpus enumeration; equal roots/pages terminate within the declared shared-path bound. Boundary, disjoint, poisoned, replayed, delayed, min-join, and stale-history cases charge aggregate fetch/byte/row/work budgets across both roots, resume from authenticated continuation, and converge to the one pure-compiler root. No SQL, LIST, private full-tree read, or alternate receive path is permitted.

title: Bound authorization staleness across resumable upload sessions
description:
OPEN proves current upload authority once, while the authenticated cursor can reissue object and pile capabilities until a fixed session expiry. The cursor currently retains only the 16-hex path member, not the full principal key, so ISSUE and FINALIZE cannot ask the current authenticated SuppTree whether that principal was removed. A long resumable session therefore intentionally or accidentally extends sharing authority until expiry. This still converges eventually, but the maximum staleness law is not stated or tested.

## Decision

Define resumable authorization as a bounded grant tied to one pinned Reader observation and the cursor/session expiry; it never grants canonical or internal-generation authority.

## Rationale

A principal can be removed after a grant is issued, so the protocol needs an explicit maximum staleness law that is enforceable without SQL and does not confuse event delay with authorization lifetime.

## Alternatives Considered

Per-object online reauthorization, revoking already-issued provider requests, broker-local membership caches, and unbounded session grants are rejected unless provider evidence proves equivalent or stronger confinement.
design: Choose an explicit bearer-lease law. Either session TTL is the bounded revocation-staleness limit, or retain the full principal and recheck published liveness through pinned RepositoryReader at ISSUE and FINALIZE. Already-issued exact PUTs remain valid until their shorter expiry. Define behavior for stale/unavailable roots without SQL or a broker-specific view.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a resumable session law bounds every OPEN, ISSUE, and FINALIZE capability by exact workspace, uploader principal, provider, source digest, remaining byte/object limits, cursor state, root observation, expiry, and clock skew. Seeded tests remove the uploader immediately before and after each phase, restart cold brokers, cross expiry boundaries, and exercise already-issued requests. New authorization consults one pinned database-free RepositoryReader; no SQL or broker-local view substitutes. Already acknowledged client ingress remains retained, and no capability can address canonical objects, root, or an Applier internal generation. The criteria state the latest possible pile-marker authorization and separate bounded authorization staleness from root/event propagation.

title: Cut legacy local caches to root-derived disposable projection
description:
Old SQLite projections may contain legitimate-looking dormant facts or unchecked raw rows with no authenticated admission witness. They are not repository authority and cannot be migrated into the candidate join by inference. Cut local projection over to rebuilding solely from RepositoryReader root-reachable candidates; retain exact pending PileSender intent separately.

## Decision

Perform a clean format cut: discard unauthenticated legacy cache tables and rebuild only the disposable combined projection from a pinned RepositoryReader root.

## Rationale

SQLite is not repository authority, so inferring candidates, proofs, edges, actions, suppression, staging, or receipts from old rows would create a second admission and pile-to-root path.

## Alternatives Considered

Row-by-row authority migration, proof inference, compatibility receiver wrappers, and republishing from cache are rejected. Manual recovery must create an ordinary PileSender pile for RepositoryApplier.
design: Perform a clean local projection cut. Rebuild admitted state only from RepositoryReader root-reachable candidates. Preserve exact unsent local authoring intent behind PileSender and exact received internal piles behind RepositoryApplier. Quarantine or discard proof-less SQLite rows; never infer authority from them. A manual export must become a normal PileSender pile delivered to the exact RepositoryApplier.
acceptance_criteria: Done when one projection-format owner performs the complete destructive cut of obsolete local tables, and query modules such as suppression_state perform no schema migration. Opening any legacy full-P2P directory drops or ignores every unauthenticated cache table and rebuilds only canonical fact blobs plus the one combined generic type/dependency/reference/offer/eligibility-edge/suppression-action index from a pinned RepositoryReader root. No proof, edge, action, suppression, offer, staged, or receipt table is migrated into authority. Forged/proof-less rows never become candidates or change root; wiping or interrupting projection rebuild changes no repository answer. Exact unsent local intent stays PileSender-owned; exact received internal generations stay RepositoryApplier-owned; manual recovery uses an ordinary pile.
close_reason: Implemented the clean projection cut: catalog is the sole schema owner, all legacy authority/action tables are discarded, suppression queries own no migration, and pinned RepositoryReader refresh reconstructs only facts plus the combined generic index. Legacy/forged/wipe/restart/root-side-effect tests pass (41 focused).

title: Confine broker canonical reads when an R2 bucket is shared
description:
RepositoryReader is the brokers only canonical-read facet, but its backing R2 Object Read credential is bucket-wide and includes LIST. A configured prefix or wrapper does not provide provider isolation when multiple workspaces share a bucket.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Place two workspaces in one R2 bucket, give the broker every credential generated for one workspace, and attempt direct and Reader-mediated reads and mutations against the other workspace.
design: Either require/verify a dedicated canonical bucket per workspace or back RepositoryReader with a provider-enforced exact-workspace read service/capability. Never leave a bucket-broad parent in the broker and never create a parallel broker-specific repository reader.
acceptance_criteria: Done when compromise of every broker-held R2 credential still cannot read canonical data outside the exact workspace and cannot mutate any canonical object/root. The broker calls the same pinned database-free RepositoryReader through a provider-enforced least-privilege capability and receives only the bounded objects needed for one decision; credentials and bearer material are not observable. Generated-policy, adversarial fake, and opt-in live R2 tests prove confinement. If R2 cannot enforce it in a shared bucket, deployment fails closed and requires a dedicated workspace bucket; no application filter, SQL view, or alternate Reader counts.

title: Make the ingress-retirement obligation oracle workspace-bound
description: The workspace-anchor cutover updated production decode_pile and Fact construction but missed the independently developed F10 obligation checker/tests. tests/ingress_obligations.py calls decode_pile(raw) without the authenticated workspace, poison helpers omit workspace, and hostile Fact fixtures omit ws. As a result the full suite reports decoder program failures and leaves every valid pile obligation live, so the destructive-retirement proof tests no longer test production behavior.
design: Thread the exact trace workspace into every oracle decode and construct every hostile fact/pile under that same anchor. Preserve the intentional malformed property while making ambient-workspace mismatch impossible. Update the static delete-call line ratchet only after re-running its AST inventory.
acceptance_criteria: All F10 publication, lost-CAS, pagination, rejection, recreation, and static-delete inventory tests pass after workspace binding; at least one mutation still demonstrates that wrong-workspace bytes cannot discharge an obligation.
close_reason: Workspace-bound F10 oracle and hostile fixtures now use the exact trace workspace; retirement, poison, pagination, recreation, and static inventory tests pass in the 602-pass full suite.

title: Model root CAS conflicts and ambiguous retirement deletes in staging
description: The staging corpus now erases actor state and covers crashes after validate, promote, durable root commit, pile delete, and object delete, but it does not yet model a competing root CAS winner, an unapplied/ambiguous CAS result, or an ambiguous DELETE response.
design: Compose promotion histories with the shared-bucket CAS token model and F10 ObligationTrace. Reconcile an unknown CAS against authenticated root bytes before retirement; treat DELETE outcome as unknown until exact pile read-back; preserve idempotence under a competing publisher.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded histories cover CAS win/stale/unapplied/applied-response-lost and pile/object DELETE applied-response-lost. Only a read-back authenticated root discharges the exact pile, concurrent winners converge, and every first failure has a minimized replay.
notes:
Implemented as a refinement, not a stronger abstract event oracle: real Node/Publisher creates authenticated root bytes over AdversarialBucket opaque tokens; ObligationTrace decodes manifest and every WorkerView tree before pile discharge. Eight bounded seeded cases cover win, stale competition, definitely-unapplied CAS, applied/lost CAS with cold actor read-back, and before/after ambiguous pile/object DELETE. core.object_store.retire_exact is the shared running exact-value/read-back primitive; its create-only/body-bound address precondition is checked at Node's pile call boundary. Weak CAS-attempt and unknown-DELETE controls retain replayable first failures.
Final validation: focused direct-upload/F10/store set 97 passed; full repository 661 passed, 2 skipped. The executable broad-parent replacement race is tracked by related P0 poc-16-x1p.17.9.1 and intentionally remains a rejected negative history.
close_reason: Completed real opaque-token Publisher/ObligationTrace refinement with eight seeded CAS/DELETE histories, exact idempotent retirement primitive, realistic attachment coverage, and replayable weak controls; focused/full suites green.

title: Split broker mint authorization from provider-visible PUT authority
description: The design corpus currently presents workspace, member, object class, and digest as independent UploadRequest fields even though an S3/R2 PUT sees only endpoint, bucket, key, headers, conditions, and bytes. A combined model can accidentally claim that a provider enforced issuer-only metadata.
design: Model two refinements: a broker mint request/policy that validates workspace/member/class/digest and derives an exact key, then a provider wire PUT whose authority is only its actual signed URL, path, headers, expiry, condition, and body. Bind semantic metadata through the derived key or explicitly signed metadata values; run mutations at the correct boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove issuer swaps cannot mint a capability, wire mutations cannot exceed the minted capability, no oracle credits a provider for invisible fields, and live adapter tests inspect the actual signed request surface.
notes:
Implemented the credential-free split model in tests/direct_upload_method.py. BrokerMintRequest carries only pinned MintAuthorization plus canonical descriptor bytes; BrokerImplementation checks pinned workspace/member/evidence, active membership, descriptor commitment/canonicality, workspace/member agreement, class/digest/size/type, then derives the exact key and signed PUT values from trusted provider configuration. WirePut contains only endpoint, method, bucket, key, actual headers, credential expiry/time, and body; WirePutCapability represents only verified signed provider claims. Object issuer identity is deliberately erased at this boundary, while pile member identity is bound by the derived key. Field-inventory, seeded broker/wire mutation, planted-weak-policy, issuer-swap, replay, collision, and missing-signed-claim tests ratchet the split. The abstract-body-sha256 claim remains symbolic contract-model vocabulary, not S3/R2 evidence. Actual presigner/query/header inspection remains in x1p.3, x1p.17.1, and x1p.17.7.
Self-review found a second broker-only invariant: equality to pinned authority is insufficient before path interpolation. The model now requires workspace to satisfy core.shape.valid_fid and member to be exactly 16 lowercase hex characters, even when malformed values carry otherwise accepted model evidence and match the descriptor. Authenticated slash-bearing workspace/member cases plus weak-policy controls prove omission can escape the derived prefix.
Final local validation on codex/upload-wire-authority: focused direct-upload gate 58 passed; full repository gate 650 passed, 2 expected skips. git diff --check clean before export. Live provider evidence is intentionally not claimed by this closure and remains required on linked open beads.
close_reason: Split the design corpus into canonical broker-mint and provider-visible wire-PUT boundaries; seeded positive, mutation, replay, planted-negative, issuer-erasure, signed-surface, and path-shape tests pass. Linked open provider beads retain actual presigner/live evidence.

title: Erase process state at every direct-upload crash boundary
description: The first staging model called the retry through the same closure and retained process-local rooted state, so a cache-only publisher was indistinguishable from one that reconstructs from durable storage. This is a general false-positive mode for serverless crash tests.
design: Crash metamorphism by process-state erasure: give every suffix a fresh actor generation, retain only explicitly modeled bucket/root values, and require safety plus eventual progress from those durable values. Plant a cache-only-root candidate that must fail.
acceptance_criteria: Every crash case records distinct actor generations, root-crash retirement occurs in a later generation from a durable root commit, a cache-only root cannot justify retirement, and the failing seed/prefix replays.
notes: Implemented by promotion_history actor generations. A crash-after-root trace commits the abstract durable root in generation 1 and retires in fresh generation 2; PromotionImplementation(durable_root=False) is a planted cache-only negative that the retirement oracle rejects.
close_reason: Fresh actor generations reconstruct from durable bucket/root state; cache-only root negative is rejected and crash boundaries replay.

title: Preserve non-target constraints in capability mutations
description: A one-field negative control can be falsely reassuring when it also violates another enforced constraint. The first body-binding mutant changed body length, so an implementation that ignored SHA-256 still rejected it on size and the corpus appeared to prove a body check it had not exercised.
design: For every nominally one-dimensional authority mutation, preserve all other constraints exactly. The body-binding case flips one byte without changing length; coherent multi-field substitutions remain separate cases. Keep an intentionally weak implementation for each dimension and require the corpus to report that dimension in its first failing seeded trace.
acceptance_criteria: The unchecked-body negative control fails on a same-length key/body mismatch, the exact implementation rejects without storing bytes, the full mutation inventory remains seeded and replayable, and a test ratchets coverage of every authority dimension.
notes:
Implemented in tests/direct_upload_method.py: key-body-mismatch flips one byte while preserving length, while body-checksum-substitution remains a separate coherent multi-field case. tests/test_direct_upload_method.py plants ignored-body and exact-state negative controls and ratchets full dimension coverage plus deterministic replay.
Final ratchet also handles empty bodies without a length-changing false negative: a standalone abstract binding-algorithm mutation exercises the body check while preserving zero length. Extra signed constraints are accepted as safe tightening; missing required conditions fail. Every authority dimension has an ignored-policy negative control.
close_reason: Constraint-preserving same-length and zero-length binding mutants plus per-dimension weak-policy ratchets pass in the direct-upload corpus.

title: Method: inventory every production ingress-delete call site
description: Reusable F10 coverage ratchet: statically walk the running core AST and enumerate every ObjectStore-style delete call whose argument is an ingress source. Require all such calls to remain centralized behind Node._retire_ingress_exact, then exercise that seam through both valid committed-root discharge and typed-rejection discharge with the same ghost-obligation checker. A new direct deletion path must fail CI before it can bypass the proof obligation.
acceptance_criteria: The AST inventory reports exact file/function/line identities, fails on any new ingress-source delete outside the one reviewed retirement seam, and tests demonstrate that every current caller of that seam is covered by either committed-root or durable-rejection trace evidence. The method has no string-only whitelist that silently accepts renamed/moved calls.
notes: Implemented as an AST reference inventory, not a call-only grep: it reports direct, aliased, and literal-getattr method capabilities with file/function/line/receiver/use. Production is ratcheted to the sole direct st.delete reference in Node._retire_ingress_exact and both callers are exercised through publication/rejection proof. Alias/getattr mutation fixture proves the inventory cannot be evaded by deleter = st.delete.
close_reason: AST capability inventory and both production proof callers are ratcheted, including alias/getattr mutation controls.

title: Diagnose intermittent second-invite join HTTP 500 in daemon blackbox
description:
During the final full suite on codex/x1p-s3, tests/test_blackbox.py::test_alice_bob_carol returned HTTP 500 when Carol joined the second invite immediately after Bob joined the first (pytest temp run 3643; all three daemons were alive and logs contained no exception detail). The exact isolated test then passed in 10.49s, so this is an intermittent core/daemon failure rather than a deterministic adapter regression.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the daemon black-box join flow repeatedly with two sequential invitations, preserve the failing HTTP body/server traceback/root and pile bytes, and replay the second invite against a cold restart.
acceptance_criteria: Make the second-invite sequence reliably expose its server-side exception/response body, identify the race or transient failure, and add a deterministic regression test proving two immediate independent joins never produce an unclassified HTTP 500.

title: Deny version-specific ACL changes on authoritative S3 objects
description: The bucket guard denies s3:PutObjectAcl but AWS authorizes ACL changes to a request carrying versionId through the distinct s3:PutObjectVersionAcl action. A writer with that permission can alter read/access control for an authoritative root or object version without hitting the current deny.
acceptance_criteria: Both threat-profile policies deny s3:PutObjectVersionAcl on the exact root and obj resources; exact-action tests ratchet the versioned and unversioned ACL pair; documentation continues to state the ACL/Object Ownership boundary.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 2fce775: the authoritative metadata guard now denies s3:PutObjectVersionAcl beside s3:PutObjectAcl on the exact root/obj resources under both profiles; focused adapter/deployment gate passes (204 tests).

title: Deny ETag-preserving S3 encryption-key mutation
description: AWS UpdateObjectEncryption can change an existing object to a KMS key while preserving its ETag and checksums. A principal with s3:UpdateObjectEncryption can therefore make authoritative bytes unreadable to the gateway without invalidating the root CAS token or content identity checks.
acceptance_criteria: Both bucket-policy profiles deny s3:UpdateObjectEncryption on root and obj resources; tests ratchet the exact action/resource/principal mapping; the README identifies encryption and KMS administrators who can replace the guard as trusted.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 2fce775: the guard denies ETag-preserving s3:UpdateObjectEncryption on authoritative root/obj resources under both profiles, with exact-action tests and the KMS-admin residual boundary documented; focused gate passes (204 tests).

title: Method: validate cache validators through a standards-strict HTTP boundary
description: Handler dict-equality tests cannot reveal invalid entity-tag syntax or intermediary normalization. A reusable wire probe should cross daemon, Function URL, and workerd boundaries with an RFC-validating parser or strict proxy.
acceptance_criteria: The harness varies quoted strong tags, weak tags, whitespace, lists, duplicates, header casing, malformed validators, and 304 behavior across daemon/Lambda/Worker transports; it reports the first divergent parse and is linked to poc-16-x1p.10.2 without claiming provider CAS tokens are HTTP validators.

title: Fail host cloud-store startup on an incapable SDK
description: The new no-I/O SDK smoke is only an operator command. S3Store construction still checks Config endpoint-isolation incidentally but does not inspect the PutObject service model, so a host can start and serve reads with an old or patched botocore, then fail only on its first conditional publication. The same capability function should guard SDK-backed store construction before any provider client or workspace I/O.
acceptance_criteria: Constructing a non-injected S3/R2-S3 store invokes the provider-free capability check before client creation; a fake old service model fails startup with the missing fields named; injected test clients and provider-free imports remain unaffected.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 87ad8cb is 989ccef on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 87ad8cb: every non-injected S3/R2-S3 store runs the no-I/O Config/service-model capability check before boto3 client creation; a fake old model names missing IfMatch and records zero client calls; injected clients bypass the installed-SDK probe. 130 focused tests pass.

title: Deny unbounded S3 annotation mutation on authoritative objects
description: Current AWS docs expose PutObjectAnnotation/DeleteObjectAnnotation (up to 1,000 mutable 1 MiB sidecars per object) and ReplicateObjectAnnotation. Annotations do not alter the parent ETag or bytes, so the current bucket guard and byte/CAS tests cannot observe them. A publisher with annotation permission can attach large mutable metadata/cost to every authoritative root/object despite the declared mutation guard.
acceptance_criteria: The chosen bucket-policy threat profiles explicitly deny direct annotation put/delete on authoritative resources or document a deliberate trusted-principal exception; replication/configuration authority is classified; tests ratchet the current action names and README states the residual admin boundary.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit b53917c is a01bab0 on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit b53917c after current AWS annotation-surface audit: direct PutObjectAnnotation/DeleteObjectAnnotation are denied on root/obj under both profiles; tests assert exact actions/resources/principals; docs explicitly retain ReplicateObjectAnnotation/config administrators as a residual boundary. 112 focused tests and cfn-lint pass.

title: Authenticate and bound shared RepositoryApplier rejection evidence
description:
Shared failed/meta and failed/pile objects can authorize exact internal-pile retirement only when content-addressed, strictly typed, bounded, workspace/source-bound, and read back durably. RepositoryReader may expose bounded status but never treats untrusted metadata as authority.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Forge partial, excessive, cross-workspace, stale-generation, wrong-hash, and colliding rejection records around a retryable and a permanent pile, then race identical writers and submit later healthy work.
acceptance_criteria: Done when RepositoryApplier alone writes bounded, content-addressed, typed permanent-rejection evidence binding workspace, exact internal source/generation, pile digest/bytes, classification, and linked payload hash under create-only collision checks. Exact count/byte/fetch/schema budgets apply before mutation. Fabricated, excessive, partial, cross-workspace, stale-generation, ambiguous-write, and collision records cannot appear legitimate or authorize F10; retryable failures retain the exact generation without permanent evidence. Concurrent identical evidence converges across FS/S3/R2, later healthy piles proceed, RepositoryReader may expose evidence read-only, and neither SQL nor provider adapters decide rejection semantics.

title: Method: audit bead identity collisions across parallel worktrees
description: Reusable tracker-integrity probe: before accepting parallel worktree exports, compare each issue id's immutable creation identity (title/body/created provenance) across branches and reject one id with divergent origins. Also verify the union cardinality and all newly reported finding titles after reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: A script or test consumes two independently exported issue sets, reports divergent same-id creations with both origins, and proves a collision cannot silently replace one finding. The agent handoff checklist runs it before main export.

title: Prevent concurrent worktrees from reusing and clobbering bead IDs
description:
CONFIRMED during the provider/harness parallel run: one worktree created kgp.15 for the real-process crash-sweep method while another independently created kgp.15 for the shared-retirement diagnostic schedule. Reconciliation left only the latter, so a legitimate method issue silently disappeared and had to be recreated as kgp.23. Parallel agents must not overwrite distinct issue identities during export/merge.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From two concurrent worktrees sharing the bead backend, synchronize immediately before ID allocation, create distinct issues, and verify IDs, issue bodies, dependency edges, and audit events are not overwritten.
acceptance_criteria: Document and automate a collision-safe parallel-bead workflow (or configure globally unique allocation); a realistic two-worktree test creates distinct children concurrently, exports/reconciles them, and proves both titles/descriptions/dependencies survive. Existing duplicate-id conflicts are detected and fail loudly rather than last-writer-wins.

title: Method: sweep real process exits across publication boundaries
description: Reusable defect-finding method from F1: run actual FsStore/Node code in a subprocess and terminate with os._exit immediately before or after an immutable-object create, root replacement, and the post-CAS/pre-catalog-stamp boundary. Reopen from a separate process and check durable state instead of treating an in-process Python exception as crash evidence. Every child has a finite deadline so a deadlock becomes a bounded failure.
acceptance_criteria: Real subprocess tests bracket immutable create and root replacement, terminate after applied root CAS before the SQLite stamp, reopen independently, and prove acknowledged bytes survive and root/catalog recovery converges. The probe times out a deliberately hung child.
notes: Recreated under a fresh id after concurrent worktree exports assigned kgp.15 to two different legitimate method findings. Close only after the F1 source commit is integrated on main.
close_reason: Implemented and accepted in main source commit 1f747aa: real FsStore/Node subprocess exits cover object/root boundaries and post-CAS/pre-stamp recovery with finite child deadlines; focused 88-test root review and agent full 502-test suite passed.

title: Clear loser diagnostics after shared ingress retirement
description: When one worker wins publication and retires a shared pile, a CAS-losing peer records a node-local ingress attempt error. Future turns iterate only live pile keys, so the peer never revisits that source and the diagnostic leaks indefinitely despite the durable obligation having succeeded. Reconcile node-local attempt rows against the conforming store's strong current pile/ listing; absence clears presentation state only and performs no destructive action.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic two-Node shared-bucket race leaves a loser diagnostic immediately after the CAS conflict, the winner retires the exact shared pile, and the loser's next strong-list turn clears the phantom diagnostic without issuing a delete or losing any live-pile error. Repeated races do not grow stale local status.
notes: Implemented reconciliation at the start of every turn from the already-required strong pile/ listing; extended the real concurrent CAS winner/loser test.
close_reason: Implemented with realistic boundary, retry, restart, and shared-worker regressions; accepted in root review.

title: Method: smoke provider SDK capabilities before host deployment
description: Reusable discovery method: inspect the running botocore service model and Config surface before any bucket I/O so an old or distribution-patched SDK cannot reach deployment without conditional PutObject or endpoint-isolation support.
acceptance_criteria: A provider-free unit test plus an operator command prove PutObject IfMatch/IfNoneMatch/ChecksumSHA256 and Config.ignore_configured_endpoint_urls are present; failure names the missing capability and touches no bucket.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit e200a1b is e6a1987 on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit e200a1b: README exact optional host SDK install and S3/R2 --store-config examples; provider-free capability module checks endpoint isolation and conditional/checksum model fields without bucket I/O and is reused by Lambda. 128 focused tests pass; actual boto3/botocore 1.43.51 smoke reports ok.

title: Document the optional host provider SDK install
description: The strict --store-config host path lazily imports boto3/botocore, but README setup installs only PyNaCl and pytest and never tells an operator which optional provider SDK is required. A host deployment therefore fails at startup after configuration, while local and Cloudflare paths intentionally do not need that dependency.
acceptance_criteria: README gives an exact optional install path and host --store-config examples for S3 and R2-S3 while ordinary local and Cloudflare imports remain provider-free.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit e200a1b is e6a1987 on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit e200a1b: README exact optional host SDK install and S3/R2 --store-config examples; provider-free capability module checks endpoint isolation and conditional/checksum model fields without bucket I/O and is reused by Lambda. 128 focused tests pass; actual boto3/botocore 1.43.51 smoke reports ok.

title: Give ScriptedBucket has its own atomic gate and history event
description: F1 re-review found BucketHandle.has delegated to get, so a scheduled op='has' fault could never trigger and histories mislabeled HEAD-style existence checks as GET. This leaves one ObjectReader operation outside the before/after crash sweep and makes the advertised fault surface inaccurate.
acceptance_criteria: ScriptedBucket has records one atomic has event with its own before/after gates; replay validates the boolean against the exact state/token at that point; the F1 pre/post crash matrix covers has; transport faults scheduled for has are exact RetryableStoreError with no fabricated mutation outcome.
close_reason: has now has its own atomic gates, history event, replay rule, typed transport fault, and pre/post crash coverage.

title: Make ScriptedBucket unconditional put match the no-result store contract
description: F1 re-review found ScriptedBucket.put returned its newly assigned internal VersionToken even though FsStore, S3Store, R2S3Store, and the ObjectStore protocol expose unconditional non-authoritative put as a no-result operation. The fake-specific result could let code or tests depend on a capability unavailable from real providers.
acceptance_criteria: BucketHandle.put returns None while the history event still records the resulting token/state for replay; the shared conformance schedule asserts unconditional put returns None for FsStore, ScriptedBucket, S3, and R2 host adapters; existing history and Node tests pass.
close_reason: ScriptedBucket.put now returns None; sync and async shared conformance ratchet no-result put plus immediate visibility across implementations.

title: Keep retryable RepositoryApplier intents isolated without full rebuilds
description:
One permanently retryable internal pile must not force full candidate/proof reconstruction for every healthy pile. RepositoryApplier treats each exact generation as an independent obligation, joins only its authenticated affected closure, and never lets one intents uncommitted candidates leak into another root.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Retain one permanently retryable exact internal generation, submit a long sequence of independent healthy piles, crash/restart and race cold appliers, then compare roots, candidates, F10 evidence, and work per pile.
acceptance_criteria: Done when one permanently retryable exact internal pile cannot block a long sequence of independent healthy piles: RepositoryApplier retains each generation separately, applies later work with delta-plus-affected-route bounds, preserves correct root/F10 state, and never lets one pile publish another piles candidate. Restart and 2-6 cold-applier races over FS/fake-S3/fake-R2 preserve isolation through stale and unknown CAS outcomes and eventually retry under fair scheduling. No SQL staged table, whole-archive rebuild, client-ingress deletion, retry-count rejection, or alternate receive path is used; RepositoryReader exposes only committed roots.

title: Audit the full S3 authoritative-object mutation surface
description: A reusable policy review must enumerate operations that can alter authoritative bytes, visibility, ACLs, tags, versions, or lifecycle outcomes. Reviewing only PutObject/DeleteObject misses metadata mutations that can weaken availability or access without changing bytes.
acceptance_criteria: The policy harness maps each authoritative mutation action to an explicit deny or documented trusted-admin boundary under bucket-wide and single-publisher profiles; exact resources/principals are asserted and the audit is repeated when supported S3 actions change.
notes:
2026-07-29 re-opened: the live AWS S3 API now exposes PutObjectAnnotation/DeleteObjectAnnotation and ReplicateObjectAnnotation. The first audit enumerated ACL/tag/version/lifecycle actions but missed this newly documented mutation surface; method must ratchet against the current authoritative action inventory.
2026-07-29 final audit: current AWS permissions also split PutObjectVersionAcl from PutObjectAcl and added UpdateObjectEncryption, which preserves ETag/checksums while changing the KMS key. ReplicateObject, ReplicateDelete, ReplicateTags, ReplicateObjectAnnotation, and ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner are classified as the trusted replication-admin boundary rather than silently omitted.
close_reason: Completed the current-action-inventory ratchet in source commits a01bab0 and 2fce775: direct annotation, versioned/unversioned ACL, tag, delete, lifecycle, and ETag-preserving encryption mutations are mapped to exact denies; the five S3 replication actions are asserted/documented as the trusted replication-admin boundary. Focused gate passes (204 tests).

title: Differentially validate SAM inputs against Lambda runtime configuration
description: A reusable deployment probe should compare CloudFormation-accepted parameter domains and generated resources with the runtime adapter's validators and budgets, rather than testing a few happy-path YAML strings.
acceptance_criteria: Done when CI parses/transforms/lints the SAM template and differentially checks exact-limit and one-over bucket, prefix, deployment, KMS, alarm, timeout, IAM, output, and physical-key inputs against runtime validators. Generated authority remains read-only for the RepositoryReader compartment and separately least-privilege for the hosted RepositoryApplier deployment; no parameter can grant Reader mutation, cross-workspace access, SQL, or provider-policy authority.
notes:
Manual cfn-lint 1.53.3 passes the current transformed SAM template and runtime boundary tests pass, but transformed-template lint is not yet installed/codified in ordinary CI; keep open as the reusable method gap.
Final audit reran cfn-lint 1.53.3 successfully against deploy/aws_lambda/template.yaml and the integrated suite passed 551 tests with 2 expected live skips. Transformed-SAM differential CI remains unimplemented.

title: Probe bounded R2 reads through every Worker request route
description: Adapter-only size tests do not prove wrapper and callback layers preserve the bounded-read capability. A reusable request-boundary sentinel should fail if arrayBuffer is reached for route-specific N+1 metadata, including proof/tree fetches after a healthy mint root.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic Worker harness covers root, invite, single page, batch, and mint object-fetch paths; each returns its defined 413/503 outcome and an allocation-failing oversized R2 sentinel records zero arrayBuffer calls. Mint serves a healthy root and proves at least one oversized obj/* fetch was attempted.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commit 542b945 is 90bc5cf on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 542b945 after review: strict R2 size/token validation, bounded capability preserved through ReadOnlyStore, and allocation-failing root/invite/page/batch/selective-mint probes. The focused R2/Worker/Gateway gate passes 46 tests and the integrated suite passes 496; real FFI shapes remain poc-16-x1p.5.14.

title: Bound real-process crash probes so deadlocks fail CI
description: F1 review found that the new object-link/root-replace and post-CAS/pre-stamp subprocess probes called subprocess.run with check=False but no timeout. A durability or lock regression could therefore hang the entire test job instead of producing the bounded replay diagnostic the crash method exists to provide.
acceptance_criteria: All F1 crash subprocesses run through one helper with a finite default deadline; a realistic sleeping-child test proves expiration raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired promptly; the real crash-boundary probes still pass and report their exact exit codes.
close_reason: All F1 subprocess probes use a 10-second default deadline; a realistic sleeping child proves prompt TimeoutExpired behavior.

title: Probe fragmented response-body amplification at provider read boundaries
description: A reusable provider probe should vary legal response fragmentation independently of total bytes. Byte-limit tests using one or two chunks miss per-fragment memory/CPU amplification and accidental assumptions that read(n) fills n bytes.
acceptance_criteria: The deterministic harness drives a moderately large body as one-byte legal short reads, an exact body, early EOF, and N+1; it asserts bounded read requests, complete close behavior, correct bytes/errors, and is referenced from every streaming provider adapter that retains fragments.
notes:
The one-byte probe also exposed independent CPU amplification after contiguous accumulation removed retained-fragment memory. That concrete behavior is tracked separately as poc-16-x1p.1.11; closing this method bead does not claim the behavior fixed.
Final rebase mapping: source commit 1f9e645 is 408f72e on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 1f9e645: contiguous bounded accumulation plus a 64 KiB one-byte-fragment probe; 106 focused tests and the 496-test integrated suite pass.

title: Method: stress opaque LIST cursors across long and changing scans
description: Reusable defect-finding method from F1: force one-key and alternating short LIST pages, opaque cursors, a scan longer than 513 pages, a strict page budget, and an insertion between pages after the current cursor. Replay every page against the object-map history so pagination bugs cannot hide behind an all-at-once list fake.
acceptance_criteria: The seeded harness records and replays page input/output cursors, passes a 514-page bounded drain and a concurrent post-cursor insertion, fails at the configured page budget, and a repeated-cursor mutation is detected rather than looping.
close_reason: Implemented replayable opaque-cursor pages, short/514-page drains, strict budgets, concurrent post-cursor insertion, and repeated-cursor negative control.

title: Method: mutate a hidden SDK retry after an applied conditional
description: Reusable defect-finding method from F1/provider review: wrap one logical conditional mutation so the first provider attempt applies, its response is hidden, and an internal retry repeats the unchanged precondition and returns stale. Run the shared conformance schedule against the wrapper to prove it detects the false-stale logical result. This guards SDK retry configuration as part of the ObjectStore refinement.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic negative control applies a CAS, internally retries the same precondition, reports the retry's stale result, and is rejected by the shared seeded conformance schedule with provider/seed diagnostics. Production mutation clients remain configured for one total attempt.
close_reason: Implemented applied-then-hidden internal CAS retry mutation; the shared seeded conformance schedule rejects its false-stale result.

title: Method: ratchet ObjectStore laws with explicit nonconforming refinements
description: Reusable defect-finding method from F1: keep direct-store semantics strong and expose opt-in mutation controls for acknowledged-write invisibility, stale successful reads, accepting one CAS precondition twice, token aliasing across different bytes, destructive immutable deletion, and repeated LIST cursors. Each control must make the history/conformance oracle fail, proving the positive tests are not vacuous. Cached and lagged replica readers remain separate read-only negative adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Every named nonconforming mode has a deterministic test that demonstrates the bad observation and is rejected by replay or the shared conformance oracle; the default harness still passes strong visibility and linearizable history; lagged sync/async readers expose no mutation surface.
close_reason: Implemented explicit failing controls for invisibility, stale reads, double-CAS acceptance, token alias, object destruction, repeated cursors, lagged readers, and exact fault taxonomy.

title: F14: race shared retirement against loser diagnostic lifecycle
description: Race independent RepositoryAppliers discovering the same exact pile: one commits/retires while a stale loser records local retry status. Advance through strong paged discovery, unrelated piles, cold restart, and repeated races. LIST only discovers; each exact value is processed and diagnosed by RepositoryApplier.
acceptance_criteria: No diagnostic clears while its exact source is live; a later complete discovery clears absent-source local status without deletion; restart/quiescence agree; repeated races bound status; unrelated work proceeds. Hosted/full-P2P/fake-provider schedules share the one Applier and F10 trace.
notes:
The first concrete real-Node regression extends tests/test_shared_bucket_node.py. This bead owns general schedule generation and shrinking across adapters.
Tracker-integrity note: an earlier close interaction on this same textual id belongs to the independently created process-exit method that was clobbered during parallel worktree reconciliation. That method now lives at kgp.23; this F14 issue remains open. See poc-16-506 and poc-16-d3f.

title: F13: differential staged-candidate and failure-taxonomy probe
description: Run independently closed exact piles under a serial RepositoryApplier oracle and inject failure at decode, kernel/proof, pure compile, immutable create, root CAS/reconciliation, rejection evidence, and exact retirement. Include conflicting canonical offers so a failed lower-fid pile exposes any cross-intent leakage.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic seeds cover typed permanent versus retryable/store/program failures and every pre/post linearization phase. Only typed permanent input failures retire under exact evidence; all others retain exact work; one piles uncommitted candidates never affect another root; retry converges byte-identically. Hosted/full-P2P/S3/R2 wrappers run the same Applier and failures shrink to seam/order/conflict.
notes:
poc-16-itm.2 adds the first restart-backed two-pile regression. This bead owns the reusable cross-boundary differential matrix and shrinking rather than another one-off assertion.
poc-16-itm found and covers two taxonomy/isolation counterexamples: family exceptions swallowed into ordinary invalidity, and a failed staged receipt leaking into the next pile's forced rebuild. F13 remains open to generate and shrink these differentially against a serial intent oracle.
Additional concrete counterexample from poc-16-itm.7: monkeypatching the fact decoder to raise generic ValueError previously manufactured InvalidPile. Include exception-class mutation at each nested codec helper, not just the top-level decoder.

title: F11: inject exact-evidence retirement boundary faults
description: Generalize poc-16-itm.1's deterministic negative controls into a reusable destructive-retirement probe. Inject wrong/missing/raised/applied-but-lost outcomes at rejection payload create/read, typed metadata create/read, exact-source precheck, delete, and delete reconciliation. The oracle follows the pile hash ghost obligation rather than retry count or worker identity.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable helper runs each boundary before/after its linearization point against local and provider-fake stores, asserts that every deleted pile has byte-exact durable typed evidence, prints the first unsupported event, and is consumed by ingress tests plus the F10 history checker. Include source changed/missing and metadata collision negative controls.
notes:
The initial real-Node matrix lives in tests/test_ingress_hardening.py under poc-16-itm.1. This bead owns extracting and applying the method across every provider adapter; it complements, not duplicates, F10's history-level oracle.
poc-16-itm now supplies a concrete deterministic matrix at rejection payload write/readback, metadata write/readback, delete-before-apply, and delete-after-apply. F11 remains open to lift this matrix into the reusable adversarial provider harness and sweep every equivalent boundary.

title: F12: barrier-race shared rejection and retirement
description: Barrier two or more independent cold RepositoryAppliers after discovery, after immutable rejection evidence, and before exact DELETE; permute winner, lost delete response, already-retired observation, evidence coalescing, and concurrent unrelated piles. Run through hosted and full-P2P wrappers without independent Node/SQL receivers.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded schedules prove exact immutable evidence and one idempotent retirement under every permutation, continue unrelated work, validate F10, and emit replayable histories. Fs/fake S3/fake R2 plus hosted/full-P2P wrappers share the same RepositoryApplier and oracle.
notes:
The first deterministic two-Node barrier regression is implemented in tests/test_ingress_hardening.py. Keep this broader method separate from the concrete shared-metadata defect bead poc-16-itm.3.
poc-16-itm now supplies a concrete two-real-Node barrier race over one shared malformed pile, proving immutable content-addressed evidence and idempotent exact retirement. F12 remains open for seeded schedule generation, crashes, and shrinking across wider shared-retirement histories.
Concrete review counterexample poc-16-itm.9: wall-clock metadata produced one content-addressed object per retry/worker. F12 must assert exact record cardinality under repeated same-obligation schedules, not merely nonempty immutable evidence.

title: Use RFC-valid quoted HTTP validators for root cache tags
description:
Daemon and serverless gateways emit the SHA-256 root content tag as a bare ETag and compare If-None-Match by raw string equality. HTTP entity-tag syntax is quoted; strict intermediaries or clients may reject, quote, combine, or weak-prefix it, causing unnecessary transfers or broken conditional reads. This wire cache tag remains distinct from provider CAS tokens.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Serve root responses through each gateway, send quoted and unquoted If-None-Match values with a standards-strict client/cache, and compare 200/304 behavior plus exact ETag round trips.
acceptance_criteria: Root responses emit one quoted strong entity-tag, Peer and every gateway parse case-insensitive ETag/If-None-Match syntax rather than stripping arbitrary characters, and weak/multiple/malformed validators fail conservatively. Real HTTP black-box tests cross daemon, Lambda adapter, and workerd with a standards-strict client/proxy negative control while the logical snapshot identity remains h(root bytes).
notes: Reusable discovery method: validate protocol headers with a standards parser or strict proxy, not only dict equality in handler tests. Vary quoting, casing, weak prefixes, whitespace, duplicate/list syntax, and 304 behavior.

title: Make ScriptedBucket an exact opaque-token ObjectStore refinement
description: The F1 cross-implementation conformance lift found that ScriptedBucket derived its purported opaque CAS token from the value hash, implemented read_versioned as a get followed by token reconstruction instead of one atomic pair read, and rejected legal non-root conditional-create probe keys. Those shortcuts prevent the shared harness from detecting torn value/token reads and from running the same conformance schedule as FsStore and provider adapters. Refactor the existing deterministic history store to assign seeded opaque value-ABA tokens, read bytes/token under one lock and one history event, replay the token-to-bytes law, and accept the provider-neutral conditional-create surface while retaining authoritative-key guards.
acceptance_criteria: The shared conformance schedule passes against ScriptedBucket; a versioned read is one atomic history event; tokens are not content hashes and may safely repeat only for the same bytes; history replay rejects token aliasing across distinct bytes; existing deterministic Node schedules remain green.
close_reason: ScriptedBucket now assigns seeded opaque value-ABA tokens, atomically pairs bytes/token in one read_versioned event, accepts the provider-neutral conditional-create surface, and passes shared conformance.

title: Choose a rate-limited front door for the public Cloudflare Worker
description:
Application grants protect workspace data, but the public Worker route still permits unauthenticated invocation, CPU/subrequest consumption, plausible-mint R2 reads, and availability or spend exhaustion. Body/query/fetch ceilings bound one request; they do not rate-limit a caller or preserve capacity for legitimate peers.

## Decision

Select and deploy one Cloudflare front-door mechanism only after its exact rate, request-size, peer-compatibility, teardown, and account-control properties satisfy this beads acceptance criteria.

## Rationale

Worker CPU and R2 subrequests occur before application rejection, so provider-enforced abuse bounds are required without moving protocol policy out of RepositoryReader or creating another actor.

## Alternatives Considered

Evaluate rate-limit rules, WAF/custom rules, service bindings, Access, and dedicated fronting services; reject application-only counters and any choice that breaks ordinary peer grants or strands ingress.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a deployable Cloudflare rate-limit/WAF/service-binding/Access or equivalent rule preserves legitimate pinned RepositoryReader and broker grants while limiting hostile Worker CPU, R2 subrequests, platform throttling, and cost at exact request ceilings. Seeded and opt-in live probes show recovery without deleting or stranding ingress. Provider-only policy remains outside core and cannot authorize facts, mutate canonical state, invoke RepositoryApplier/F10, or alter the exact hosted=RepositoryApplier+RepositoryReader and full-P2P=PileSender+RepositoryApplier+RepositoryReader actor compositions.
notes: Reusable method: distinguish per-request complexity ceilings from cross-request admission. Replay a valid-looking mint corpus at increasing concurrency and account separately for Worker invocations, R2 reads, denied requests, and legitimate tail latency.

title: Choose a rate-limited front door for the public Lambda Function URL
description:
Application grants protect data but Function URL AuthType NONE permits unauthenticated invocation, concurrency exhaustion, plausible-mint Secrets Manager and S3 reads, and spend. Reserved concurrency and alarms bound or observe blast radius but do not rate-limit callers or preserve legitimate availability.

## Decision

Select and deploy one AWS front-door mechanism only after its exact rate, request-size, peer-compatibility, teardown, and cost properties satisfy this beads acceptance criteria.

## Rationale

Lambda, secret, and S3 read work can occur before application rejection, so a provider-enforced bound is needed without changing RepositoryReader semantics or creating another actor.

## Alternatives Considered

Evaluate AWS_IAM, CloudFront plus WAF, API Gateway, and equivalent controls; reject application-only counters and any option that cannot preserve exact application grants and safe recovery.
design: Keep this separate from data authorization. Do not claim alarms or reserved concurrency are preventive rate limiting.
acceptance_criteria: Done when a selected AWS_IAM/CloudFront+WAF/API Gateway or equivalent front door is deployable, preserves application grants and pinned RepositoryReader request bytes, and rate-limits hostile traffic before expensive Lambda/secret/S3 reads. Seeded and opt-in live probes measure invocation, reads, throttling, concurrency, cost, and recovery without mutating canonical state or ingress. The front door is provider policy only and cannot authorize facts, run RepositoryApplier, change root, or alter the exact hosted=RepositoryApplier+RepositoryReader and full-P2P=PileSender+RepositoryApplier+RepositoryReader actor compositions.

title: Strictly reject malformed Function URL query encoding
description: urllib parse_qs accepts malformed percent escapes and replacement-decoded invalid UTF-8 while the Cloudflare edge parser is strict, creating cross-runtime request-boundary drift.
design: Validate percent triplets on raw ASCII, then parse with strict UTF-8 errors and bounded field count.
acceptance_criteria: Before gateway I/O, Lambda rejects lone or short percent escapes, non-hex escapes, and percent-decoded invalid UTF-8. Tests cover %, %2, %GG, and %FF plus one valid UTF-8 encoding while retaining byte and field ceilings.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
close_reason: Implemented in source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645; 192 focused provider/deployment tests, cfn-lint 1.53.3, and the integrated 496-test suite pass. Target-image/live-provider evidence remains explicitly tracked by poc-16-x1p.4.7 and poc-16-x1p.10.1.

title: Bound attacker-controlled Lambda failure telemetry fields
description: Structured failure logging includes the raw Function URL method and path even though the record claims a bounded fixed shape. A public caller can force oversized log events and cost amplification without leaking a body or token.
design: Prefer short route classes plus bounded ASCII method/path fragments; do not log headers, query strings, exception messages, or request bodies.
acceptance_criteria: Every attacker-controlled field is classified or truncated to an explicit byte-safe ceiling. Exact-limit and one-over method/path tests prove the serialized record stays bounded and query, token, body, and workspace data never appear.
notes: Final rebase mapping: source commits 542b945 and 1f9e645 are 90bc5cf and 408f72e, respectively, on codex/x1p-s3.
