title: Restore authoritative projections before failed turns escape
description: A turn that fails after merge() dirties the derived index but before manifest publication currently returns control to the live daemon with uncommitted-to-root facts/globals still observable. This can change mint authorization until another turn or restart rebuilds. Repair the derived index and app projection from the authoritative root on the failure path before releasing the workspace lock, while retaining ingress for retry.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection before manifest CAS proves the manifest remains authoritative, an uncommitted membership/removal cannot affect mint evaluation after the failed call returns, the ingress pile remains, and a same-process retry admits the change exactly once.
close_reason: Failed-turn regression now faults the real manifest CAS during a signed removal and proves the old root still authorizes mint, global/app changes remain absent, transactions close, ingress stays retained, and same-process retry publishes once; full 88-test suite passes.

title: Recover index-ahead state after a pre-CAS crash
description: merge() commits new facts into the derived index before commit() publishes the manifest. If execution fails in that window, the old index generation stamp still appears current; retry sees no new ids, skips projection, publishes the fact, and stamps an incomplete app model. Mark the index generation dirty transactionally with index mutation and rebuild from the authoritative root before retry.
acceptance_criteria: A realistic fault immediately after merge and before manifest commit leaves the pile recoverable; restart/retry rebuilds the dirty index from the old root, then admits and projects the fact exactly once; index and app generation stamps match the resulting root; full suite and benchmark guards pass.
close_reason: Index root stamps are invalidated transactionally with merge/rebuild mutations and restored only after manifest publication; pre-CAS restart/replay regression, 84-test suite, and all 5k guards pass.

title: Make device projection replay and crash idempotent
description: The changed-fid roster optimization still materializes replayed device claims before filtering reconciliation. A stale lower-fid/rank-losing claim can overwrite the canonical projection, and a crash after root/index commit but before app materialization leaves the same inconsistency on retry. Make the read model generation-aware or otherwise ensure replays are canonical/no-op.
acceptance_criteria: A stale losing device claim cannot replace the canonical roster row; retry after commit-before-materialize repairs the app projection; ordinary device-authored writes still avoid a full roster rebuild; realistic regression tests cover both failure modes.
close_reason: App projections now carry a manifest-generation stamp, lagging projections rebuild before replay, and aligned replays materialize only new ids; crash and stale-loser regressions pass.

title: Make FsStore concurrent puts atomic
description: The chained-auth black-box suite exposed concurrent PUTs to the same FsStore key sharing p+'.tmp'. One thread renames that pathname and the other raises FileNotFoundError, returning HTTP 500. Use per-write unique temp files while preserving atomic os.replace and clean abandoned temps.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic concurrent-put regression makes both writers complete without error, leaves one complete value at the key, and leaves no temp files; the full suite passes.
close_reason: FsStore now uses unique same-directory temp files for atomic concurrent puts; deterministic race regression and black-box test pass; Codex and Claude Fable approved.

title: Reschedule sync after quarantine restoration
description: A walk can restore a locally quarantined fact only after its push set was computed, then cache the peer ETag against the new local root. Later 304 responses may return early forever, so the restored fact never reaches the peer and roots remain divergent.
acceptance_criteria: Restoring any quarantined fact invalidates or reschedules every peer walk cache for that workspace; add a realistic two-peer regression that restores after push-set calculation and proves a subsequent no-new-write walk converges; retain ordinary 304 pruning when no restoration occurs.
close_reason: Quarantine restoration now invalidates every workspace peer cache so the next unchanged walk republishes restored facts; realistic two-peer pull-then-follow-up-push regression passes.

title: Bind mint evaluation to committed canonical authority
description: A caller can present an independently valid stale closure that omits a committed conflicting authority winner. Evaluate mode currently canonicalizes only inside the caller-controlled pile, so a fact pruned from the workspace canonical set can still authorize a sync token.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluate mode compares presented need providers with committed canonical providers while preserving globals-blind durable validation and first-sync for genuinely new descendants; add a regression for a quarantined losing device chain and a positive fresh-delegation case; pass the canonical workspace view atomically from the mint seam.
close_reason: Committed canonical evaluation now checks semantic need compatibility, not provider-id equality: incompatible co-offer winners reject stale quarantined chains while honest diverged peers mint both ways and can converge.

title: Hoisting in production: settle-node closure placement (ρ→1); retire flat per-leaf closure
description: docs/SIMPLIFY.md §2 and docs/MULTILEVEL_PILE.md. Land hoisting in the PRODUCTION T_fact store/sync path as an engine capability on core/tree.py: factor each indexed fact ONCE to its settle node (the LCA of its own leaf and the leaves whose facts depend on it), so every root-to-node path is a closed set and full-sync download drops to one copy of each fact — rho approaches 1 versus the flat per-leaf-closure rho around 3x measured. Replace core/layout.py's per-leaf close(). Keep fp (in-range key/diff identity) distinct from oid (node bytes plus closure/fetch identity), so closure placement stays out of diff algebra. Range sync pays a flat shared-core tax; verify against bench_hoist, bench_hoist_sync, and bench_order. Scope: this bead lands exact one-copy T_fact placement. A secondary index that omits closure facts from its key set needs stable closure-only placement, and whole-node payload piles do not guarantee cross-index body dedup; poc-16-yez.15 owns that adapter and blocks production T_supp (yez.10). core/hoist.py remains prototype/bench-only.
notes:
Scope corrected during independent review on 2026-07-25: 808.9 guarantees one-copy hoisting within production T_fact only. It deliberately does not claim that T_supp can reuse whole-node payload piles unchanged. poc-16-yez.15 tracks closure-only dependency placement and canonical shared fact-body references, and now blocks yez.10.
Final review hardened every published-root trust boundary: rebuild/stateless authority require known DURABLE facts and exact drain-derived globals; daemon mint synchronizes its root-stamped index first. tree.merge validates untrusted inputs before identity/empty/superset shortcuts, while explicitly prevalidated roots retain bounded diff/fold behavior. Regressions cover forged removal metadata and ephemeral authority roots at every shortcut.
Final shortcut audit found full-set validation alone could accept noncanonical settle spans whose partial paths were not closed. tree.validate_view now derives the canonical dependency graph, rebuilds the expected v2 view in memory, and requires identical oid at merge, Node.rebuild, and Authority.from_root. Regression builds a self-hashed wrong-placement real workspace and rejects it across empty/identity/superset merges, rebuild, daemon mint, and stateless authority with zero external emits.

title: Make removal projection independent of membership materialization order
description: A valid removal can have an older timestamp than the target's membership fact. During canonical reprojection, close() may materialize the removal before the user row; removal's UPDATE then affects zero rows and the later user materialization inserts evicted=0. The same accepted fact set can therefore expose a non-evicted member after rebuild/reprojection even though the removal global is present. Resolve this with the suppression/remove-wins model rather than relying on projector order.
acceptance_criteria: Add a regression with an old-timestamp removal preceding target membership during reprojection; prove fresh projection, rebuild, and opposite arrival orders expose the same removed state; preserve stable validation and parallel drain; implement remove-wins through the global suppression design or another explicitly approved order-independent projection rule.

title: T_supp is a synced tree: second root per ws; sync walk reconciles it
description: docs/DELETION_CLOSURE.md §3. Make T_supp a first-class SYNCED structure (second root per workspace alongside T_fact), reconciled by the ordinary sync walk (core/walk.py / RBSR). Pulling a differing T_supp leaf pulls the co-resident deletion+targets, so out-of-range facts surface during ORDINARY SYNC — not only at read-time closure. This is the 'we want sync to catch them too' requirement. Leaves reference fact bodies by hash (dedup with T_fact); only index nodes are extra (~x2).
notes:
Instantiate the ONE tree engine rather than forking the binary prototype. This is not free from 808.9: T_supp omits authority facts from its explicit key set, while its deletion payloads must remain validity-closed; differently partitioned whole-node payload piles also do not deduplicate fact bodies. poc-16-yez.15 is therefore a hard blocker and must provide stable closure-only placement plus shared fact-body hash references before this synced second root lands.

Exact-limit and one-byte-over type, key, reference, offer, suppression, authority, and posting cases exercise the real pure compiler and RepositoryApplier; over-limit piles receive one typed permanent verdict before any canonical mutation. Full/incremental modes and full-P2P/AWS/R2 wrappers agree. Tests distinguish logical map-key limits from provider object-key limits and contain no treap path.
notes: The bounded radix codec rejects non-ASCII/over-384-byte keys, null/over-4-KiB values, and nonfitting leaves before page emit. Remaining work is earlier RepositoryApplier preflight over full FactRecord, refs, roles, offers, selectors, liveness, dormant witness fields, and all postings. Exact limit/one-over vectors replace the obsolete btreap/catalog-publication reproducer.

title: Delta-shrink generated upload and notification failures
description: The current direct-upload corpus is bounded, seeded, and mostly pre-minimized, but it does not automatically shrink an expanded generated history. As more faults compose, first-failure prefixes may include irrelevant earlier cases and obscure the minimal reproducer.
design: Give each case an isolated replay seed, then delta-shrink operations and authority mutations while preserving the same oracle reason. Report the smallest retained semantic trace plus original seed and candidate profile.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberately padded capability/history failure shrinks deterministically to the causally required operations, replays the same reason, and never drops setup needed to reproduce protected-state changes.

title: Keep the provider SDK smoke directly executable
description: Importing adapters.s3.sdk_smoke through adapters.s3 eagerly imported the module before runpy executed python -m adapters.s3.sdk_smoke, producing a RuntimeWarning under -W error and invalidating the documented provider-free host smoke command.
acceptance_criteria: The package exports the smoke helpers without pre-importing sdk_smoke, the documented python -W error -m command succeeds from an assembled artifact, and focused tests cover the lazy export.
close_reason: Implemented in source commit 06940f0: adapters.s3 now exposes SDK smoke helpers lazily, so python -W error -m adapters.s3.sdk_smoke runs without runpy pre-import warnings. The exact assembled Lambda artifact passed the direct command with boto3 1.43.51/botocore 1.43.51; focused tests passed.

title: Method: prove randomized fixture preconditions before diagnosing behavior
description: Reusable method exercised during F1 final validation: when a behavior test over random keys fails, inspect and report the fixture-shape precondition separately from the behavior assertion, then repeat the exact isolated case across fresh seeds. The full suite produced disjoint held_pages/pages in test_warm_sync_fetches_no_closure_siblings, while five immediate isolated runs passed, mapping the failure to existing poc-16-npz rather than the ObjectStore changes.
acceptance_criteria: The method records the failing fixture geometry, runs at least five isolated fresh-key reproductions, distinguishes a precondition miss from a behavioral regression, and links the result to the dedicated deterministic-fixture defect without closing or masking that defect.
close_reason: Applied to the final F1 full-suite failure: captured disjoint held/pages geometry, then five isolated fresh-key reruns passed. Correctly retained npz as the open deterministic-fixture defect instead of changing behavior code.

title: Bound non-interactive Cloudflare build and test subprocesses
description: Deployment mutations now have deadlines, but non-interactive build/test paths still call Pywrangler or pytest with timeout=None. A stuck package resolver, custom-build hook, or dry-run can hang CI and release automation indefinitely. The interactive dev server is intentionally long-running and is outside this bound.
acceptance_criteria: Done when every finite non-interactive Cloudflare build, package, test, and smoke subprocess has a separately named deadline; injected TimeoutExpired cases need no sleeps, report the exact phase, and reliably terminate/kill workerd children, while dev remains interactive. Timeout cleanup is workspace-scoped and cannot remove another build, ingress/canonical data, or remote deployment. This remains deploy tooling only and cannot fork Applier/Reader semantics.
notes: Reusable probe: capture every subprocess edge in non-interactive management commands and fail when timeout is None, with an explicit allowlist only for supervised interactive processes.

title: Centralize the provider-neutral logical-key byte budget
description: Host preflight currently duplicates the longest emitted core key as pile/<16>/<64> so it can prove workspace base prefixes fit S3's 1024-byte physical-key ceiling before any mutation. core.object_store.validate_key defines characters/segments but no total byte ceiling or emitted-key shape budget. A future longer core namespace can silently make host preflight unsound again; FsStore can also defer an oversized logical key to platform path-limit errors.
acceptance_criteria: Define one provider-neutral maximum logical-key byte budget or a central emitted-key-shape contract consumed by validate_key and host prefix validation. Tests enumerate every core-produced key namespace, prove each fits, ratchet the longest shape, reject one-byte-over logical and physical keys before I/O across FsStore/S3/R2, and fail when a new producer bypasses the declared budget.
notes: Reusable drift-finder from the independent poc-16-x1p.6 review: compare every literal/formatted store key producer against preflight's assumed maximum, then add a negative control one byte beyond the provider's physical limit. Current code is safe because pile/<16>/<64> is the longest emitted key; this is a future-proofing ratchet, not an x1p.6 blocker.

title: Batch PileSender detached-object transfer without bypassing RepositoryApplier
description: PileSender currently sends each locally available Bao object through an individually bounded create-only request before the fact pile. Design bounded batching/resumable missing-object negotiation while preserving objects-first/pile-last delivery, per-object hash checks, and the rule that only RepositoryApplier may admit canonical inbound objects or advance root.
acceptance_criteria: Large multi-slice benchmarks measure requests and bytes. Explicit request/response ceilings, adaptive splitting, retries, duplicates, corrupt/collision bodies, and missing optional objects are covered. A sender never receives canonical list/delete/root authority and never delivers its pile after an available-object transfer failure; recipient-side canonical creation occurs only through RepositoryApplier and remains compatible with hosted and full-P2P actors.

title: Make non-authoritative object-store work mutations explicitly idempotent
description: Object-store work mutations outside canonical root construction need explicit idempotency and authority labels. PileSender creates exact ingress keys; RepositoryApplier conditionally establishes canonical objects and exact internal generations; provider lifecycle cleanup is separate and cannot masquerade as root-commit or F10 evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The store contract names every namespace and its authority/idempotency rule. Content-keyed staging/evidence and fresh internal generations cannot clobber different bytes; replayed creates/deletes reconcile by exact strong read; unknown outcomes retain obligations unless equality/absence is proved. Tests cover cross-member/workspace keys, ABA generations, concurrent appliers, and prevent deletion of root, canonical objects, client markers, or another actors work.

title: rebuild's foreign-envelope branch CASes from a base that Publisher.base() never validated
description:
core/node.py:456-464. When the current root will not decode, rebuild calls
Publisher.same_snapshot_envelope (publication.py:66-78), which compares the
foreign JSON against meta['root-bytes'] -- the last root THIS index stamped --
and if five fields match, calls self.commit(ws, reuse=False, _base=base).

Passing _base skips Publisher.base() (publication.py:39-52) entirely, so there
is no check that the index is currently stamped for anything at all. It can be
mid-dirty: a prior publisher.dirty(base) deletes meta['root'] (publication.py:64).
The node then compiles a root purely from local SQLite and CASes it over the
foreign one.

On a shared bucket, two co-tenants running different LAYOUT stamps
(manifest.py:25) would each keep rewriting the other's root, with _sync_index
giving up after 8 attempts (node.py:245). Because the content stays
semantically identical this is livelock and mutual clobbering rather than
corruption -- but it is a write loop with no backoff and no detection.

tests/test_shared_bucket_node.py:400 covers only the negative case: a DIFFERENT
snapshot is correctly refused, single-threaded. The positive case -- a matching
envelope, concurrently, from a possibly-dirty index -- is untested.

Related: the same function is the reason poc-16-nuk exists, since this branch is
one of the two places rebuild re-reads root to adopt a newer base.

title: Measure and bound RepositoryApplier orphan amplification
description: Every failed or stale root attempt may leave harmless unreachable immutable pages. Measure bytes written per committed logical change under N concurrent RepositoryAppliers and repeated path-copy attempts, then define a safe reachability-based collection boundary or a provable operational bound. Object-store LIST is never authority and collection must not race pinned/current roots.
acceptance_criteria: Fixed 1-6 writer schedules report unique/orphan bytes and object puts per commit, including stale, unknown, crash, retry storms, and PileSender object delivery abandoned before its pile. The operational bound includes valid-but-unreferenced direct objects. If amplification exceeds the declared bound, a collector retains current and explicitly protected historical roots, proves reachability before deletion, tolerates paginated/stale discovery hints, and never deletes an object while any protected or pinned root can name it. Full-P2P, S3, and R2 traces use the same model; no SQL catalog supplies reachability.

title: Node.rebuild re-reads root to adopt a newer base, contradicting the stated law
description:
DESIGN.md, under Store and publication: "Catalog settlement returns a
publication plan pinned to the exact root bytes and ETag that settlement read.
Object and tree compilation never rereads `root` to adopt a newer base."

core/node.py rebuild() rereads root and adopts a newer base at two points:

  node.py:462-464   foreign-envelope branch, after commit(..., _base=base)
  node.py:481-483   semantic-upgrade branch, after commit(..., reuse=False)

Both do the same three lines: raw = st.get("root"); base = (raw, h(raw));
root = manifest.decode_root(raw). Between our own CAS and that re-read another
writer can land its own CAS, so the adopted base can be a root we never wrote.

Effect appears benign rather than unsafe: the adopted root is a real committed
root, resident() then reads that root's manifest, settlement derives from it,
and publish CASes against its ETag -- so the pinning is internally consistent
and a concurrent change still loses at the CAS. What is wrong is the stated
law, which is currently false for the one code path most likely to run during
contention and recovery.

Resolve one way or the other: either re-read into a fresh pinned pair and say
so in DESIGN.md (the law becomes "compilation never MIXES bases"), or hoist the
re-read so rebuild restarts cleanly from a single pin. The second is easier to
reason about and matches how Publisher.base() already behaves.

Related evidence gathered during review: racing writers DO converge on this
path. Three nodes with independent SQLite, racing deletions (which force the
non-incremental publish branch), 4 lost CASes retried -- 5 commits, every one
agreeing with a from-scratch rebuild of its own manifest, all nodes converged,
bucket history linearizable. So this is a documentation/clarity defect, not a
known correctness break.

title: Inject failures across PileSender, RepositoryApplier, and HTTP boundaries
description: Build a provider-neutral peer/HTTP harness that can hang, truncate, return typed failures, close between pinned root and object reads, fail object delivery before pile delivery, and fail every RepositoryApplier object/CAS/F10/delete seam. A partial sender or transport attempt cannot stamp convergence, mutate a reader, or create an alternate receive path.
acceptance_criteria: Real daemon/socket plus AWS/Cloudflare local adapters cover each seam, retry, restart, stale cache, and next-turn recovery. Failed object delivery never sends the pile; a durable exact pile is retained across retryable apply failures; root advances only through RepositoryApplier after complete immutable closure; RepositoryReader routes remain side-effect-free; fixed histories replay and shrink with no SQL receiver dependency.

title: Simplify kernel contexts behind one explicit fact-context protocol
description: Replace duck-typed SQL-versus-memory branching in offer selection, ranks, closures, and edge resolution with one declared family-facing protocol. RepositoryApplier and the pure settlement engine use the database-free implementation; a SQL-backed PileSender/query adapter may implement the same protocol but cannot become receiving authority.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol and differential tests cover every registered family, offers/co-offers, refs, proof rank, closure limits, validation exceptions, and adversarial ordering. The running RepositoryApplier and settlement code call the same implementation; no hasattr dispatch, future store-only special case, alternate admission judgment, or legacy treap cleanup is folded into this bead. Net core LOC falls or the change is rejected.

title: Make declared co-offer checks match the authenticated authority index
description:
The current need_key(requires=...) address can be read by a cold recipient but is never written. Keep authority selection keyed only by the canonical base need address, then validate family-declared co-offers against the selected providers authenticated FactRecord. Remove any phantom composite-key route from compiler, reader, and tests.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Commit a canonical base-offer winner that lacks or conflicts on a family-declared co-offer, then run full-P2P and hosted apply/read paths across suppression, removal, fallback, malformed, and one-over cases.
acceptance_criteria: Every registered Need with and without requires is checked through the same base AuthorityTree selection plus exact provider FactRecord. Full-P2P and hosted RepositoryReader/Applier agree for valid, missing, conflicting, losing, suppressed, malformed, and over-budget co-offers. Static tests reject construction or lookup of an unwritten requires-encoded authority key and reject family-specific indexes.

title: A peer that echoes our action_etag silently disables the action-sync leg in both directions
description:
core/manifest.py decode_root validates action_etag only as valid_fid
(manifest.py:293) -- it is a free 64-hex field, bound to nothing. core/sync.py
then trusts it for a skip decision:

    same_actions = remote_root and local_before
        and remote_snapshot.action_etag
        == manifest.decode_root(local_before).action_etag     (sync.py:130-132)

When it matches, remote_actions is populated from our OWN local SQLite
(sync.py:134-140). That value is then used BOTH ways: pull_actions receives it
as `rows` and pulls nothing, and push_actions receives it as `remote_rows` and
computes an empty push set (sync.py:143-145, 300-318).

So a peer that simply copies our action_etag out of our root makes the entire
authenticated action leg a no-op in both directions.

Severity is bounded rather than critical: removal facts still travel as
ordinary facts through the RangeTree diff, and merge() re-archives and
re-settles them (core/node.py:383-384), so the removal is recovered. What is
lost is the evidence leg and its independent validation.

The reason to fix it anyway is that DESIGN.md states the opposite -- "Workers
never trust it, and action evidence remains authoritative only through the
authenticated trees" -- and that is true of Workers and false of sync. Either
bind action_etag to the SuppTree root it claims to summarize, or drop the
shortcut and let the oid comparison do the pruning it already does everywhere
else.

Fuzz assertion to add regardless: a peer lying about action_etag must not
change the converged state of either side.

title: F7: model N appliers over the real four-map root
description: Extend the explicit shared-bucket state model to N writers and one or more pinned readers using the real composite shape: FactOrder, FactTree, SuppTree, and AuthorityTree under one root CAS. Writers model the RepositoryApplier protocol: pin, compile, ensure immutable closure, CAS, reconcile, prove F10, exact retire. Readers never mutate.
acceptance_criteria: Bounded exploration includes at least three writers, retry-of-a-retry, stale and unknown CAS, crash at every boundary, and concurrent pinned readers. It proves no split four-map root, no reachable missing object, no ACTIVE suppression without rooted action evidence, no unsupported retirement, and convergence under fair retries. Mutation switches for non-atomic CAS, pre-object CAS, unpinned reads, and premature deletion each yield a minimal counterexample.
notes: The current explorer is 1,000 states by default and 18,456 with crashes, leaving room for a third writer and real root arity. Extend the snapshot to manifest + all three authenticated trees + action_etag and add the cross-structure law that ACTIVE suppression evidence is manifest-reachable. ABA is excluded today by monotone toy token sets. First find whether full production roots can go A->B->A under deactivate/reactivate or action winner changes. Model provider tokens as opaque and possibly reusable. Assert each CAS can be linearized against the then-current token; do not reject duplicate expected strings globally. If byte-identical A is an extensional state, show why stale computation from A remains safe. Otherwise add an explicit generation to root bytes and test it.

title: Bound file queries to one descriptor's chunks
description: A file resolve/save/bytes call currently scans every file_bao and chunk_bao fact and performs hashing/Bao verification for every resident slice while holding the Node lock. The canonical catalog is intentionally simple, but one file query should not cost O(all workspace chunks).
design: Keep facts(fid, blob) as the sole canonical body store and do not reintroduce app.db, family tables, or materialized views. Extend the generic family-declared index only as needed so a file descriptor selects its own chunk facts (for example, an indexed parent/reference key). Assemble the result in the file family. Pin the required local state under the Node lock, then decode/hash/Bao-verify outside the lock where concurrency semantics permit.
acceptance_criteria: A single file resolve/save/bytes operation decodes and verifies only that file's descriptor and chunks; unrelated workspace files are not visited. Canonical blobs remain the source of truth, there is no projection database or file-family table, concurrent root/query behavior remains safe, and a realistic multi-file test instruments decoding or Bao verification to prove unrelated chunks are untouched. The resulting code is at least as readable and does not increase total production LOC without explicit justification.
close_reason: Implemented generic explicit-reference routes, bounded file queries, coherent unlocked verification, migration crash safety, and realistic regressions.

title: Simplify the client projection boundary if it reduces total code
description: WHY: Client nodes currently keep a separate app.db plus log, cursor, replay, and reproject recovery around the workspace catalog. This is understandable but may duplicate the root-stamp recovery transaction already present in the workspace index. CF Workers must remain database-free; clients may use SQLite. WHAT: Prototype one workspace-local transactional projection boundary, measure total branches/LOC and crash semantics, and keep it only if it is materially simpler rather than a file move.
design: Candidate: place family projection tables in the workspace index transaction, use root-stamp mismatch as the sole crash recovery rule, and remove app cursor/log only if exact replay and blob-received semantics remain clear. Never introduce SQLite into WorkerView or mint.
acceptance_criteria: Either land a design with fewer total production lines and fewer recovery states while preserving projection crash/restart, blob arrival, suppression, rebuild, and multi-workspace tests, or document the measured reason the existing separate pump is simpler and discard the prototype.
close_reason: Replaced app.db, projection pump/log/cursor, and family materialization tables with one canonical fact-blob catalog plus generic type/offer indexes and query-time family assembly. Production LOC and recovery states decreased; WorkerView remains SQLite-free. Added migration, restart, corruption-reindex, blob, suppression, and crash tests.

title: Make suppression-state publication incremental without another tree
description: WHY: Ordinary authenticated-index updates still enumerate the full effective action table, even when no suppression state changed. WHAT: Feed exact changed suppression ids from Catalog settlement into Publisher/indexes and path-copy only those FactTree corroboration and SuppTree slots. Keep the composite root and one B-treap codec; do not add a second action/removal index.
acceptance_criteria: A conflict-free ordinary append performs no full SELECT over effective suppression actions; action add/clear and duplicate-winner changes still produce byte-identical roots to a full rebuild; realistic trace and equivalence tests ratchet both properties.
notes: Implemented exact changed-SID propagation through Eligibility and PublicationPlan. Conflict-free appends reuse the pinned action_etag, perform only indexed action point reads, and path-copy only new reservations; activation and winner deltas update only their FactTree/SuppTree slots. Action facts are resolved through catalog callbacks rather than actions.j. Added SQL trace/query bound, path-copy delta, randomized incremental-vs-full, clear, and evidence-only plan coverage. Validation: 254 pytest tests pass; latency benchmark 1000/5000/10000 passes; compileall and diff check clean; production Python LOC 6810 -> 6849 (+39).
close_reason: Exact incremental suppression publication and equivalence/query-count ratchets implemented and validated.

title: Thin Node with a stable family-neutral admission catalog
description: core/node.py still combines turn orchestration with local account configuration, application projection, canonical-proof quarantine, suppression projection, and family-registry interpretation. The current delete-to-quarantine-JSON/reinsert cycle duplicates fact storage and SQL mutation paths, while principal reservation rules leak concrete offer kinds into core indexing.
design: Keep Node as the serial workspace coordinator. Replace physical fact deletion/reinsertion and the quarantine offer cache with one immutable admitted-fact catalog plus a derived eligible/proof set. Have family policy declare principal and liveness suppression reservations so indexes and suppression_state iterate data rather than naming member/device offer kinds. Move application projection and local account concerns behind their existing keychain/pump boundaries only where doing so removes duplicate coordination paths; do not perform file-only extraction.
acceptance_criteria: core/node.py retains orchestration but no quarantine JSON restore/delete machinery, application schema construction, or concrete fact/offer kind tests; opposite-arrival, shadow/restore, rebuild, suppression, daemon, and property suites remain green; production Python LOC decreases overall rather than merely moving the same methods to new files.
close_reason: Landed the stable admission catalog, family-owned named authority policy, DB-free Worker judge, composite authenticated indexes, thin workspace runtime/publication boundaries, and realistic convergence/crash/deletion tests; 219 tests pass and production LOC decreases.

title: Rename suppression state and document authenticated index invariants
description: The stateful core/actions.py name is ambiguous, and core/indexes.py does not clearly explain its three security-critical authenticated views. Rename the module to suppression_state.py and document the lookup questions, CLEAR/ACTIVE semantics, duplicated action witness invariant, and incremental-versus-bulk equivalence.
design: Keep core/suppression.py as the pure clear-envelope selector/target vocabulary. Move admitted action state, liveness scopes, screening, and local reverse projection to core/suppression_state.py. Document the three tree schemas and atomic/deterministic publication invariants beside core/indexes.py.
acceptance_criteria: No core/actions.py or imports remain; behavior tests use core.suppression_state; a reader of core/indexes.py can determine what each tree maps, why FactTree and SuppTree both bind an active action, what CLEAR and ACTIVE certify, and which determinism/rebuild invariants incremental updates preserve.
close_reason: Renamed the stateful module to suppression_state.py, documented all three authenticated index roles and CLEAR/ACTIVE/atomic/determinism invariants, updated behavioral imports, and verified the full 208-test suite.

title: Eliminate the full canonical-key scan on commit
description: Authenticated trees and changed manifest ranges update incrementally, but each commit still scans every indexed fact key to derive the canonical range partition. This is the remaining corpus-sized cost in hot posting.
design: Use the published authenticated RangeTree itself as the persistent range map. For each new canonical key, perform a bounded predecessor/successor lookup, verify the selected old pile, union its members with the additions, and path-copy replacements. Content-derived cuts never disappear, so only those old leaves can split. Keep the full catalog-backed build solely for client repair, format cutover, deactivation, and authority changes.
acceptance_criteria: A one-fact hot commit does not call Node.keys or execute a corpus-wide ordered key scan; incremental and from-scratch builds produce byte-identical roots under randomized insertion orders; realistic latency tests show sublinear touched objects and no regression in sync diffing.
notes: 2026-07-29 correction: the original close reason's SQLite neighborhood was removed to preserve client/CF read isomorphism. Incremental publication now uses bounded authenticated RangeTree neighbor reads; fact_keys and fact_boundaries SQLite indexes no longer exist. Randomized updates remain byte-identical to full builds.
close_reason: Incremental publication finds affected leaves with bounded authenticated RangeTree predecessor/successor reads, verifies and extends those piles, and path-copies canonical rows. No SQLite range directory, fact_keys/fact_boundaries index, Node.keys call, or corpus scan remains; randomized roots equal full builds and sync still prunes by OID.

title: Retire temporary docs and out-of-scope design-only test models
description:
## Background
The temporary docs tree and test-only encryption models are larger than the running product and can preserve bankrupt feature mandates.

## Scope
Consolidate current behavior into README and DESIGN, delete docs including TODO, and either bind remaining design-model tests to running APIs or remove them from the product test suite.
design: Historical rationale may remain clearly marked in DESIGN. Unimplemented encryption, versioning, and infrastructure designs do not remain as executable-looking product coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Only AGENTS.md, DESIGN.md, and README.md remain as Markdown entry points; README quickstart and all local links pass; DESIGN describes the running engine and plaintext-body status; no test-only reference model is presented as proof of unimplemented runtime behavior; full realistic suite remains green.
close_reason: Temporary docs, compatibility handlers, and design-only test models are retired; current behavior is consolidated in root docs.

title: S10: Consolidate README and DESIGN, retire the ledger, and close recovery
description:
Background: the front-door documents describe deleted engines and false encryption guarantees; docs/TODO.md is intentionally temporary bankruptcy authority.

Scope: fold current operational guidance into README and the landed model/costs/history/open work into DESIGN, reduce AGENTS to routing, enforce stale-reference checks over docs, delete docs/ including this ledger, reconcile the bead export, and close poc-16-kb6.
design: History explaining why may survive when clearly marked; unimplemented feature epics do not survive as mandates.
acceptance_criteria: README quickstart works; DESIGN matches running code and states plaintext bodies honestly; only AGENTS.md, DESIGN.md and README.md remain; link/stale-reference/layout tests pass; no bankrupt bead is reopened; all S1-S9 acceptance criteria and full suite are green; final same-worktree commit closes the epic.
close_reason: README and DESIGN now describe the running current-only format and its explicit remaining limits.

title: First production deletion family + measurements
description: Every deletion=True site is a test; the only deletion family is monkeypatched (tests/util.py:37-81). Ship a real family through the author chokepoint, then measure: index size at point and kill granularity, head width, slice locality, re-encode cost per admitted removal. All growth numbers in docs/REMOVALS.md are projections until this lands.
close_reason: Executed as oyd.7 (9163d8f): facts/content/delete.py in production plus the CUT=64 measurements in docs/COSTS.md §3.1.

title: Reject stale protected heads inside rollback-resistant restore
description: Rollback-resistant restore must compare the snapshot active/staged head and schedule position with the protected live head and monotonic floor before reporting success. A pre-retirement snapshot restored after later rotation must fail within restore or return an explicit unusable reconciliation-required state; callers must never receive a nominally restored provider that only fails on a later check.
acceptance_criteria: Restore contract tests replay snapshots from every P/S/T/U lifecycle phase after later claim, retirement, promotion, finalization, and rotation. Stale heads and floors fail in the restore result before any open, seal, lease, migration, or destruction operation can run; exact current snapshots restore; weaker tiers report their scoped limitation. Crash and cloned-state cases exercise both API restore and direct rollbackable-disk replacement.
close_reason: Bead bankruptcy 2026-07-27: superseded by docs/TODO.md and replacement epic poc-16-kb6. Closed history is preserved; no requirement survives unless restated under poc-16-kb6.

title: Coalesce completed transition retries before mutable-state validation
description: An exact retry of finalization or another completed lifecycle step must return the authoritative completed result before comparing mutable live-cover state that may legitimately change afterward. Mismatched transition tokens must still fail without mutation.
acceptance_criteria: State-machine tests retry every lifecycle operation after each later phase and after ordinary successor writes, cover replacement, restart, and additional rotations. Exact completed-token retries are safe no-ops/current-state results; wrong predecessor, successor, batch, proof, or token never coalesces or mutates state. The cases are incorporated into the exhaustive retry matrix.
close_reason: Bead bankruptcy 2026-07-27: superseded by docs/TODO.md and replacement epic poc-16-kb6. Closed history is preserved; no requirement survives unless restated under poc-16-kb6.

title: Remove pre-rename shims: walk(), push(), Node.materialize, unread columns
description:
Remove the shims left by the walk/sync rename and the pump cutover:

  - core/walk.py walk(): a pure-delegation alias whose docstring says
    "Compatibility name for the shared engine diff driver"; it forwards to sync().
    Call sites: facts/auth/user.py:71,93 and tests/test_devices.py:979,985,990.
    NOTE the call sites are direct calls, not monkeypatches — :977 patches Peer,
    not walk. Only tests/test_auth_upgrade.py:145 patches the string target, and
    that test dies with child .1 anyway.
  - core/sync.py:91-93 push(): the same one-line delegation to core/walk.py's
    _push, with exactly one caller (:70). The walk/sync split left three
    symmetrical halves of one module importing each other; collapse them.
  - Node.materialize: superseded by the pump. One call site, bench/bench_sync.py:156,
    becomes pump(node, ws).
  - Unread projection columns: the duplicated src aliases, plus file_rows.pk —
    written by the projector (facts/content/file.py:58-60) and re-exported in the
    files view, but selected by nothing. Verified: files() and bytes_for() select
    neither.

Each is small; they are grouped because they share one test story and no
production behaviour changes.
acceptance_criteria: core/walk.py exposes no walk() alias, core/sync.py no push() delegation, Node has no materialize(); the two modules no longer import each other's halves. No projection column is written without a reader. bench/bench_sync.py calls pump directly. Full suite green with no behavioural diff.
close_reason: Bead bankruptcy 2026-07-27: superseded by docs/TODO.md and replacement epic poc-16-kb6. Closed history is preserved; no requirement survives unless restated under poc-16-kb6.

title: Remove facts/content/legacy_file.py and the blob-v1 encoding gate
description:
Delete facts/content/legacy_file.py (about 77 lines of "read compatibility" for the
pre-bao whole-blob file fact) and the encoding discriminator that selects it.

This module was ADDED by the attachments port (cf5a5c8, currently on branch
codex/post-landing-20260725, not yet on main) to keep old whole-blob file facts
readable alongside the new bao-rooted descriptor. Under the project's no-backwards-
compatibility rule it should not exist: the new format should simply replace the
old one.

Scope:
  - facts/content/__init__.py: drop the module from MODULES, drop its two tables
